FDA instead accepted a three-study bridging program, agreed with the sponsor in a Type B teleconference on February 4, 2015: Study PALO-15-17 (non-inferiority trial isolating the palonosetron component, IV 30-minute infusion vs. the already-approved IV 30-second bolus), NCT02557035; Study PNET-12-23 (Phase 1 relative-bioavailability/bioequivalence bridging study, IV fosnetupitant vs. oral netupitant, healthy subjects; no ClinicalTrials.gov record found — appears unregistered, a Phase 1 European single-center study); and Study NEPA-15-18 (Phase 3 safety trial, IV NEPA FDC vs. oral Akynzeo capsules, efficacy assessed only descriptively), NCT02517021
design_text: PALO-15-17 — randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, parallel-group, non-inferiority trial isolating a single component (palonosetron infusion duration) rather than the fixed-dose combination itself; NEPA-15-18 — randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial (oral NEPA capsules as comparator) powered only for safety, with efficacy as a descriptive secondary objective; PNET-12-23 — Phase 1 relative-bioavailability/bioequivalence bridging study. The overall pattern — a component-level non-inferiority trial plus a PK bioequivalence bridge plus a safety-only comparative trial, substituted for any dedicated efficacy trial of the new formulation/combination — is not currently captured by a single Design term in `Keyword_Taxonomy.md`; flagged as a candidate new term, "PK/bioequivalence-bridged formulation approval (in lieu of a dedicated efficacy trial for the new formulation)"

pivotal_trial: COLUMBUS (Study CMEK162B2301), NCT01909453
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled, two-part trial (Part 1: 1:1:1 encorafenib+binimetinib "Combo 450" vs. vemurafenib vs. encorafenib monotherapy 300 mg; Part 2: 3:1 encorafenib+binimetinib "Combo 300" vs. encorafenib monotherapy, added mid-trial via protocol amendment at FDA's request to address a contribution-of-components concern), event-driven trial, biomarker-selected/enriched population (BRAF V600E/K mutation-positive), companion diagnostic co-approval (bioMerieux THxID BRAF assay), mid-trial SAP amendment adding a second trial part after FDA raised a design objection

pivotal_trial: COLUMBUS (Study CMEK162B2301), NCT01909453
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled, event-driven trial, biomarker-selected/enriched population (BRAF V600E/V600K mutation, centrally confirmed), 2-part design in which Part 2 (Combo 300 vs. encorafenib monotherapy, 3:1 randomization) was added mid-conduct via a protocol amendment at FDA's request, after FDA stated Part 1's design (which used a higher encorafenib dose in the combination arm than the monotherapy arm) could not adequately assess binimetinib's individual contribution to the combination — an application of the combination-rule "contribution of each component" requirement to two simultaneously-developed, previously-unapproved drugs

pivotal_trial: Study AG120-C-001, NCT02074839 (single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion trial; the R/R AML expansion cohorts, Arms 1 and 4, provided the pivotal efficacy population)
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial (Phase 1 dose-escalation and multi-arm expansion, not a dedicated registration-intent Phase 3), companion diagnostic co-approval (Abbott RealTime IDH1 Assay), FDA-conducted independent expansion of the efficacy analysis population beyond the sponsor's pre-specified primary analysis set, using a later data cut and revised inclusion criteria

pivotal_trial: MAVORIC (Study 0761-010), NCT01728805
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled, event-driven trial, stratified by disease type (MF vs. SS) and stage (IB/II vs. III/IV) and (at analysis) region, crossover permitted at progression, biomarker-agnostic enrollment (irrespective of CCR4 expression status)

sponsor: AstraZeneca AB (BLA applicant, via AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP/MedImmune LLC); Study 1053 was originated by the NCI Center for Cancer Research (protocol 13-C-0106) and transitioned to MedImmune LLC as industry sponsor at Protocol Amendment 4 (12-Aug-2014)
pivotal_trial: Study 1053 / CD-ON-CAT-8015-1053, "A Pivotal Multicenter Trial of Moxetumomab Pasudotox in Relapsed/Refractory Hairy Cell Leukemia," NCT01829711
design_text: Single-arm, open-label trial — here supporting *regular* approval rather than the accelerated-approval use this taxonomy term more typically describes; mid-study sponsor transition from an NCI-originated protocol to industry sponsorship

sponsor: Verastem, Inc. (original NDA holder at approval; U.S. marketing rights and the NDA were subsequently transferred to Secura Bio, Inc., which is the applicant of record on the 2021-2024 supplements cited below)
pivotal_trial: DUO (Study IPI-145-07), NCT02004522, randomized duvelisib vs. ofatumumab in relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL. For the FL accelerated-approval indication (documented here for completeness, not the SAP-depth focus of this entry): Study IPI-145-06 (DYNAMO), NCT01882803 — single-arm, open-label Phase 2 study, ORR as primary endpoint.
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled (DUO/Study IPI-145-07, duvelisib vs. ofatumumab, stratified by del(17p) status, purine-analog refractory/early-relapse status, and Grade 4 cytopenias); event-driven trial (both PFS- and OS-event-driven); single-arm, open-label trial (DYNAMO/Study IPI-145-06, the accelerated-approval basis for the separate FL indication, later voluntarily withdrawn)

pivotal_trial: ARCHER 1050 (Pfizer/SFJ Pharmaceuticals Study A7471050), NCT01774721
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled, event-driven trial, biomarker-selected/enriched population (EGFR exon 19del/L858R), no crossover permitted (contrast with FLAURA, which permitted crossover)

pivotal_trial: EMPOWER-CSCC-1 / Study R2810-ONC-1540 ("Study 1540"), NCT02760498; supportive: Study R2810-ONC-1423 ("Study 1423," first-in-human Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion trial), NCT02383212
design_text: single-arm, open-label, multicenter, non-randomized, multicohort Phase 1/2 program (Study 1423 dose-escalation + expansion Cohorts 7 [metastatic CSCC] and 8 [locally advanced CSCC]; Study 1540 Groups 1 [metastatic CSCC, 3 mg/kg Q2W] and 2 [locally advanced CSCC, 3 mg/kg Q2W], with a not-yet-mature Group 3 [350 mg Q3W] excluded from the efficacy analysis population); pre-specified pooled efficacy analysis combining the Phase 1 expansion cohorts and the Phase 2 multicohort trial into a single primary analysis population per disease-stage group; dose-bridging of the to-be-marketed flat dose (350 mg Q3W, Group 3) to the trial dose (3 mg/kg Q2W, Groups 1–2) via population PK modeling rather than inclusion in the pooled efficacy population

pivotal_trial: EMBRACA (Study C3441009), NCT01945775
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled (physician's-choice single-agent chemotherapy: capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine), biomarker-selected population (germline BRCA1/2 mutation via BRACAnalysis CDx or another applicant-approved lab), companion diagnostic co-approval, event-driven trial, multiple SAP amendments (4 versions) prior to database lock

single-arm, open-label trial, non-randomized multi-cohort dose-finding and dose-expansion (Phase 1/2) design, biomarker-selected population (ALK-positive NSCLC, ROS1-positive cohort also enrolled but not part of this indication), continual reassessment model (CRM) for dose-finding, post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts into one primary analysis population (FDA-defined "primary efficacy population" spanning Part 1, Part 2, and the Japanese lead-in cohort, broader than any single sponsor-reported cohort)

pivotal_trial: BRIGHT AML 1003 (Study B1371003), randomized Phase 2 "P2Unfit" sub-study, NCT01546038
design_text: randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled (low-dose cytarabine [LDAC] alone comparator), event-driven trial (target 92 OS events), stratified by cytogenetic risk (poor vs. good/intermediate), randomized sub-study nested within a larger multi-cohort Phase 1b/2 trial that also included non-randomized intensive-chemotherapy and decitabine cohorts

pivotal_trial: pooled analysis across three single-arm trials — LOXO-TRK-14001 (adult Phase 1), NCT02122913; SCOUT (LOXO-TRK-15003, pediatric Phase 1/2), NCT02637687; NAVIGATE (LOXO-TRK-15002, adult/adolescent Phase 2 basket), NCT02576431
design_text: tumor-agnostic basket trial, pooled/integrated analysis across three independently conducted single-arm trials of different phase and population (adult Phase 1, pediatric Phase 1/2, adult/adolescent Phase 2 basket), formally agreed sponsor-FDA Statistical Analysis Plan for an Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE) defining a fixed-size "Primary Analysis Set" (first 55 evaluable NTRK-fusion patients across all three trials) rather than a single trial's enrollment, biomarker-defined population (NTRK1/2/3 gene fusion, tumor histology-agnostic), rare-disease/ultra-rare-biomarker population (estimated US incidence 1,500-5,000 cases/year across all tumor types)

pivotal_trial: ADMIRAL (Study 2215-CL-0301), NCT02421939
design_text: randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled (salvage chemotherapy: LDAC, azacitidine, MEC, or FLAG-IDA per investigator preselection), event-driven trial, stratified by response to first-line AML therapy and preselected salvage chemotherapy, companion diagnostic co-approval (LeukoStrat CDx FLT3 Mutation Assay), interim single-arm response-rate analysis nested within an ongoing randomized trial while the sponsor remained blinded to the randomized comparison

sponsor: Servier Pharmaceuticals LLC (BLA developed by Baxalta, Inc./Shire; Shire's oncology portfolio, including calaspargase pegol, was acquired by Servier in October 2018, shortly before approval)
pivotal_trial: DFCI Protocol 11-001 (also referred to in FDA review as DFCI 11-011), NCT01574274; supportive: COG AALL07P4
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled (pegaspargase comparator), stratified by disease type/age/initial risk group, historical-control comparison against a prior institutional protocol (DFCI 05-001) for safety/MRD monitoring, dose-comparison arm within the supportive trial (AALL07P4 tested calaspargase pegol 2100 IU/m2 vs. 2500 IU/m2 vs. pegaspargase 2500 IU/m2)

single-arm, open-label trial, multi-stage (4-stage) design with a data-driven carve-out of a later-enrolled cohort (Stage 3) formally designated as the pivotal cohort by FDA agreement mid-trial, rare-disease population (no biomarker enrichment — BPDCN itself is the defining diagnosis), dose-focused analysis restricting the efficacy population to patients treated at the intended 12 µg/kg/day dose

single-arm, open-label trial (final/pivotal Regimen 3 cohort), preceded by an internal randomized dose-comparison stage (Regimen 1 vs. Regimen 2) resolved via a Data Review Committee interim analysis before a third, pharmacodynamically-guided dose regimen was selected for further single-arm enrollment — an adaptive seamless dose-selection-into-expansion design, biomarker-selected population (susceptible FGFR3/FGFR2 genetic alterations by clinical trial assay), companion diagnostic co-approval (therascreen FGFR RGQ RT-PCR Kit, PMA P180043 reviewed concurrently by CDRH)

pivotal_trial: SOLAR-1 (Study CBYL719C2301/BYL719C2301), NCT02437318
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, international multicenter Phase III trial, biomarker-selected primary cohort (PIK3CA-mutant tumor tissue, confirmed by a Novartis-designated central laboratory) with a parallel PIK3CA non-mutant cohort analyzed as an independent proof-of-concept objective, stratified by presence of lung/liver metastases and prior CDK4/6-inhibitor use

pivotal_trial: Study GO29365 (randomized Phase Ib/II cohort, Arms C/D), NCT02257567
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled, small-sample Phase Ib/II trial used as the pivotal registration study (not a dedicated Phase 3), multi-histology/multi-regimen master protocol (also enrolling R/R follicular lymphoma and obinutuzumab-containing arms not part of this indication), stratified permuted-block randomization, single-arm supportive cohort (Arm G, lyophilized formulation) analyzed separately without a concurrent comparator

pivotal_trial: STORM Part 2 (Study KCP-330-012), NCT02336815
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510, dose/schedule carried forward from a non-randomized Phase 1 trial (KCP-330-001) with no dedicated dose-ranging study at the to-be-marketed dose/schedule, indication narrowed mid-review from a broader triple-class-refractory population to a narrower quad-refractory subpopulation via a post-ODAC major amendment

pivotal_trial: ARAMIS (Study 17712, protocol BAY 1841788/17712), NCT02200614
design_text: randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial, group-sequential design (interim OS analysis coincident with the final primary MFS analysis), Special Protocol Assessment (SPA)-agreed design that was formally amended twice before database lock to revise the target hazard ratio and event target in light of external trials' published results

pivotal_trial: ENLIVEN (Study PLX108-10), NCT02371369
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-part study (Part 1 randomized/controlled, Part 2 open-label extension with placebo crossover), randomization stratified by US vs. non-US sites and by upper vs. lower extremity tumor location, REMS-restricted distribution due to hepatotoxicity risk

sponsor: Genentech, Inc. (a member of the Roche Group; entrectinib was originally developed by Ignyta, Inc., acquired by Roche/Genentech in 2018, and traces to an earlier compound code NMS-1191372/RXDX-101)
pivotal_trial: Pooled cross-trial analysis of three independently conducted, single-arm, open-label trials — ALKA-372-001 ("ALKA", Study GO40783, EudraCT 2012-000148-88, not registered on ClinicalTrials.gov), STARTRK-1 (NCT02097810), and STARTRK-2 (NCT02568267, "Basket Study of Entrectinib... for Solid Tumors Harboring NTRK 1/2/3, ROS1, or ALK Gene Rearrangements")
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial, first-in-human dose-escalation design with 3+3 scheme (ALKA-372-001), Phase 1 multicenter dose-expansion (STARTRK-1), basket trial — histology-agnostic enrollment by shared molecular alteration (STARTRK-2, an explicitly named "Global Phase 2 Basket Study"), cross-trial pooled integrated analysis across independently conducted single-arm trials — distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts into one primary analysis population" (PALOMA-1), which pools cohorts *within* one trial rather than pooling patients across three separately sponsored/protocoled trials run years apart

sponsor: University of Iowa Health Care (UIHC PET Imaging Center)
pivotal_trial: RET-NET-01, a retrospective pooled analysis of three prospective single-center studies conducted at the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics — Study 1 (NCT01619865), Study 2 (NCT01869725), and Study 3 (NCT02441062)
design_text: diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison against a composite reference standard), retrospective pooled/cross-trial analysis of three independently conducted prospective single-center studies, academic (non-industry) 505(b)(2) NDA sponsor

single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H, pooled/supportive analysis across two independently conducted single-arm studies (206 as primary, AU-003 as supportive)

sponsor: Astellas Pharma US, Inc. (co-developed with Seattle Genetics, Inc.)
pivotal_trial: EV-201 (Study SGN22E-001) Cohort 1, NCT03219333
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510, confirmed ORR primary endpoint agreed with FDA prospectively at a pre-protocol End-of-Phase-1 Type B meeting, two-cohort structure (Cohort 1 platinum-treated, Cohort 2 platinum-naive/cisplatin-ineligible, only Cohort 1 supporting the initial approval), exposure-response analysis pooled across two trials (EV-101 Part C and EV-201 Cohort 1) used as supportive evidence

pivotal_trial: DESTINY-Breast01 (Study DS8201-A-U201), NCT03248492
design_text: single-arm, open-label, multi-part trial (Part 1 dose-finding, Part 2a/2b dose-expansion at the recommended Phase 2 dose) supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510, independent adjudication committee established specifically for a drug-class safety signal (interstitial lung disease) rather than for the efficacy endpoint

pivotal_trial: NAVIGATOR (Study BLU-285-1101), NCT02508532
design_text: single-arm, open-label, multi-part, multi-cohort (Part 1 dose-escalation, Part 2 dose-expansion with molecularly-defined groups) trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510, biomarker-selected/enriched population (PDGFRA exon 18-mutant GIST, predominantly D842V), sample-size logic based on three separately powered Part 2 expansion groups defined by mutation status and prior therapy line

pivotal_trial: Study EZH-202, Cohort 5 (epithelioid sarcoma), NCT02601950
design_text: single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort basket trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.500, Green-Dahlberg two-stage design (a named variant of Simon's two-stage design) used for Cohort 5, with an unplanned mid-trial primary-endpoint reversal

pivotal_trial: ICARIA-MM (Study EFC14335), NCT02990338
design_text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial (1:1, isatuximab + pomalidomide + dexamethasone [IPd] vs. pomalidomide + dexamethasone [Pd]), event-driven trial (enrollment capped at ~300 patients or upon reaching the PFS analysis event target, whichever came first), randomization stratified by age (<75 vs. ≥75 years) and number of prior lines of therapy (2-3 vs. >3) via interactive response technology

sponsor: AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP (NDA applicant); the pivotal trial itself (SPRINT) was designed, sponsored, and conducted by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Pediatric Oncology Branch (POB) under the NCI Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP) — AstraZeneca was not the trial sponsor and submitted the NDA based on NCI's trial data, per FDA's Multi-Discipline Review
pivotal_trial: SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1 (Study 11-C-0161 / CTEP #8799), NCT01362803
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial — an NCI-designed and NCI-run academic Phase II study (not an industry-designed registration trial) later used by AstraZeneca as the sole pivotal basis for its NDA; external natural-history/historical-control comparison used descriptively only, not for formal statistical testing

pivotal_trial: FIGHT-202 (Study INCB 54828-202), NCT02924376
design_text: single-arm, open-label, non-randomized, multicenter, multi-cohort Phase 2 trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510; biomarker-selected/enriched population (Cohort A restricted to central-genomics-laboratory-confirmed FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement, the only cohort supporting the approved indication; Cohorts B [other FGF/FGFR alterations] and C [FGF/FGFR-negative, US only] were exploratory and not part of the approved claim); concurrent companion-diagnostic co-approval (FoundationOne CDx, via supplemental PMA) restricting the indication to FDA-approved-test-confirmed patients

sponsor: Seattle Genetics, Inc. (rebranded Seagen Inc. in 2020; acquired by Pfizer in December 2023)
pivotal_trial: HER2CLIMB (Study ONT-380-206), NCT02614794 — confirmed via ClinicalTrials.gov and the FDA review to be a randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled **Phase 2** trial (official CT.gov title: "Phase 2 Randomized, Double-Blinded, Controlled Study of Tucatinib vs Placebo in Combination With Capecitabine and Trastuzumab in Patients With Pretreated Unresectable Locally Advanced or Metastatic HER2+ Breast Carcinoma"), not a dedicated Phase 3 trial, despite supporting regular (not accelerated) approval.
design_text: randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled (add-on design: both arms received the same trastuzumab + capecitabine background therapy, with the control arm substituting placebo for tucatinib), biomarker-selected/enriched population (centrally confirmed HER2-positive by IHC/ISH), dynamic hierarchical (biased-coin/minimization-type) randomization scheme balancing on 3 stratification factors with re-randomization-based inference, primary-endpoint analysis timed to a fixed subset of the first 480 randomized patients rather than to a target event count or calendar date

pivotal_trial: Study IMMU-132-01 (Phase I/II, open-label, multi-cohort basket trial; mTNBC expansion cohort), NCT01631552
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval, conducted as one disease-specific expansion cohort (mTNBC, n=108, treated at the to-be-marketed 10 mg/kg dose with ≥2 prior therapies for metastatic disease) within a larger Phase I/II basket protocol that separately enrolled and analyzed non-TNBC breast, urothelial, NSCLC, SCLC, and other epithelial-cancer cohorts (efficacy not pooled across histologies), no formal sample size calculation or statistical hypothesis pre-specified for the trial

pivotal_trial: GEOMETRY mono-1 (Study CINC280A2201/A2201), NCT02414139
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500, multi-cohort trial with cohorts stratified by molecular-alteration subtype (MET exon 14 skipping mutation vs. MET amplification by gene copy number [GCN]) and line of therapy — of the trial's 7 cohorts, only the two MET exon-14-skipping-mutation cohorts (Cohort 4, previously treated, N=69; Cohort 5b, treatment-naïve, N=28) supported this NDA's approved indication, while the MET-amplification cohorts (1a, 1b, 2, 3, 5a, 6) did not, companion diagnostic co-approval (FoundationOne CDx)

sponsor: Loxo Oncology, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Eli Lilly and Company
pivotal_trial: LIBRETTO-001 (Study LOXO-RET-17001), a single multicenter, single-arm, open-label, first-in-human Phase 1/2 dose-escalation and dose-expansion trial, NCT03157128 — the sole trial supporting all three indications, with tumor-type- and treatment-history-defined analysis populations (not separate registration trials) carved out of one continuously enrolling study
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial (first-in-human dose-escalation and dose-expansion design) supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500/314.510; multi-cohort trial with independently analyzed, tumor-type- and treatment-history-defined primary analysis sets carved from one continuously enrolling study

pivotal_trial: INVICTUS (Study DCC-2618-03-001), NCT03353753
design_text: randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial (primary analysis triggered by accrual of a target number of PFS events), crossover permitted at progression (placebo patients unblinded and offered ripretinib after BICR-confirmed progression; 66% of placebo patients switched)

sponsor: Zionexa-US Corporation (NDA holder of record at approval; the compound and its predecessor French-market product, Estrotep, were developed academically over three decades at institutions including the University of Washington before Zionexa's 505(b)(2) submission; per the 2024-revised label, Cerianna is now "Distributed by GE Healthcare Inc., Marlborough, MA," reflecting GE Healthcare's subsequent acquisition of the product)
pivotal_trial: No sponsor-conducted pivotal trial exists. Zionexa's 505(b)(2) submission relied on published reports of three independently designed, independently sponsored academic studies, none run by the Applicant: Study 1, Chae et al. 2019 (Asan Medical Center, South Korea), NCT01986569; Study 2, Peterson et al. 2014 (University of Washington/Fred Hutchinson, sponsored by the U.S. National Cancer Institute), NCT00602043; and Study 3, Venema et al. 2017 (University Medical Center Groningen, Netherlands), NCT01988324. A fourth study, Estrotepredic (NCT01627704, Assistance Publique-Hôpitaux de Paris), an exploratory trial of FES to predict hormone-therapy response, was also submitted but was not relied upon for the approved detection indication.
design_text: retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis (academic or literature-derived, not a company-sponsored pivotal trial); diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient comparison of FES PET against a histopathology/IHC reference standard, rather than an active-comparator drug); 505(b)(2) NDA relying on three independently conducted, non-pooled academic studies rather than a single integrated dataset (contrast with the cross-study pooling protocol used for Ga 68 DOTATOC/NDA 210828)

sponsor: NDA held by Pharma Mar USA, Inc. (the FDA approval letter is addressed to Pharma Mar USA, Inc.); the molecule was discovered and is globally developed by PharmaMar, S.A. (Madrid, Spain). Jazz Pharmaceuticals holds an exclusive license/collaboration agreement for commercialization of lurbinectedin in the United States and jointly announced the 2020 approval with PharmaMar — the precise date and full terms of the Jazz–PharmaMar agreement were not independently verifiable in this session (web search was unavailable; PharmaMar/Jazz press-release URLs attempted via direct fetch returned 403/404), so this should be treated as a plainly-stated but not primary-source-confirmed detail.
pivotal_trial: PM1183-B-005-14 ("Study B-005"), the SCLC cohort of a multicenter, open-label, single-arm, multi-cohort Phase 2 basket trial ("A Multicenter Phase II Clinical Trial of Lurbinectedin (PM01183) in Selected Advanced Solid Tumors"), NCT02454972 — confirmed via the ClinicalTrials.gov registry record (sponsor PharmaMar, official title as above) and independently confirmed as the sole pivotal evidentiary trial in FDA's Multi-Discipline Review
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.510; FDA's own review explicitly labels Study B-005 "a single-arm, multi-cohort, basket trial" (nine tumor-type-specific cohorts — SCLC, head and neck carcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors, biliary tract, endometrial, BRCA1/2 breast, carcinoma of unknown primary, germ cell tumors, Ewing's-family tumors — each analyzed independently by tumor type rather than pooled across histologies, unlike a tissue-agnostic basket trial)

sponsor: Astex Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (the NDA applicant of record; both Astex and its US commercial affiliate Taiho Oncology, Inc., which is the label's medical-inquiries/adverse-event contact, are subsidiaries of Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.)
pivotal_trial: ASTX727-02 ("ASCERTAIN"), NCT03306264, supported by the earlier phase 1/2 study ASTX727-01 (dose-confirmation/FDC stages, referred to as ASTX727-01-B in the FDA review) — **this was not a randomized efficacy trial; it was a PK/exposure-equivalence (bioequivalence-style) bridging study** comparing oral decitabine-cedazuridine to IV decitabine, leveraging IV decitabine's pre-existing 2006 efficacy approval
design_text: two-period, two-sequence, randomized (1:1), open-label crossover trial with no stratification factors, used to bridge effectiveness from a previously approved reference product via demonstrated pharmacokinetic exposure-equivalence rather than a new randomized efficacy comparison; after the two crossover cycles, all subjects rolled over to open-label oral therapy only (single-arm from Cycle 3 onward)

sponsor: MorphoSys US Inc. (in collaboration with Incyte Corporation)
pivotal_trial: L-MIND (Study MOR208C203), NCT02399085
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601.41 (BLA accelerated approval regulations), no randomized comparator; supportive single-arm monotherapy trial for contribution-of-tafasitamab evidence (MOR208C201); propensity-score-matched retrospective real-world comparator cohort used only for supportive, non-primary context, explicitly not accepted by FDA as demonstrating statistical significance

application: BLA 761158 (original 2020 accelerated approval, revoked 2023); BLA 761440 (2025 re-approval, new application)
sponsor: GlaxoSmithKline Intellectual Property Development Ltd. England (original 2020 BLA 761158 holder); GlaxoSmithKline LLC (2025 BLA 761440 holder)
pivotal_trial: DREAMM-2 (Study 205678), NCT03525678 — basis of the original 2020 accelerated approval (BLA 761158); DREAMM-3 (Study 207495), NCT04162210 — the required confirmatory trial, failed; DREAMM-7 (Study 207503), NCT04246047 — basis of the October 2025 re-approval under new BLA 761440 (with bortezomib + dexamethasone); DREAMM-8 (NCT04484623) — a related trial (with pomalidomide + dexamethasone) reviewed at the same 2025 advisory committee meeting but not approved
design_text: DREAMM-2 — two-arm, randomized (1:1), open-label Phase II trial in which each dose arm (2.5 mg/kg vs. 3.4 mg/kg) was analyzed independently against a fixed ORR performance goal rather than compared to the other arm — a randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design (cf. brigatinib/ALTA); group-sequential design with a single non-binding futility interim analysis plus an additional Bayesian cross-arm comparative-futility rule; protocol amended mid-conduct to shift the primary analysis population from a planned first-130-patient subset to all ~200 randomized patients after substantial over-enrollment. DREAMM-3 (confirmatory) — randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled Phase III trial of belantamab monotherapy vs. pomalidomide plus low-dose dexamethasone. DREAMM-7 (basis of 2025 re-approval) — randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, event-driven Phase III trial of belantamab mafodotin + bortezomib + dexamethasone (BVd) vs. daratumumab + bortezomib + dexamethasone (DVd)

sponsor: RadioMedix, Inc. (developer and clinical-trial sponsor of record on the NDA and on ClinicalTrials.gov); Curium US LLC is listed as the applicant/marketer on Drugs@FDA and manufactures/distributes the approved product
pivotal_trial: Study RMX-18-22 ("NETMedix"), NCT03673943, plus a sponsor re-analysis of previously published data (the "NETMedix Denmark Study," re-analyzing patients from Pfeifer et al. 2015) and two additional published studies (Pfeifer et al. 2012; Johnbeck et al. 2017) reviewed as supportive-only evidence
design_text: diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — Study RMX-18-22 was a prospective, single-center (Excel Diagnostics and Nuclear Oncology Center, Houston), single-dose, single-arm, non-comparative Phase 3 trial conducted under a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement (request 4/6/2018, agreement letter 5/17/2018); retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis (academic or literature-derived, not a company-sponsored pivotal trial) for the two supportive studies (Pfeifer et al. 2015/NETMedix Denmark re-analysis, Johnbeck et al. 2017); 505(b)(2) NDA for a designated new molecular entity, the first NDA submitted for an imaging drug labeled with a copper radionuclide

sponsor: Blueprint Medicines Corporation (sponsor of record at approval). Global rights subsequently moved more than once: by the time of the November 2021 EU approval and the August 2023 accelerated-to-regular-approval conversion, correspondence to FDA was submitted by Genentech, Inc./F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd (the posted ClinicalTrials.gov protocol and SAP versions from this period are headed "Pralsetinib—{Genentech, Inc./F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd}"); by September 2023 (NDA supplement removing a related thyroid-cancer indication) and September 2024 (a further supplement), correspondence reverted to Blueprint Medicines Corporation; by March 2025 (NDA supplement adding a boxed warning), the sNDA sponsor of record was Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc., which remains the manufacturer named on the current (December 2025) label
pivotal_trial: ARROW (Study BLU-667-1101/BO42863), NCT03037385
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H; a disease-and-treatment-history-defined efficacy cohort (RET fusion-positive NSCLC, split into platinum-pretreated and treatment-naïve subgroups) analyzed within one arm of a much larger multi-cohort, multi-tumor-type Phase 1/2 basket trial (ARROW also enrolled RET-altered medullary thyroid cancer, RET-fusion thyroid cancer, and other RET-altered solid tumors, each as a separately powered/analyzed cohort) — not a tumor-agnostic pooled analysis, since each disease cohort was analyzed and reported separately; Phase 1 dose-escalation (BOIN design) feeding into a Phase 2 dose-expansion at the RP2D (400 mg QD)

pivotal_trial: two independently conducted single-arm trials pooled to support approval — Study 12-230 (Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center protocol), NCT01757626, and Study 201, NCT03363373
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial (x2, cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis of independently conducted, separately protocoled trials — Study 12-230 is a single-institution MSK trial, Study 201 is a separate multicenter trial), pediatric rare-disease context (rare pediatric disease priority review voucher granted per FDCA §529)

sponsor: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA Biomedical Cyclotron), NDA 212642; and University of California, San Francisco (UCSF Radiopharmaceutical Facility), NDA 212643 — two academic (non-industry) sponsors, each holding a separate, simultaneously-approved New Drug Application for the same unbranded radiopharmaceutical
pivotal_trial: PSMA-PreRP (initial-staging population), run in parallel at UCLA (NCT03368547) and UCSF (NCT02919111); and PSMA-BCR (biochemical-recurrence population), run in parallel at UCLA (NCT02940262) and UCSF (NCT02918357) — each a prospective, single-arm, open-label, two-center (UCLA + UCSF) diagnostic-accuracy trial, with supportive literature meta-analyses (PSMA-PreRP-Meta, PSMA-BCR-Meta) submitted but treated as high-risk-of-bias secondary evidence, not primary evidence
design_text: diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — patients underwent both 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET and a reference standard (surgical histopathology in PSMA-PreRP; a composite clinical reference standard in PSMA-BCR), prospective single-arm open-label two-center trial run jointly across two academic sponsors under a rare "dual-NDA" filing structure, unplanned interim analysis conducted by the Applicants without any statistical adjustment

pivotal_trial: Study CP-MGAH22-04 ("SOPHIA"), NCT02492711
design_text: randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial, stratified permuted randomization, non-randomized infusion-duration sub-study nested within the same protocol (Stages A1/A2/B, evaluating a reduced 30-minute infusion), event-driven trial

sponsor: Myovant Sciences GmbH (parent: Myovant Sciences, Inc.) at approval; Myovant was acquired by Sumitomo Pharma in 2023, and the U.S. business now operates as Sumitomo Pharma America, Inc.
pivotal_trial: HERO (Study MVT-601-3201), NCT03085095
design_text: randomized (2:1), open-label, parallel-group, active-controlled (leuprolide acetate depot) phase 3 trial; dual primary-endpoint definition (protocol vs. regulatory) — Evaluation Criterion 1 (a single-arm ≥90% lower-CI-bound threshold in the relugolix group only) was the FDA-designated primary success criterion, while Evaluation Criterion 2 (non-inferiority of relugolix vs. leuprolide) was designated primary for EMA/PMDA; no formal interim efficacy analysis was performed; an external independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board reviewed only periodic safety data, under a separate safety SAP

sponsor: EMD Serono, Inc. (Billerica, MA) — the US commercial name for the healthcare business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, in the United States and Canada; not affiliated with Merck & Co., Inc. (Kenilworth, NJ/Rahway, NJ), an entirely separate company that has held the "Merck" name in the US/Canada since the two firms split in 1917. Tepotinib was discovered and is manufactured by Merck KGaA (the VISION trial's clinical-trial-registry sponsor is listed as Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany).
pivotal_trial: VISION (Study MS200095-0022), NCT02864992
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial; multi-cohort Phase II design in which Cohort A (METex14 skipping, first enrolled) and Cohort C (METex14 skipping, opened later via Protocol Amendment 6 as an explicitly-labeled "confirmatory part" enrolling under identical eligibility criteria and procedures) together supplied the confirmatory evidence for the same molecularly-defined indication, while a third, ineligible-for-this-indication cohort (Cohort B, MET amplification/METex14-negative) was enrolled in parallel under the same protocol; biomarker-selected/enriched population (METex14 skipping alterations confirmed centrally by tissue [TBx] and/or plasma circulating-tumor-DNA liquid biopsy [LBx] assay); interim futility analysis with a pre-specified minimum-responder stopping rule (enrollment of TBx-only-positive patients into Cohort A would have stopped had ≤3 of the first 12 TBx-analysis-set subjects responded; analogous ≤2-of-12 rule for Cohort B)

pivotal_trial: UNITY-NHL (Study UTX-TGR-205), NCT02793583 — MZL and FL cohorts (single-arm, Simon's two-stage design per cohort), within a larger multi-cohort Phase 2b trial that separately also contained a randomized combination-therapy comparison unrelated to these two accelerated-approval cohorts
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial (Simon's two-stage design per cohort, embedded within a larger multi-cohort trial whose overall registration record on ClinicalTrials.gov is titled as a Phase 2b randomized study, though the MZL/FL accelerated-approval cohorts themselves were single-arm), biomarker/histology-selected cohorts (MZL cohort required ≥1 prior anti-CD20 regimen; FL cohort required ≥3 prior lines, a threshold FDA raised from the sponsor's proposed ≥2)

pivotal_trial: G1T28-05, NCT03041311 (confirmatory/primary evidentiary trial), with two additional randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled supportive trials, G1T28-02 (NCT02499770) and G1T28-03 (NCT02514447)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (three: G1T28-05 the pivotal trial, G1T28-02 and G1T28-03 explicitly supportive/exploratory only per FDA — "due to the limitations of the study design for Study G1T28-02-Part 2 and Study G1T28-03-Part 2, these 2 studies will be considered as supportive. No inference should be made by analysis results from these 2 studies"); mid-trial SAP amendment changing endpoint status — G1T28-05 was originally powered for overall survival, then amended prior to unblinding to two co-primary myelosuppression endpoints once early OS data from G1T28-02 showed no signal; co-primary endpoints (duration of severe Grade 4 neutropenia in Cycle 1, and occurrence of severe Grade 4 neutropenia)

pivotal_trial: HORIZON (Study OP-106), NCT02963493 (single-arm accelerated-approval basis); confirmatory trial OCEAN (Study OP-103), NCT03151811 (randomized, active-controlled vs. pomalidomide/dexamethasone)
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial (HORIZON) supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500, with the accelerated-approval indication restricted to a triple-class-refractory subpopulation (97 of 157 enrolled patients) rather than the full enrolled cohort; randomized, open-label (assessor-blinded), active-controlled confirmatory trial (OCEAN) using a non-inferiority-margin framework repurposed as a superiority test (superiority declared only if the hazard ratio's 95% CI upper bound fell below 1.0)

pivotal_trial: TIVO-3, NCT02627963 (randomized, open-label, active-controlled vs. sorafenib)
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial (comparator sorafenib, itself an approved active RCC therapy), stratified by IMDC risk category (favorable/intermediate/poor) and prior-therapy category (two prior VEGFR TKIs vs. checkpoint inhibitor+VEGFR TKI vs. VEGFR TKI+other systemic agent); non-proportional-hazards concern flagged by FDA on the primary PFS analysis (Schoenfeld residual test p=0.01)

sponsor: GlaxoSmithKline (originally developed by Tesaro, Inc., acquired by GSK)
pivotal_trial: GARNET, NCT02715284 (dMMR endometrial cancer Cohort A1, within a larger multicohort Phase 1 trial)
design_text: single-arm, open-label, multicohort, non-randomized, sequential dose-escalation/cohort-expansion Phase 1 trial, with the dMMR endometrial cancer cohort (A1) serving as the accelerated-approval evidentiary basis and other cohorts (A2/MMR-proficient EC, E/NSCLC, F/other dMMR tumors) run in parallel; biomarker-selected population (dMMR/MSI-H status by central IHC, VENTANA MMR RxDx Panel)

pivotal_trial: LOTIS-2 (Study ADCT-402-201), NCT03589469
design_text: single-arm, open-label, single-group Phase 2 trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E; Simon's two-stage design (futility interim analysis on the first 52 patients, requiring ≥10 responders to continue to full enrollment)

pivotal_trial: CHRYSALIS, NCT02609776 (Cohort D of a Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion trial)
design_text: single-arm, open-label, multi-part Phase 1 trial (dose escalation plus multiple dose-expansion cohorts) supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E; biomarker-selected population (EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation, post-platinum); non-binding futility interim analysis built into the cohort-expansion design

pivotal_trial: OSPREY, NCT02981368 (Cohort A, pre-prostatectomy/pelvic-nodal-staging setting) and CONDOR, NCT03739684 (biochemical-recurrence setting) — two independent diagnostic-accuracy trials
design_text: diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — OSPREY Cohort A compared PET findings against surgical histopathology in the same patients undergoing planned radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection; CONDOR compared PET localization findings against a composite reference/truth standard (histopathology, or informative conventional imaging, or confirmed PSA response) in patients with biochemically recurrent disease; both trials used multiple independent, blinded central readers rather than a single reader

pivotal_trial: CodeBreaK 100 (Study 20170543), NCT03600883; confirmatory trial CodeBreaK 200, NCT04303780 (randomized vs. docetaxel)
design_text: single-arm, open-label, multicohort trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 (dose-expansion phase of a Phase 1/2 trial); confirmatory trial (CodeBreaK 200) is a randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial with crossover permitted from docetaxel to sotorasib at confirmed progression

sponsor: BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (QED Therapeutics); later commercialized in the US by Helsinn Healthcare SA
pivotal_trial: Study CBGJ398X2204 (Study 2204), NCT02150967, Cohort 1; intended confirmatory trial PROOF-301 (also referred to as "PROOF 301"), NCT03773302
design_text: single-arm, open-label, multicohort trial supporting accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 (Cohort 1, FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement); intended confirmatory trial (PROOF-301) was a randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled (gemcitabine+cisplatin) first-line Phase 3 trial that was terminated early for a reason unrelated to safety or efficacy (see Regulatory below)

sponsor: Jazz Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (drug developed as JZP-458 / recombinant crisantaspase produced in *Pseudomonas fluorescens*)
pivotal_trial: Study JZP458-201 (also reported as the pediatric-oncology-cooperative-group study AALL1931), NCT04145531
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial; sequential-cohort, multi-part dose-confirmation design with a Study Data Review Committee (SDRC) reviewing accruing NSAA data at pre-specified patient counts and issuing stop/continue/expand decisions per cohort

sponsor: Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC (drug developed by Peloton Therapeutics, a subsidiary of Merck; internal code MK-6482/PT2977)
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial; biomarker/genetically-defined rare-disease population (germline VHL alteration) with multiple VHL-associated tumor types (RCC, CNS hemangioblastoma, pNET) each analyzed as a separate efficacy cohort within one single-arm trial rather than pooled across unrelated histologies

sponsor: Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc. (drug developed as TAK-788 / AP32788)
pivotal_trial: Study 101 / AP32788-15-101, Part 3 extension cohort ("EXCLAIM"), NCT02716116; confirmatory trial EXCLAIM-2, NCT04129502
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial (accelerated-approval basis, Part 3 of a Phase 1/2 dose-escalation/expansion/extension study); confirmatory trial was randomized, open-label, active-controlled (mobocertinib vs. platinum-based chemotherapy, 1:1)

pivotal_trial: innovaTV 204 / GOG-3023 / ENGOT-cx6, NCT03438396
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial

pivotal_trial: ASCEMBL (Study CABL001A2301), NCT03106779 (indication 1); single-arm Phase 1 dose-expansion cohort of Study CABL001X2101, NCT02081378 (indication 2, T315I, per label — not independently verified against a posted SAP for this entry)
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial (indication 1); single-arm, open-label trial (indication 2, T315I)

pivotal_trial: Study OTL-2016-OTL38-006 ("Study 006"), NCT03180307
design_text: within-patient paired-comparison diagnostic-imaging study — every enrolled patient underwent both standard visualization (normal light/palpation) and fluorescence-guided imaging with the same investigational agent, with detection compared per-lesion within-patient rather than between randomized treatment arms (randomization in this trial governed the imaging system/workflow used, not drug vs. no-drug) — reuses and extends the existing "Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison)" concept to an intraoperative fluorescence-imaging agent

randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 2 trial (2:1 randomization vs. investigator's choice); dual-analysis-population design with independent alpha allocation to an Intent-to-Treat (ITT) set and a "Randomized-and-Started" (RAS) set to address immortal-time bias in the experimental arm

sponsor: CTI BioPharma Corp. (subsequently acquired by Sobi)
pivotal_trial: PERSIST-2, NCT02055781
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial (pacritinib vs. best available therapy, including ruxolitinib); post-clinical-hold, safety-restricted approval narrowing the indication to a severe-thrombocytopenia subgroup

pivotal_trial: RELATIVITY-047 (Study CA224-047), NCT03470922
design_text: randomized, double-blind, active-controlled Phase 2/3 trial; adaptive seamless Phase 2-to-3 design with a blinded, DMC-reviewed interim go/no-go decision on whether to continue enrollment into Phase 3

sponsor: Advanced Accelerator Applications USA, Inc., a Novartis company (drug developed by Endocyte, Inc., subsequently acquired by Novartis)
pivotal_trial: VISION (Study PSMA-617-01), NCT03511664
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase 3 trial; co-primary endpoints (radiographic progression-free survival, rPFS, and overall survival, OS)

pivotal_trial: Two co-pivotal Phase 3 trials — Study SPI-GCF-301 / "ADVANCE" (NCT02643420) and Study SPI-GCF-302 / "RECOVER" (NCT02953340)
design_text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (pegfilgrastim as the active comparator rather than placebo); two co-pivotal replicate non-inferiority trials required because FDA told the sponsor a single pivotal trial "may not be sufficient evidence for approval of a marketing application of a supportive care drug"

pivotal_trial: TAS-120-101 / FOENIX-CCA2, NCT02052778 (Phase 1/2, cholangiocarcinoma expansion cohort)
design_text: Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 basket trial (dose-escalation followed by Phase 1 expansion across 8 disease groups) supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.500; biomarker-selected/enriched population (FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement, 78% fusions/22% other rearrangements); sample-size logic based on ruling out a historical control response rate

pivotal_trial: HIMALAYA (Study D419CC00002), NCT03298451
design_text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (sorafenib as the active comparator); event-driven trial; originally a four-arm design (tremelimumab 75 mg + durvalumab [T75+D], tremelimumab 300 mg single priming dose + durvalumab [T300+D, the "STRIDE" regimen], durvalumab monotherapy [D], sorafenib [S]) that dropped the T75+D arm mid-trial and restructured to a dual-primary/hierarchical design after an interim analysis from a separate companion trial (Study 22) suggested inferior tolerability/activity for the lower tremelimumab dose

pivotal_trial: MajesTEC-1, NCT03145181 (Phase 1) and NCT04557098 (Phase 2)
design_text: Single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 601.41; step-up ("priming") dosing regimen prior to the therapeutic dose, specifically to mitigate cytokine release syndrome (CRS) risk from a T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody

pivotal_trial: SORAYA (Study IMGN853-0417), NCT04296890
design_text: Single-arm, open-label trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 601.41; biomarker-selected/enriched population (FRα-positive by the VENTANA FOLR1 [FOLR1-2.1] RxDx companion diagnostic assay); companion diagnostic co-approval

pivotal_trial: Study 2102-HV / 2102-HEM-101, NCT02719574 (Phase 2 Cohort 1)
design_text: Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; group-sequential design with two interim analyses for the pivotal Phase 2 Cohort 1; biomarker-selected/enriched population (IDH1-R132 mutation confirmed by companion diagnostic); other Phase 2 cohorts used Simon optimal two-stage designs not relevant to the approval-supporting cohort

pivotal_trial: KRYSTAL-1 (Study 849-001), Cohort A, NCT03785249
design_text: Single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort Phase 1/2 basket trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 314.500; biomarker-selected/enriched population (KRAS G12C mutation by the ctDx FIRST companion diagnostic assay); noncomparative design using a confidence-interval-to-exclude-a-benchmark approach against a literature-derived standard-of-care ORR (descriptive/exact-binomial single-arm response-rate analysis against a pre-specified performance goal)

Single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multi-cohort trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H/21 CFR 601.41; step-up ("priming") dosing regimen across the first two cycles specifically to mitigate CRS risk from a T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody (reused proposed term introduced at teclistamab in this same batch); fixed-duration regimen for complete responders (treatment limited to 8 cycles, with continuation to a maximum of 17 cycles only for patients with a partial response or stable disease)

sponsor: Loxo Oncology, Inc. (a subsidiary of Eli Lilly and Company)
pivotal_trial: BRUIN (Study LOXO-BTK-18001), NCT03740529
design_text: Single-arm, open-label, international, multicenter trial supporting accelerated approval under Subpart H; pirtobrutinib is a noncovalent (reversible) BTK inhibitor, mechanistically distinct from the covalent BTK inhibitors (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib) that all enrolled patients had previously progressed on or discontinued

sponsor: Stemline Therapeutics, Inc. (a Menarini Group company)
pivotal_trial: EMERALD (Study RAD1901-308), NCT03778931
design_text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled Phase III trial (standard-of-care fulvestrant or an aromatase inhibitor as the comparator); stratified randomization by ESR1 mutational status (ESR1-mut vs. ESR1-mut-not-detected) determined by a central ctDNA (Guardant360 CDx) assay; two pre-specified co-primary populations sharing the same endpoint construct — PFS tested as primary in both the ESR1-mut subpopulation and the full ITT population

pivotal_trial: POD1UM-201 / INCMGA 0012-201 (NCT03599713) — an open-label, multiregional, single-arm Phase 2 study of retifanlimab 500 mg IV every 4 weeks in patients with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced MCC who had not received prior systemic therapy for advanced disease; primary efficacy population N=65 chemotherapy-naive patients (FDA's primary analysis population), with a broader safety population of 105 patients
design_text: Single-arm, open-label trial

sponsor: Genmab US, Inc. (Genmab); AbbVie is a collaborator/co-commercialization partner per the ClinicalTrials.gov record for the pivotal trial.
pivotal_trial: EPCORE NHL-1 (Study GCT3013-01; NCT03625037), an open-label, multi-cohort, multicenter, single-arm Phase 1/2 trial; efficacy in the accelerated-approval decision was based on 157 patients with relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) in the aggressive-NHL expansion cohort (label's Table 10 reports on a 148-patient subset restricted to DLBCL-NOS/high-grade B-cell lymphoma, excluding other LBCL subtypes such as PMBCL and FL grade 3B).
design_text: Single-arm, open-label trial

pivotal_trial: LIGHTHOUSE / BED-PSMA-301 (NCT04186819) — newly diagnosed, unfavorable intermediate-, high-, or very-high-risk prostate cancer, pre-prostatectomy nodal staging — and SPOTLIGHT / BED-PSMA-302 (NCT04186845) — suspected biochemical recurrence after prior therapy.
design_text: Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) — both LIGHTHOUSE and SPOTLIGHT were prospective, multicenter, single-arm, open-label, within-patient Phase 3 imaging trials (no control arm; every enrolled patient served as their own comparison against a reference standard), with flotufolastat F 18 PET/CT interpreted by both a local (site) reader and, for the primary endpoint, by three blinded independent central readers (BIE), with a pre-specified majority (2-of-3) read as the primary analysis.

sponsor: Genentech, Inc. (a member of the Roche Group)
pivotal_trial: NP30179 (NCT03075696), an open-label, multicenter, multicohort Phase I/II trial sponsored by Hoffmann-La Roche; the pivotal efficacy cohort was expansion Cohort D3 (fixed-dose obinutuzumab-pretreatment cohort), analyzed in 132 patients
design_text: Single-arm, open-label trial; fixed-duration regimen (glofitamab given for a maximum of 12 cycles regardless of continuing response, after a single fixed 1000 mg obinutuzumab pretreatment dose)

pivotal_trial: QuANTUM-First (Protocol AC220-A-U302), NCT02668653
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; event-driven trial; randomization 1:1 stratified by age, region, and WBC count at diagnosis

sponsor: Janssen Biotech, Inc. (Janssen Research & Development, LLC is the ClinicalTrials.gov study sponsor)
pivotal_trial: MonumenTAL-1 (Study 64407564MMY1001 / MMY1001), a single-arm, open-label, multicenter Phase 1/2 study combining a Phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion study (NCT03399799) and a Phase 2 dose-expansion study (NCT04634552) under one protocol; the two registered subcutaneous regimens (0.4 mg/kg weekly and 0.8 mg/kg every 2 weeks) were the RP2Ds identified in Phase 1 Part 2 and each was independently enrolled and analyzed as a separate, non-randomized Phase 2 Part 3 cohort (Cohort A = 0.4 mg/kg weekly, Cohort C = 0.8 mg/kg biweekly; supportive Cohort B enrolled patients with prior T-cell redirection exposure)
design_text: Single-arm, open-label trial — non-randomized, parallel dose-regimen expansion cohorts (Phase 2 Part 3 Cohort A and Cohort C), each independently analyzed for efficacy rather than compared to one another; FDA's statistical review states plainly "Assignment to treatment: Randomization was not applicable," so patients were assigned to a cohort based on RP2D selection and enrollment period, not individually randomized between the 0.4 mg/kg weekly and 0.8 mg/kg biweekly regimens — "non-randomized parallel dose-regimen expansion cohorts, each analyzed independently"

pivotal_trial: MagnetisMM-3 (Study C1071003, NCT04649359), an open-label, multicenter, non-randomized Phase 2 study; the approved indication is supported by the 97-patient primary efficacy population within Cohort A (BCMA-directed-therapy-naive patients who met the ≥4-prior-line criterion and were treated at the recommended dose)
design_text: Single-arm, open-label trial; two-cohort structure with independent primary endpoints for each cohort — Cohort A (BCMA-directed-therapy-naive) and Cohort B (prior exposure to a BCMA-directed therapy), each with its own null-hypothesis performance goal and its own two-stage exact-binomial design — "two independently-tested, non-comparative prior-therapy-defined cohorts within a single-arm trial, each with a distinct null-hypothesis ORR threshold"

sponsor: Shanghai Junshi Biosciences Co., Ltd. (originator/trial sponsor); Coherus BioSciences, Inc. (U.S. license holder/co-applicant)
pivotal_trial: JUPITER-02 (Study JS001-015-III-NPC, NCT03581786) for indication (1), and POLARIS-02 (Study JS001-Ib-CRP-1.0, NCT02915432) for indication (2)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial for JUPITER-02 (toripalimab + cisplatin/gemcitabine vs. placebo + cisplatin/gemcitabine, 1:1); single-arm, open-label trial for POLARIS-02 (Cohort 3, previously treated patients); both trials were conducted exclusively at sites in China (POLARIS-02) or China/Taiwan/Singapore (JUPITER-02) — regular approval based on entirely foreign (Asia-only) trial data under 21 CFR 314.106(b)

sponsor: Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc. (originally developed by Hutchmed/Hutchison MediPharma Limited, which sponsored the pivotal trial and holds the ClinicalTrials.gov registration)
pivotal_trial: FRESCO-2 (Study 2019-013-GLOB1, NCT04322539), a global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial, with the earlier China-only FRESCO trial as supportive evidence
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (quadruple masking: participant, care provider, investigator, outcomes assessor); event-driven trial; fruquintinib plus best supportive care (BSC) vs. placebo plus BSC, 2:1 randomization

sponsor: Bristol Myers Squibb Company (originally developed by Turning Point Therapeutics, Inc., acquired by BMS in 2022; Turning Point remains the ClinicalTrials.gov study sponsor of record)
pivotal_trial: TRIDENT-1 (Study CA127-1024 / TPX-0005-01, NCT03093116), an international, single-arm, open-label, first-in-human Phase 1/2 dose-escalation-and-expansion study; the primary efficacy evidence comes from pooled expansion cohorts EXP-1 (ROS1 TKI-naive) and EXP-4 (1 prior ROS1 TKI, no prior chemotherapy)
design_text: Single-arm, open-label trial; multi-cohort expansion structure defined by prior ROS1-TKI/chemotherapy exposure (EXP-1 through EXP-6), with EXP-1 and EXP-4 pooled as the primary efficacy analysis populations — this is a ROS1-specific (not tissue/tumor-agnostic) multi-cohort design, so the taxonomy's "Tumor-agnostic (tissue-agnostic) basket trial" term does not apply; described here as "pooled prior-therapy-defined expansion cohorts within a single-arm, single-gene-target trial"

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; dual primary-population design testing PFS in both the all-comers overall population and a pre-specified PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup, both populations pre-specified from trial start rather than post-hoc; randomization stratified by liver metastases, prior CDK4/6 inhibitor use, and geographic region; dedicated China-cohort enrollment target (~134 patients) run in parallel to satisfy NMPA requirements

pivotal_trial: DeFi (Protocol NIR-DT-301), NCT03785964
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; double-blind phase followed by an open-label extension permitting placebo patients to cross to active treatment

sponsor: Avid Radiopharmaceuticals, Inc. (an Eli Lilly and Company subsidiary; adverse-event reporting in the label routes through Eli Lilly and Company)
pivotal_trial: Two phase 3 trials formed the efficacy basis: Study 18F-AV-1451-A16 ("A16," the autopsy/neuropathological-correlation study), NCT02516046, and Study 18F-AV-1451-FR01 ("FR01," the reader-reproducibility substudy), NCT03901092. design_text: diagnostic-accuracy study against an autopsy-confirmed neuropathological reference standard (single-arm, no comparator imaging/mapping agent) — a variant of the taxonomy's "Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison)" in which the paired "reference standard" is postmortem histopathology rather than a second active comparator diagnostic agent (proposed refinement of existing term); co-primary endpoints (Study A16 required both a B3-Braak-stage hypothesis and a separate NIA-AA ADNC hypothesis to each reach significance); prospectively planned inter-reader/intra-reader reproducibility substudy using rereads of the same image set by a second independent panel of five blinded readers (Study FR01)

pivotal_trial: N-MOmentum (Study CD-IA-MEDI-551-1155), NCT02200770

sponsor: Genentech, Inc. (Roche); satralizumab was co-developed and the pivotal trials were run by Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., sponsorship of the BLA was later transferred to Roche/Genentech
