sponsor: Shire Orphan Therapies, Inc. (the 2011 approval holder; the NDA was originally filed in October 2007 by Jerini US, Inc./Jerini AG, and the February 2011 Complete Response was submitted by Shire Human Genetic Therapies, Inc. following Shire's 2008 acquisition of Jerini)
pivotal_trial: Three randomized, double-blind Phase III trials of icatibant 30 mg subcutaneous injection — FAST-1 (Study JE049-2103, NCT00097695), FAST-2 (Study JE049-2102, NCT00500656), and FAST-3 (Study HGT-FIR-054, NCT00912093)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (FAST-1/Study 2103; FAST-3/Study HGT-FIR-054) and randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (FAST-2/Study 2102, versus oral tranexamic acid) trials in the same drug-development program; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1; HAE prevalence ~1 in 10,000-50,000, with 56 randomized patients in FAST-1, 74 in FAST-2, and 88 non-laryngeal randomized patients in FAST-3); approval program with a substantial proportion of negative/failed pivotal trials (adapted from Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1 — of the two trials submitted with the original 2007 NDA, the placebo-controlled FAST-1 did not meet its pre-specified primary endpoint, producing an April 2008 Not Approvable action letter, and FDA required a third confirmatory placebo-controlled trial, FAST-3, before approval); ethically-mandated non-randomized open-label icatibant arm carved out for the most severe (laryngeal) attacks in all three trials, with stochastic-minimization randomization (unequal 80%/20% allocation toward the arm that minimizes imbalance) stratified by symptom location/type and prior C1-inhibitor use for the remaining patients

pivotal_trial: STRIVE (Study 102 / VX08-770-102), NCT00909532 (ages ≥12) and ENVISION (Study 103B / VX08-770-103), NCT00909727 (ages 6-11); both randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials with an identical design and primary endpoint, reviewed together by FDA as the joint efficacy basis for approval
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (STRIVE, ENVISION; quadruple-masked per ClinicalTrials.gov, 14-day run-in, 24-week double-blind efficacy period followed by a second 24-week double-blind "extension" period preserving the blind through Week 48 to assess durability); small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (ENVISION enrolled only 52 subjects, and the approved indication — CF patients with a G551D-CFTR gating mutation — represented only about 4% of the overall CF population per FDA's Medical Review, i.e., a rare mutation-defined subgroup within an already-rare disease); a third, separately reviewed Phase 2 trial (Study 104/VX08-770-104A, NCT00953706) tested the same drug and endpoints in CF patients homozygous for the more common F508del-CFTR mutation and was negative, serving as a mechanistic/genotype-specificity negative control rather than part of the approved indication's evidentiary basis

sponsor: Protalix Biotherapeutics, Ltd. (developed the product; Pfizer, Inc. holds the exclusive worldwide marketing license and is listed as the labeler)
pivotal_trial: PB-06-001, NCT00376168 (randomized, double-blind, dose-ranging trial in treatment-naive patients — FDA's statistical reviewer designated this the sponsor's sole adequate and well-controlled study); supported by PB-06-002, NCT00712348 (open-label switchover trial from imiglucerase/Cerezyme) and PB-06-003, NCT00705939 (blinded long-term extension of both PB-06-001 and PB-06-002)
design_text: small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) — PB-06-001 enrolled only 33 randomized treatment-naive patients, the entire addressable population for a from-scratch Gaucher ERT trial; randomized, double-blind, two-active-dose parallel-group trial with no placebo or active-comparator arm, primary efficacy assessed by two separate within-dose one-sample tests rather than a between-arm comparison; open-label, single-arm switchover trial in patients stable on an already-approved enzyme replacement therapy, with efficacy judged as absence of pre-specified clinical deterioration rather than improvement — PB-06-002; FDA-conducted independent expansion of the efficacy analysis population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) — FDA's statistical reviewer rejected the sponsor's pre-specified Intent-to-Treat definition as under-inclusive for a rare-disease trial and constructed a "Corrected ITT" set restoring 2 excluded randomized patients (31→33) as the basis for all primary analyses; Complete Response Letter (CRL) followed by resubmission and approval (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §7) — original NDA submitted April 26, 2010, CR action issued February 25, 2011, Class 2 resubmission August 1, 2011, approved May 1, 2012

pivotal_trial: MOR-004, NCT01275066, phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (the pivotal publication's author group is named the "STRIVE Investigators," but no acronym is registered for the trial on ClinicalTrials.gov)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm parallel-group trial (elosulfase alfa 2 mg/kg once weekly vs. 2 mg/kg once every other week vs. placebo); small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) — MPS IVA US prevalence estimated at 520-800 patients, with 177 randomized into the entire pivotal program; sponsor sought a Special Protocol Assessment (submitted December 3, 2010) but FDA issued a formal **No-Agreement letter** (January 20, 2011) rather than reaching SPA agreement, so the trial proceeded to completion without SPA protection (*SPA sought, No-Agreement Letter issued — trial proceeds without SPA protection*, distinct from the taxonomy's existing "SPA rescinded" and "SPA formally amended" rows, both of which presuppose an agreement was reached first)

pivotal_trial: GZGD02507 (ENGAGE), NCT00891202 — pivotal, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, treatment-naïve patients; GZGD02607 (ENCORE), NCT00943111 — key supportive, randomized, open-label, active-controlled non-inferiority trial in patients switching from enzyme replacement therapy (ERT)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (ENGAGE, treatment-naïve GD1 patients); Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (ENCORE, non-inferiority switch-from-ERT design against imiglucerase/CEREZYME); Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (ENGAGE N=40; ENCORE N=160; GD1 worldwide incidence estimated at 1 in 50,000-100,000 births per the FDA Summary Review) — ENGAGE recruitment stalled at 16/36 target patients 18 months into enrollment, prompting an April 2011 Type C meeting where the sponsor unsuccessfully proposed shifting the pivotal-efficacy burden to ENCORE

sponsor: Asklepion Pharmaceuticals, LLC (the underlying compassionate-use research program and Investigator IND 45,470 were held by James E. Heubi, MD, and Kenneth D.R. Setchell, PhD, at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center (CCHMC) from 1994; the IND was transferred to Asklepion in May 2007, and Drs. Heubi and Setchell continued treating patients under it thereafter; ClinicalTrials.gov now lists Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. as sponsor of record post-acquisition)
pivotal_trial: CAC-91-10-10 (NCT00007020), "Investigation in the Pathogenesis of Liver Disease in Patients With Inborn Errors of Bile Acid Metabolism" — single-center, open-label, non-randomized treatment/compassionate-use protocol at CCHMC, 1992-2009, N=85 (ITT: 54 SED, 31 PD); supportive: extension trial CAC-002-01 (NCT01438411), open-label continuation, 2010-2016, N=53 (31 rollover + 10 de novo per the FDA Statistical Review's Table 1, growing to 53 total by study completion per ClinicalTrials.gov); also supportive: CAC-001-01 (NCT01115582), a small open-label formulation-bridging study (N=16) comparing the to-be-marketed capsule against the CCHMC-compounded capsule used in CAC-91-10-10
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Single-arm; External/historical control; Literature-based
design_text: small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md, §1) — estimated US prevalence of <100 total patients per the Office of Orphan Products Development designation (2007); multi-decade investigator-held-IND compassionate-use/expanded-access treatment protocol (1992-2009), begun purely as an academic research program with no initial intent to seek marketing approval, later retrospectively reconstituted (via a sponsor-created "Paper CRF" transcribed from patient charts starting in 2007) into the pivotal efficacy/safety dataset for an NDA; sponsor-submitted literature-derived historical control cohort found non-comparable to the treated population and rejected by FDA as an adequate control; open-label continuation/extension trial (CAC-002-01) submitted late in the review cycle and used to materially revise the peroxisomal-disorder efficacy conclusion

pivotal_trial: Two replicate Phase 3 trials — TRAFFIC (VX12-809-103), NCT01807923, and TRANSPORT (VX12-809-104), NCT01807949
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group design; two replicate 24-week Phase 3 trials (TRAFFIC and TRANSPORT), each with 3 arms (placebo, LUM 600mg qd/IVA 250mg q12h, LUM 400mg/IVA 250mg q12h), stratified randomization by age (<18 vs. ≥18), sex, and ppFEV1 severity at screening (<70% vs. ≥70%); biomarker-selected/enriched population (enrollment restricted to CF patients homozygous for the F508del-CFTR mutation, confirmed by genotype — Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, analogous to KEYNOTE-024's PD-L1 selection and FLAURA's EGFR selection); no lumacaftor-monotherapy or ivacaftor-monotherapy arm was included in either pivotal trial, so FDA assessed lumacaftor's own contribution to the combination post hoc via a cross-study "synthesis method" comparing the pivotal trials' placebo-controlled effect against a separately-reviewed ivacaftor-monotherapy phase 2 trial (Study 770-104, from NDA 203-188) under a non-inferiority framework and an untestable "constancy assumption" (contribution-of-components assessment via cross-trial non-inferiority synthesis, used because no monotherapy arm existed in the pivotal trials themselves)

pivotal_trial: Study 401.13.001 ("Open-Label Study of Uridine Triacetate in Pediatric Patients With Hereditary Orotic Aciduria"), NCT02110147, open-label, single-arm/single-group, baseline-controlled, Phase 3, N=4
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Single-arm; External/historical control; Literature-based
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial (no randomized concurrent control) in an ultra-rare monogenic disease — small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md, §1); reviewed under Section 505(b)(2) because dose selection and the efficacy case relied in part on decades of published literature on oral uridine (the drug's active metabolite, to which the sponsor held no right of reference) rather than on a company-run comparator arm — a 505(b)(2), literature-bridged historical-control approval built on physiological/pharmacological reasoning rather than a formal PK-equivalence bridging trial to an already-approved reference product; within-patient, baseline-controlled comparison for 3 of the 4 patients (each was already on chronic oral uridine and was switched to uridine triacetate, serving as their own historical control), plus a single treatment-naïve patient; the trial's 4 enrolled patients were reported by the sponsor to represent all HOA patients identifiable in the United States at the time, out of only ~20 cases (roughly 15 well-documented) ever reported worldwide in the medical literature.

sponsor: Alexion Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (development originated under Enobia Pharma Inc., IND 100,619 opened June 2008; Alexion acquired Enobia and notified FDA of the transfer on February 7, 2012)
pivotal_trial: No single randomized pivotal trial; two indication-specific open-label trial programs, each compared against a separately extracted retrospective natural-history historical-control cohort — perinatal/infantile-onset HPP: ENB-002-08 (NCT00744042, N=11) with long-term extension ENB-003-08 (NCT01205152), pooled with ENB-010-10 (NCT01176266, N=59; combined qualifying N=68) vs. natural-history control ENB-011-10 (NCT01419028, N=48); juvenile-onset HPP: ENB-006-09 (NCT00952484, N=8 juvenile-onset patients of 13 enrolled) with extension ENB-008-10 (NCT01203826) vs. natural-history control ALX-HPP-502 (NCT02104219) and its substudy ALX-HPP-502s (NCT02235493, N=6, gait subset)
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Single-arm; External/historical control; Pooled/basket
design_text: small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) — cohorts of 11 (ENB-002-08), 59 (ENB-010-10), and 8-of-13-enrolled (ENB-006-09) patients; two independently dosed company trials in the same indication pooled post hoc into one primary efficacy population for perinatal/infantile-onset HPP (ENB-002-08/ENB-003-08 + ENB-010-10, combined N=68), related to but not an exact match of the taxonomy's "Cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis (independently conducted, separately sponsored/protocoled trials)" (§1), since both trials share a sponsor/drug and the pooling plan was negotiated with FDA well into trial conduct; primary efficacy analysis compared against a non-randomized, non-concurrent historical control drawn from a separately conducted, eligibility-matched retrospective natural-history chart-review study rather than a randomized concurrent arm — no existing taxonomy term precisely covers this design ("retrospective natural-history chart-review historical control"); a sponsor-proposed randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-arm confirmatory trial for juvenile-onset HPP (ENB-014-12, ~30 patients planned) was never conducted after FDA gave the sponsor the option to substitute the historical-control approach instead

sponsor: Alexion Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (BLA originally filed October 21, 2014 by Synageva BioPharma Corporation, which Alexion acquired in 2015 prior to approval)
pivotal_trial: Two pivotal studies supported full approval under 21 CFR Part 601 for two distinct patient populations — LAL-CL02 / ARISE ("Acid Lipase Replacement Investigating Safety and Efficacy"), NCT01757184, randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in children/adults with CESD; and LAL-CL03, NCT01371825, open-label single-arm dose-escalation phase 1/2 trial in infants with rapidly progressive Wolman-disease-phenotype LAL deficiency, compared against a historical control extracted from the retrospective natural-history study LAL-1-NH01
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trial (LAL-CL02/ARISE; 1:1 randomization via IVRS/IWRS, stratified by age <12/≥12 years, screening ALT <3×ULN/≥3×ULN, and baseline use of lipid-lowering medication), 20-week double-blind period followed by an open-label extension to 130 weeks; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) for LAL-CL03 (9 treated infants); historical natural-history-cohort comparison for a survival endpoint in a single-arm ultra-rare-disease trial, full-approval pathway under 21 CFR Part 601 rather than a threshold-based historical-control comparison (distinct from the taxonomy's existing "non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical-control threshold," since this used a directly matched external cohort analyzed by log-rank test/Cox HR rather than a fixed rate threshold)

pivotal_trial: Study 201 (double-blind, placebo-controlled core), NCT01396239, with continuous open-label extension Study 202, NCT01540409; postmarketing confirmatory trial Study 4658-301 (open-label, multicenter, with a concurrent untreated control arm), NCT02255552, publicly referred to by the sponsor as PROMOVI
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Crossover permitted; Single-arm; External/historical control
design_text: small randomized, single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple-dose trial (N=12) with a 4-week placebo-crossover, rolled into a continuous open-label extension; patient-level comparison of the open-label extension against an external historical-control/DMD-registry cohort (small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population)

sponsor: Biogen Inc. (antisense oligonucleotide originally developed by Ionis Pharmaceuticals)
pivotal_trial: ENDEAR (Study CS3B), NCT02193074, in infantile-onset SMA (2 copies of SMN2); supportive topline (not yet independently FDA-reviewed at approval) data from CHERISH (Study CS4) in later-onset SMA
design_text: randomized (2:1), double-blind, sham-procedure-controlled, event-driven, group-sequential Phase 3 trial, stratified by disease duration at screening (≤12 weeks vs. >12 weeks), with a separate randomization list for Japan; early-stopped for efficacy at a prespecified interim analysis

sponsor: Marathon Pharmaceuticals, LLC (data for the pivotal trials licensed from the original study sponsors; NDA later transferred to PTC Therapeutics)
pivotal_trial: Study MP-104-NM-001 ("Study NM-001," US/Canada, 1993-1995) and supportive Study MP-104-NM-002 ("Study NM-002," Italy, 1988 era) — both conducted more than 20 years before this NDA and neither registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (predating routine US trial registration)
design_text: multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (prednisone), parallel-group trial (NM-001, 1993-1995) plus a supportive randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (NM-002); retroactively reconstructed statistical analysis of decades-old completed trials, with a sponsor-drafted 2015 SAP deviating from the original 1992 protocol's pre-specified primary analysis method (analysis of a historical trial dataset via a modern SAP written decades after study completion, with source documents partially destroyed)

pivotal_trial: Study 190-201/202 (continuous single-arm, open-label, intracerebroventricular dosing study), NCT01907087, compared against non-treatment natural-history cohort Study 190-901 (the DEM-CHILD registry)
design_text: single-arm, open-label, dose-escalation trial (no concurrent control) with efficacy assessed via patient-level matched comparison against an external natural-history registry cohort (matched comparison against an independently conducted, multi-rater natural-history registry, distinct from the taxonomy's existing "non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical-control threshold," which uses no patient-level matching)

pivotal_trial: Study UX003-CL301, NCT02230566 — a randomized, placebo-controlled, "Blind Start," single-crossover (delayed-start) trial; supportive Study CL201 (Phase 1/2 dose-finding, NCT01856218) and Study CL203 (patients <5 years, NCT02418455)
design_text: randomized, placebo-controlled, "Blind Start," single-crossover (delayed-start) trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=12) — a named design (Signorovitch 2014) in which subjects and investigators remain blinded to the timing of each patient's individual crossover from placebo to active drug ("Blind Start"/staggered-crossover design is more specific than the taxonomy's existing general "small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population" entry and was explicitly contested by FDA as a study design during pre-BLA meetings)

pivotal_trial: EVOLVE (Study 106), NCT02347657 (F508del homozygous); EXPAND (Study 108), NCT02392234 (F508del/residual-function heterozygous, crossover); supportive Study 107, NCT02516410 (F508del/minimal-function heterozygous — negative, contributed to the boundaries of the approved population)
design_text: two independent randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials supporting distinct genotype populations — EVOLVE (parallel-group) and EXPAND (2-period, 3-treatment [tezacaftor/ivacaftor, ivacaftor monotherapy, placebo], 6-sequence crossover) — plus a third, differently-genotyped parallel-group trial (Study 107) that was negative and helped define the exclusion of minimal-function mutations from the label

pivotal_trial: PRISM clinical program — Study 165-301 (open-label, randomized dose-regimen induction/titration/maintenance study, NCT01819727) and Study 165-302 (4-part randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized-withdrawal study, NCT01889862)
design_text: randomized-withdrawal (randomized discontinuation) trial design — patients who responded during open-label induction/titration/maintenance are re-randomized to continue active drug or switch to placebo for a fixed period (Keyword_Taxonomy.md does not currently list a "randomized withdrawal/randomized discontinuation" trial-design term; distinct from the taxonomy's crossover and Blind-Start designs)

pivotal_trial: FACETS (Study AT1001-011), NCT00925301 (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled); ATTRACT (Study AT1001-012), NCT01218659 (randomized, open-label, active-controlled switch trial vs. enzyme replacement therapy)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (FACETS) plus a randomized, open-label, active-controlled non-inferiority switch trial from ERT (ATTRACT); efficacy population narrowed after unblinding because a companion in vitro amenability assay was still undergoing validation in parallel with the trial ("efficacy population redefined post hoc by a concurrently-validated companion assay," distinct from the taxonomy's existing FDA-conducted independent expansion/contraction-of-population entries, which involve FDA-driven not assay-driven changes)

pivotal_trial: APOLLO (Study 004), NCT01960348
design_text: randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven Phase 3 trial; notable for being the first FDA approval of a small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutic — a genuinely novel RNA-interference mechanism of action delivered via lipid nanoparticle, requiring a corticosteroid/antihistamine/antipyretic premedication regimen due to infusion-related reactions, though this did not alter the trial's blinded, placebo-controlled structure

pivotal_trial: Study STP-2279-002, NCT01420627 (open-label, multicenter, one-way crossover from pegademase bovine [Adagen] to elapegademase); supportive Study STM-279-301 (open-label, uncontrolled, Japan-directed development program)
design_text: open-label, multicenter, one-way crossover trial (from an already-approved enzyme-replacement product to the new recombinant product) in an extremely small ADA-SCID population (small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population); no formal inferential hypothesis testing performed by the sponsor given sample size

sponsor: Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (commercialized via Akcea Therapeutics, a majority-owned Ionis subsidiary; Akcea is listed as the current applicant of record on Drugs@FDA)
pivotal_trial: NEURO-TTR (Study ISIS 420915-CS2), NCT01737398
design_text: single pivotal trial, Phase 2/3 randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, 66-week treatment trial in a rare/orphan disease population (24 sites, 10 countries), randomization stratified by prior use of TTR-tetramer stabilizers (tafamidis/diflunisal), disease stage (1 vs. 2), and V30M vs. non-V30M TTR mutation

pivotal_trial: VX17-445-102 ("Trial 102"), NCT03525444 (F508del/minimal-function heterozygotes, F/MF, placebo-controlled); and VX17-445-103 ("Trial 103"), NCT03525548 (F508del homozygotes, F/F, active-controlled vs. tezacaftor/ivacaftor)
design_text: two pivotal trials, both randomized, double-blind, parallel-group; Trial 102 (F/MF heterozygotes, placebo-controlled, n=403) had a 24-week treatment period but its primary efficacy endpoint was assessed early, at Week 4, with key secondaries assessed through Week 24 for durability (early-timepoint primary endpoint nested within a longer placebo-controlled trial); Trial 103 (F/F homozygotes, n=107) used only a 4-week double-blind treatment period, active-controlled against background tezacaftor/ivacaftor (TEZ/IVA) after a 4-week open-label TEZ/IVA run-in, and served as the sole comparative efficacy evidence for that population (short 4-week active-controlled trial as sole pivotal comparative evidence)

pivotal_trial: Study 4053-101 (SRP-4053, a first-in-human, 2-part, dose-titration/open-label study), NCT02310906
design_text: small first-in-human trial with a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dose-titration Part 1 (n=12) rolled into a single-arm open-label Part 2 (n=25 golodirsen-treated), with clinical-outcome comparisons drawn against a non-randomized, non-exon-53-amenable untreated comparator group (n=8) rather than a concurrent placebo arm

pivotal_trial: This NDA is unusual in that the applicant's intended pivotal trial was rejected by FDA as inadequate, and approval instead rested on a different, smaller trial run by academic investigators. Three trials matter: the Gillingham et al. (2017) double-blind RCT, NCT01379625 (the trial FDA actually relied on for approval); UX007-CL201, NCT01886378 (the applicant's intended registrational single-arm trial, whose efficacy claim FDA refused to accept); and UX007-CL202, NCT02214160 (an open-label long-term safety/extension study)
design_text: approval rested on a 4-month, double-blind, randomized (1:1), parallel-group, active-comparator trial (triheptanoin vs. trioctanoin, both medium-chain triglycerides), N=32, stratified by diagnosis and site (Gillingham et al. 2017) — not the applicant's intended pivotal design; the applicant's intended pivotal trial (UX007-CL201) was instead an open-label, single-arm, prospective "switch" study (N=29) comparing each patient's own retrospective pre-triheptanoin major-clinical-event rate to their prospective on-treatment rate, a within-patient historical-control design that FDA ultimately ruled inadequate to support a comparative-efficacy claim ("within-patient retrospective historical-control 'switch' design ruled inadequate for a comparative-efficacy claim, approval instead granted on a narrower, non-comparative indication supported by a separate smaller RCT")

sponsor: Genentech, Inc. (member of the Roche Group)
pivotal_trial: FIREFISH, NCT02913482 (Type 1 SMA, open-label, single-arm, two-part); SUNFISH, NCT02908685 (Type 2/3 SMA, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-part)
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Single-arm; External/historical control; Adaptive/seamless; Dose-ranging
design_text: FIREFISH — open-label, single-arm, two-part (Part 1 dose-finding/Part 2 confirmatory), external natural-history/performance-goal comparator, no concurrent control; SUNFISH — two-part seamless, multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, with age-stratified randomization (2-5, 6-11, 12-17, 18-25 years)

sponsor: NS Pharma, Inc. (a subsidiary of Nippon Shinyaku Co., Ltd.)
pivotal_trial: Study NS-065/NCNP-01-201 ("Study 201"), NCT02740972
design_text: very small (n=16), 2-period, multicenter dose-finding trial: a 4-week randomized (3:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled safety period in two sequentially enrolled dose cohorts (40 mg/kg/week, then 80 mg/kg/week), followed by continued open-label dosing through Week 25 with all patients (including former placebo patients) on active drug; functional secondary endpoints compared descriptively against an external natural-history cohort (CINRG DNHS) rather than a concurrent control

sponsor: Eiger BioPharmaceuticals, Inc. (NDA holder at approval; Eiger partnered with the Progeria Research Foundation, which had sponsored the original investigator-initiated trials; Sentynl Therapeutics later acquired U.S. commercialization rights to Zokinvy)
pivotal_trial: two investigator-initiated, open-label, single-arm Phase 2 trials — ProLon1 (Study 07-01-0007), NCT00425607, and ProLon2 (Study 09-06-0298, a zoledronic-acid/pravastatin/lonafarnib triple-therapy protocol), NCT00916747 — with efficacy demonstrated via a post hoc retrospective survival comparison against a 1:1-matched, untreated natural-history cohort from the Progeria Research Foundation's International Progeria Registry (no registered NCT number for the natural-history cohort itself)
design_text: two sequential, non-randomized, open-label, single-arm trials (no concurrent control) pooled and compared retrospectively to a 1:1-matched external natural-history control cohort — a within-disease matched historical-control survival-comparison design run and revised largely under FDA direction after NDA submission ("post hoc 1:1-matched natural-history-control survival analysis, matching algorithm revised by FDA after submission")

pivotal_trial: ILLUMINATE-A, NCT03681184
design_text: randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter/multinational Phase 3 trial in an ultra-rare genetic disease (PH1), ages 6 and older, with stratified randomization on baseline urinary oxalate level

pivotal_trial: Study 4045-301 ("ESSENCE"; a double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study with an open-label extension to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SRP-4045 and SRP-4053 in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy), NCT02500381 — casimersen (SRP-4045) arm, interim Part 1 dystrophin data at Week 48
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter combined trial enrolling two genetically distinct DMD subgroups (exon-45-skip-amenable and exon-53-skip-amenable) into parallel drug-specific arms (casimersen vs. placebo; golodirsen vs. placebo) within one protocol, each arm independently analyzed and used to support a separate NDA ("interim single-arm-of-a-combined-trial biomarker analysis supporting accelerated approval"); 96-week randomized double-blind period (Part 1) plus 48-week open-label extension (Part 2) to Week 144; accelerated approval relied on an interim analysis of the casimersen-arm subset only

sponsor: Origin Biosciences, Inc. (applicant of record on the NDA and approval letter; Origin licensed/acquired the program, including IND 117502, from Alexion Pharmaceuticals, Inc., the original developer, via an IND transfer in September 2018; the drug is currently marketed by Sentynl Therapeutics, Inc., a BridgeBio Pharma affiliate, which was not the NDA holder at the time of approval)
pivotal_trial: no single randomized pivotal trial; the "adequate and well-controlled investigation" was a pooled, cross-study, genotype-matched external-control survival comparison built from four studies: MCD-501 (retrospective observational, NCT01640717), MCD-201 (open-label, NCT02047461), and MCD-202 (open-label Phase 2/3, originally intended as the confirmatory trial, NCT02629393) as the treated cohort, versus MCD-502 (retrospective-and-prospective natural-history study, NCT01735188) as the untreated historical-control cohort
design_text: uncontrolled, open-label, single-arm/multi-study pooled treatment cohort (n=13 across three trials) compared to an external, non-contemporaneous, genotype-matched natural-history control cohort (n=18 matched of a 37-patient full untreated cohort) — a genotype-matched external/historical-control survival comparison ("genotype-matched full-matching survival comparison against a pooled external natural-history cohort, with inverse-probability weighting for unequal match ratios"); the originally planned confirmatory trial (MCD-202) used a Bayesian design comparing a responder proportion to a fixed threshold derived from an interim natural-history analysis, but was abandoned after enrollment failure (1 patient enrolled) in favor of a post hoc pooled overall-survival analysis

sponsor: Albireo Pharma, Inc. (original NDA applicant; Ipsen acquired Albireo in 2023 and is the current marketing sponsor)
pivotal_trial: Trial A4250-005 (PEDFIC 1), NCT03566238
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=62, three arms)

pivotal_trial: Trial EFC14028 (COMET), NCT02782741
design_text: randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial (avalglucosidase alfa vs. alglucosidase alfa, not placebo); non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=100)

pivotal_trial: Trial LUM001-304 (ICONIC), NCT02160782
design_text: randomized-withdrawal design (open-label run-in followed by a double-blind, placebo-controlled withdrawal period); small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=31 enrolled, 29 randomized)

randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=121); pre-trial natural-history run-in period used to establish each subject's own baseline growth rate (Study 111-901) rather than an in-trial placebo run-in

pivotal_trial: Study 1042-CDD-3001 (Marigold), NCT03572933
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=101)

pivotal_trial: Study ALN-TTRSC02-002 (HELIOS-A), NCT03759379; external control drawn from the APOLLO trial (NCT01960348, patisiran)
design_text: randomized (3:1), open-label, active-controlled trial (vutrisiran vs. patisiran as a concurrent reference/active comparator) combined with an external placebo control drawn from a different, previously completed trial (APOLLO) of the related approved drug patisiran; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=164 randomized in HELIOS-A; N=77 external APOLLO placebo)

pivotal_trial: Trial DFI12712 (ASCEND), NCT02004691; supported by Trial DFI13803 (ASCEND-Peds)
design_text: randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with a crossover extension (placebo-arm subjects crossed over to active treatment after the primary analysis period); small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=36)

sponsor: Chiesi Farmaceutici S.p.A. (trial rhLAMAN-05 was originally conducted by Zymenex A/S, later acquired by Chiesi)
pivotal_trial: Trial rhLAMAN-05, NCT01681953; supported by Trial rhLAMAN-08 and the rhLAMAN-10 integrated long-term analysis
design_text: randomized (3:2), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=25); trial conducted entirely outside the US (EU, supporting a 2018 EMA approval) with no FDA input into its design, later repurposed as the single pivotal trial for a US BLA after a planned US confirmatory trial (SHAMAN) was abandoned pre-enrollment due to COVID-19

pivotal_trial: Study PROTECT, NCT03762850 (single trial serving as both the accelerated-approval interim-analysis study and its own confirmatory trial at final analysis)
design_text: randomized (1:1), double-blind, active-controlled trial (sparsentan vs. irbesartan, an ARB — not placebo, since background ACEI/ARB therapy could not ethically be withheld); single trial with a planned unblinded interim analysis used for accelerated approval and the same trial's final analysis used as the confirmatory trial ("Single trial serving as both the accelerated-approval basis and its own confirmatory trial via a pre-planned interim-then-final-analysis structure," distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Accelerated approval based on a randomized, non-registrational Phase 2 trial," where the confirmatory trial is a separate, later study)

sponsor: Reata Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (original NDA applicant; Biogen acquired Reata in 2023, after this approval)
design_text: randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, stratified by pes cavus status, nested within a larger 2-part study (Part 1 was a separate dose-ranging stage); small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=103 randomized, 82 in the primary efficacy analysis set)

sponsor: Chiesi Farmaceutici S.p.A. (sponsor of record on the BLA per FDA's Drugs@FDA overview page; pegunigalsidase alfa was originated by Protalix BioTherapeutics/Protalix Ltd., which manufactures the enzyme and is sponsor of record for the pivotal trial on ClinicalTrials.gov; Chiesi USA, Inc. distributes the product in the US under license from Protalix)
pivotal_trial: BALANCE (Protalix protocol PB-102-F20), NCT02795676 — a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled switch trial in ERT-experienced Fabry patients; FDA's review ultimately treated BALANCE as confirmatory evidence rather than the sole "adequate and well-controlled" trial, with that role instead filled by the single-arm renal-biopsy trial PB-102-F01/F02 (part of the same early-phase dose-ranging program registered as NCT01678898)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, switch/continuation-of-therapy design (all patients ERT-experienced on agalsidase beta ≥1 year before randomization), small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population, regular approval grounded in a single-arm histological-surrogate trial (renal Gb3/BLISS score) as the sole adequate and well-controlled study, with a randomized active-controlled trial downgraded from primary to confirmatory evidence after FDA rejected the sponsor's non-inferiority margin

sponsor: Ipsen Biopharmaceuticals, Inc. — palovarotene was originally developed by Clementia Pharmaceuticals Inc. (which licensed the compound from Roche and held the IND from 2014), and Clementia was acquired by Ipsen in April 2019; Ipsen is the applicant of record on NDA 215559 (FDA Integrated Review, Reference ID 5227463, p.2, Table 1: "Applicant — Ipsen Biopharmaceuticals, Inc.")
pivotal_trial: Study PVO-1A-301 ("MOVE" trial), NCT03312634, with Clementia's separately conducted natural history study PVO-1A-001 (NCT02322255) serving as the external untreated-comparator cohort
design_text: small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (~800 confirmed FOP cases worldwide); Phase 3, multicenter, open-label, single-arm study using a non-concurrent natural-history-study cohort as an external control for the primary efficacy comparison, rather than a randomized or placebo comparator (no existing taxonomy row covers an external natural-history control design); partial clinical hold on a specific age-defined pediatric subgroup imposed mid-trial for an emergent safety signal, with treatment never resumed in that subgroup

pivotal_trial: R3918-PLE-1878, NCT04209634, open-label, single-arm, phase 2/3
design_text: single-arm, open-label trial (no randomized concurrent control) in an ultra-rare monogenic disease (worldwide patient count in the low tens at time of filing); FDA-accepted external-control design under 21 CFR 314.126, using two historical-control sources — a published 14-patient uncontrolled case series of eculizumab-treated CHAPLE patients (Ozen 2021; Kurolap 2019), and each enrolled subject's own pre-treatment medical-chart history — rather than a concurrent placebo arm, which the sponsor and FDA agreed would be unethical given prior evidence that C5 inhibition (eculizumab) resolves life-threatening manifestations; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md, §1); within-patient (pre-treatment vs. on-treatment) comparison as a secondary analytic frame for hospitalization, growth, and other objective endpoints

sponsor: Amicus Therapeutics (co-reviewed and co-approved in parallel with NDA 215211 for Opfolda/miglustat, the obligate co-administered oral chaperone, also an Amicus product incorporating Zavesca/miglustat safety data by reference from Actelion's NDA 021348)
pivotal_trial: ATB200-03 / PROPEL, NCT03729362
design_text: randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (vs. non-U.S.-approved alglucosidase alfa co-administered with oral placebo), parallel-group, multicenter, international phase 3 trial; 2:1 randomization, stratified by baseline 6MWD category and ERT status (ERT-experienced vs. ERT-naive), not stratified by center

sponsor: Novo Nordisk, Inc., c/o Dicerna Pharmaceuticals, Inc. — Dicerna Pharmaceuticals originated and developed nedosiran (internal code DCR-PHXC) and ran the pivotal trial as lead sponsor of record on ClinicalTrials.gov; Novo Nordisk A/S acquired Dicerna in December 2021, and the NDA itself (submitted September 30, 2022) lists Novo Nordisk, Inc. as the applicant, with Dicerna staff handling regulatory correspondence
pivotal_trial: PHYOX2 (sponsor protocol DCR-PHXC-201), NCT03847909
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group; small ultra-rare-disease trial population (35 randomized: 23 nedosiran, 12 placebo); covariate-adaptive minimization randomization (2:1 ratio, 80%/20% biased-coin allocation to the treatment minimizing imbalance across age-category and eGFR-category strata) (not currently a distinct row in Keyword_Taxonomy.md § Trial design)

sponsor: Santhera Pharmaceuticals (Switzerland) Ltd. (applicant of record on the original NDA and the FDA approval letter, dated October 26, 2023); the underlying IND (118,942) had been held by ReveraGen BioPharma, Inc. through most of development and was transferred to Santhera on October 1, 2022, shortly before NDA submission; Catalyst Pharmaceuticals, Inc. became the applicant of record on the first efficacy supplement (NDA 215239/S-001, approved 2024) after acquiring North American commercialization rights, and is now listed as the current "Company" on Drugs@FDA's overview page for this application
pivotal_trial: Study VBP15-004 ("VISION-DMD"), NCT03439670
design_text: randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo- and active-controlled trial in which the placebo and prednisone arms crossed over to vamorolone at a fixed protocol timepoint (Week 24-28) rather than at investigator/patient-triggered progression — this fixed-timepoint mandatory crossover of control arms is distinct from the taxonomy's existing "crossover permitted at progression" entry ("fixed-timepoint mandatory crossover of control arms to the experimental drug"); six treatment groups (vamorolone 2.0 mg/kg, vamorolone 6.0 mg/kg, prednisone 0.75 mg/kg, placebo, each further split by Period 2 vamorolone dose) randomized 2:2:1:1:1:1, stratified by baseline age (<6 years vs. ≥6 years); small randomized trial (n=121) in a rare pediatric neuromuscular disease

sponsor: Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was the applicant of record at the time of FDA approval — the NDA approval letter (December 21, 2023) is addressed to Ionis Pharmaceuticals, and FDA's Integrated Review lists "Applicant: Ionis Pharmaceuticals" in its Application Information table — eplontersen was developed by Ionis in collaboration with Akcea Therapeutics under IND 139521. Drugs@FDA's current overview page for NDA 217388 lists "AstraZeneca AB" as the sponsor, reflecting AstraZeneca's role as Ionis's global collaboration/commercialization partner for eplontersen; the exact administrative date on which applicant-of-record status transferred to AstraZeneca was not independently confirmed in this research pass
pivotal_trial: NEURO-TTRansform (Study ION-682884-CS3), NCT04136184; its efficacy comparator was not a concurrent placebo arm but the external/historical placebo cohort from the earlier pivotal inotersen trial NEURO-TTR (ISIS-420915-CS2, NCT01737398, EudraCT 2012-001831-30)
design_text: randomized (6:1), open-label, multicenter, multinational Phase 3 trial with a concurrent active-reference arm (inotersen, summarized descriptively only, no statistical comparison) plus a propensity-score-weighted external (cross-trial) historical placebo control drawn from a prior, separately conducted pivotal trial of a different drug in the same indication, used in place of a concurrent placebo arm ("randomized, open-label trial with a propensity-score-weighted external/historical placebo control substituting for a concurrent placebo arm"); single adequate/well-controlled trial supported by pharmacodynamic/mechanistic confirmatory evidence and same-class precedent (*Regular approval supported by same-pharmacologic-class precedent as confirmatory evidence*)

sponsor: Italfarmaco S.p.A. (Italian parent company, applicant of record on the NDA; U.S. commercial distribution and labeling is through ITF Therapeutics, LLC, Italfarmaco's U.S. subsidiary; the NDA's U.S. regulatory agent of record was Freyr Inc.)
pivotal_trial: EPIDYS (Italfarmaco/Veristat internal designation "Study 48," DSC/14/2357/48; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02851797; EudraCT 2016-000401-36)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre, quadruple-masked (participant/caregiver/investigator/outcomes-assessor) Phase 3 trial; 2:1 randomization (givinostat:placebo); stratified by concomitant corticosteroid regimen (4 strata: deflazacort daily, deflazacort intermittent, other-steroid daily, other-steroid intermittent); biomarker-selected/enriched population — a prospectively defined "Target Population" (baseline vastus lateralis muscle fat fraction [VL MFF] by MRS >5% and ≤30%) served as the sole primary-efficacy analysis population, with a concurrently enrolled "Off-Target Population" (VL MFF ≤5% or >30%) providing supportive-only data, not formally tested; single planned interim analysis conducted by an independent data monitoring committee (IDMC)

randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group (not crossover), multicenter, international phase 3 trial in an ultra-rare disease population; 1:1 randomization stratified by prior immunoglobulin (Ig) replacement use; 52-week Randomized Placebo-Controlled Period followed by an open-label extension, with a prespecified "Early Release" pathway (blinded independent Adjudication Committee-determined) allowing subjects with recurrent/significant infections to cross over early into open-label treatment — also fits *Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population*

sponsor: Zevra Denmark A/S (the application was originally submitted by Orphazyme A/S in 2020; ownership of NDA 214927 and IND 124547 was transferred to KemPharm Denmark A/S on June 10, 2022, and KemPharm's corporate name was changed to Zevra Denmark A/S on April 13, 2023; the September 2024 NDA approval letter is addressed to "Zevra Denmark A/S c/o Zevra Therapeutics, Inc.")
pivotal_trial: CT-ORZY-NPC-002 ("Study NPC-002"), a 12-month randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, NCT02612129
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population, 2:1 randomization stratified by background-miglustat-use status, post-Complete-Response-Letter primary-endpoint redefinition on the same pivotal trial's dataset

sponsor: IntraBio Ltd. (applicant of record at approval; the product was acquired by Zevra Pharmaceuticals shortly after approval and is now marketed under the Zevra corporate umbrella, per assignment brief — the FDA review and label of record both name IntraBio Ltd./IntraBio Inc. as applicant/distributor)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover trial (no washout period between periods); small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=60)

pivotal_trial: SKYLINE Trials VX20-121-102 (Trial 102), NCT05033080, and VX20-121-103 (Trial 103), NCT05076149 (supportive pediatric PK/safety: RIDGELINE Trial VX21-121-105)
design_text: two co-pivotal randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor [ELX/TEZ/IVA]), parallel-group noninferiority trials, each with a 4-week active run-in period to establish an on-treatment baseline; randomization stratified by age, run-in ppFEV1, run-in sweat chloride, and prior CFTR-modulator use

sponsor: Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation (compound originated at Abbott Laboratories/AbbVie as ABT-627/CHK-01, then licensed to Chinook Therapeutics, which Novartis acquired in 2023)
pivotal_trial: ALIGN Trial (Study CHK01-01), NCT04573478
design_text: ongoing, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial with background RASi therapy in all subjects; two enrollment strata (main non-SGLT2i stratum and an exploratory SGLT2i stratum) with separate randomization schedules; group-sequential design with a single pre-specified unblinded interim analysis at the first 270 randomized subjects' Week-36 visit, used as the basis for accelerated approval while the trial continues to its Week-136 eGFR-slope readout

pivotal_trial: APHENITY (PKU-003), NCT05099640 (supportive: PKU-002; long-term extension: PKU-004)
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Randomized withdrawal; Single-arm; Dose-ranging
design_text: two-part, phase 3, global trial — Part 1 an open-label, single-arm 14-day responsiveness-determination run-in (≥15% blood Phe reduction required to proceed), followed by a 14-day washout, then Part 2 a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalating (20→40→60 mg/kg QD) parallel-group trial restricted to Part-1 responders aged ≥2 years; run-in responder-enrichment design (open-label lead-in used to select pharmacodynamic responders before randomization, distinct from a randomized-withdrawal design since no one was exposed to drug during a subsequent placebo phase)

pivotal_trial: SPIBA-201 / TAZPOWER, NCT03098797 (Part 1: randomized crossover; Part 2/TAZPOWER Extension: single-arm open-label); supportive externally-controlled study SPIBA-001
design_text: small (N=12), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover trial (Part 1, no washout gap issue but a 4-week washout between periods) followed by a long-term (192-week), single-arm, open-label extension in a subset (Part 2/TAZPOWER Extension, N=10); small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Barth syndrome, ~150 U.S. patients)

pivotal_trial: Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE) pooling Trial TK0102 (NCT03845712, ongoing single-arm open-label), Study MT-1621-101 (NCT03701568, retrospective chart review), Study MT-1621-107 (NCT05017818, retrospective chart review), EAP/TK0114 (NCT06590493), and a literature-derived Updated Untreated Patient Database
design_text: cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis combining a prospective single-arm open-label trial, two retrospective chart-review natural-history studies, an expanded-access program, and a literature-derived untreated-patient database, compared via a matched external-control survival analysis (4-parity matched-pair external-control design — random, 50th-, 75th-, and 100th-percentile selection rules for assigning one untreated match per treated subject from an eligible "upper-half" pool)

pivotal_trial: VISIONARY (Trial 417-201-00007), NCT05248646 (long-term extension: NCT05248659)
design_text: ongoing, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial with background ACEI/ARB (± SGLT2i) therapy; main cohort (eGFR ≥30) plus a small exploratory cohort (eGFR 20-29, not the focus of this review); randomization stratified by screening UPCR, screening eGFR band, and SGLT2i use; group-sequential design with a single pre-specified unblinded interim analysis at 62.5% information fraction, used as the basis for accelerated approval

pivotal_trial: Integrated efficacy analysis pooling Study 90-CH-0149 (NCT00001262, NIH, 1990-2013) and Study 09-CH-0059 (NCT00811785, NIH Phase 3, 2009-2019), both open-label single-arm studies conducted at the NIH Clinical Center; supportive ongoing expanded-access program CYP-001
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Single-arm; External/historical control; Pooled/basket
design_text: cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis of two decades-spanning, NIH-run, open-label single-arm academic studies, compared against an untreated historical-control cohort via four parallel age-of-symptom-onset-stratified matching schemes (random, 50th-, 75th-, and 100th-percentile selection of one untreated match per treated subject) — structurally the same matched-external-control survival design as Kygevvi/doxecitine-doxribtimine (entry 6), independently arrived at by a different sponsor/review division for a different ultra-rare metabolic disease

sponsor: Immedica Pharma AB (originally developed by Aeglea BioTherapeutics, Inc.; BLA ownership transferred to Immedica in September 2023)
pivotal_trial: PEACE (Trial CAEB1102-300A), NCT03921541
design_text: randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, single-pivotal-trial (single adequate and well-controlled trial) superiority trial, stratified by severity of prior hyperammonemia history; small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (N=32)

pivotal_trial: DNLI-E-0002, NCT04251026 (supportive natural-history study: DNLI-E-0001; long-term extension: NCT06075537)
design_text: Phase 1/2, single-arm, open-label, multi-cohort dose-escalation trial with no concurrent control, accepted by FDA as a "baseline-controlled" adequate and well-controlled trial for a biomarker endpoint rather than a randomized design; brain-penetrant enzyme-replacement therapy using a transferrin-receptor-targeting fusion protein (an "ETV"/BBB-crossing platform) engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier, distinguishing it from conventional (non-CNS-penetrant) MPS II enzyme-replacement therapies

pivotal_trial: ORIGIN 3 (Study VT-001-0050), NCT04716231 — Week 36 interim analysis (Interim Analysis Set, N=203 of 428 dosed); final analysis (eGFR slope through Week 104) pending as the accelerated-approval confirmatory endpoint
design_text: randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase 2b/3 trial; accelerated approval granted from a prespecified unblinded interim analysis of an ongoing randomized trial, with that same trial's later final analysis serving as the confirmatory/verification evidence rather than an independently conducted confirmatory trial (distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Confirmatory evidence via continuation/expansion of the same pivotal single-arm trial," which covers single-arm, not randomized, designs; this proteinuria-to-eGFR paradigm is shared with other recent IgAN drugs such as sparsentan and atrasentan)

pivotal_trial: Study 1, NCT05394116 (Phase 3, 56-week double-blind period plus double-blind extension)
design_text: small (N=63), randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter, placebo-controlled, three-arm (two active doses + placebo) Phase 3 trial in an ultra-rare disease population — an extension of the taxonomy's existing "Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population" entry (previously seen in Lomitapide, Mipomersen, Metreleptin, Evinacumab-dgnb) to a three-arm dose-comparison version

pivotal_trial: Study 1, NCT04849741 — double-blind, randomized, controlled Main Study (N=49, ages 2-65) plus a 4-patient open-label substudy in children under 2 years
design_text: small (Main Study N=49; total N=53 with the open-label substudy), randomized (2:1 within ascending-dose cohorts), double-blind, controlled, multi-part Phase 1-3 trial in an ultra-rare pediatric/adult leukodystrophy population, with randomization stratified by age, motor-symptom onset, and a gross-motor-abnormality criterion — an instance of the taxonomy's existing "Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population" entry

sponsor: Human Genome Sciences, Inc. (co-developed with GlaxoSmithKline)
control: Placebo; Dose comparison; Standard of care
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1:1 parallel-group, multicenter, international phase 3 trials (52-week BLISS-52 and 76-week BLISS-76), two co-identical dose arms (belimumab 1 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg) plus placebo, all on top of standard-of-care SLE therapy; randomization stratified by baseline SELENA-SLEDAI score (6-9 vs. ≥10), proteinuria level, and race (African/indigenous-American descent vs. other)

pivotal_trial: BENEFIT, NCT00256750, and BENEFIT-EXT, NCT00114777
design_text: two randomized, active-controlled (cyclosporine), open-label(-ish; blinded central adjudication where feasible), parallel-group, multicenter, international phase 3 trials, each with 3 arms — belatacept more-intensive (MI) regimen, belatacept less-intensive (LI) regimen, and cyclosporine — in standard-criteria/living-donor kidney recipients (BENEFIT) or extended-criteria-donor (ECD) kidney recipients (BENEFIT-EXT)

pivotal_trial: Four phase 3 trials — Study 016 (PEP005-016, NCT00916006) and Study 025 (PEP005-025, NCT00915551) for face/scalp; Study 014 (PEP005-014, NCT00742391) and Study 028 (PEP005-028, NCT00942604) for trunk/extremities
design_text: four near-identical, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter (US + Australia) phase 3 trials, run as two co-identical pairs (one pair per anatomic location/dose/regimen), each 1:1 randomized and stratified by site (and, for the head trials, by anatomic sub-location target of ~80% face/~20% scalp); Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) agreement reached with FDA for the non-head-location design in June 2008, before the head-location trials were designed by extension of the same agreed template

pivotal_trial: ORAL Solo (A3921045), NCT00814307; ORAL Standard (A3921064), NCT00853385; ORAL Sync (A3921046), NCT00856544; ORAL Scan (A3921044), NCT00847613; and A3921032 (TNF-inadequate-responder trial), NCT00960440
design_text: five phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials differing in background therapy/population (monotherapy in ORAL Solo; background methotrexate with an adalimumab active-comparator arm in ORAL Standard; background non-biologic DMARD in ORAL Sync; background methotrexate with 2-year radiographic follow-up in ORAL Scan; background methotrexate in TNF-inadequate responders in A3921032); placebo patients advanced (rescued) to tofacitinib at Month 3 (all placebo non-responders) and/or Month 6 per trial, blinding maintained via a pre-determined blinded treatment sequence

three near-identical, multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trials, each 1:1:1 to apremilast 20 mg BID (A20), apremilast 30 mg BID (A30), or placebo, with a titration period during the first 7 days; concurrent stable background DMARD therapy (methotrexate, sulfasalazine, or leflunomide) permitted; blinded early-escape mechanism at Week 16 for inadequate responders (<20% joint-count improvement), with placebo-arm early-escapers re-randomized 1:1 (blinded) to A20 or A30; at Week 24 all remaining placebo patients crossed over to A20/A30 under a blinded re-randomization

pivotal_trial: ERASURE (Trial 2302 / A2302), NCT01365455, and FIXTURE (Trial 2303 / A2303), NCT01358578
design_text: two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, international phase 3 trials — ERASURE was 3-arm (secukinumab 300 mg, 150 mg, placebo); FIXTURE was 4-arm, adding an EU-sourced etanercept active-comparator arm; both used lyophilized-formulation (LYO) secukinumab, subcutaneous, with an induction schedule followed by monthly maintenance dosing; randomization stratified by geographic region and baseline body weight (<90 kg vs. ≥90 kg)

pivotal_trial: MENSA (Study 88/MEA115588, NCT01691521) and SIRIUS (Study 75/MEA115575, NCT01691508)
control: Placebo; Dose comparison; Standard of care
design_text: two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, international phase 3 trials with different regimens and objectives — MENSA (exacerbation-reduction trial, 32 weeks, 3-arm: mepolizumab 75 mg IV, 100 mg SC, or placebo, added to standard of care) and SIRIUS (oral-corticosteroid-sparing trial, 24 weeks including a 3-4 week OCS-optimization run-in, 2-arm: mepolizumab 100 mg SC or placebo, with a mandatory OCS down-titration schedule); a supportive Phase 2b dose-ranging trial (Study 97/DREAM, IV doses 75/250/750 mg vs. placebo) preceded both and informed dose selection

pivotal_trial: UNCOVER-1 (Trial RHAZ/I1F-MC-RHAZ), UNCOVER-2 (Trial RHBA/I1F-MC-RHBA), UNCOVER-3 (Trial RHBC/I1F-MC-RHBC)
design_text: three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, international phase 3 trials in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (PASI≥12, sPGA≥3, BSA≥10%); UNCOVER-1 was 3-arm (ixekizumab Q2W, ixekizumab Q4W, placebo); UNCOVER-2 and UNCOVER-3 were 4-arm, adding a US-licensed (Enbrel) or EU-approved etanercept active-comparator arm depending on study site; all ixekizumab arms received a 160 mg loading dose at baseline followed by 80 mg Q2W or Q4W through Week 12; UNCOVER-1 and UNCOVER-2 continued into a 48-week maintenance/re-randomization period

sponsor: Teva Respiratory, LLC (originally developed by Cephalon/Ception Therapeutics)
pivotal_trial: Study 3082 (C38072/3082, NCT01287039) and Study 3083 (C38072/3083, NCT01285323), two identically-designed 52-week exacerbation trials; supportive Study 3081 (C38072/3081, 16-week FEV1 trial) and Study 3084 (C38072/3084, 16-week FEV1 trial in an eosinophil-unselected population)
design_text: four principal phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials — two identically-designed, concurrently-conducted 52-week trials (3082, 3083) powered for exacerbation-rate reduction in an eosinophil-selected population (≥400 cells/µL at screening), plus two 16-week trials (3081, testing two IV doses [0.3 mg/kg, 3.0 mg/kg] in the same eosinophil-selected population; 3084, testing 3.0 mg/kg in an eosinophil-unselected population) powered for FEV1 change from baseline; primary efficacy analyses pre-specified to include all randomized subjects regardless of prohibited-medication use or discontinuation

pivotal_trial: Trial 301 (AD-301) and Trial 302 (AD-302), two identically-designed phase 3 trials
design_text: two identically-designed, randomized, multicenter, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trials (2:1 randomization to crisaborole 2% ointment or vehicle ointment, twice daily for 28 days) in patients ≥2 years old with atopic dermatitis, BSA involvement ≥5% (excluding scalp), and Investigator's Static Global Assessment (ISGA) of 2 (mild) or 3 (moderate); centers with low enrollment were pooled into combined "analysis centers" per a pre-specified minimum-enrollment rule before being used as a stratification factor

sponsor: Valeant Pharmaceuticals Luxembourg S.à r.l. (via Valeant Pharmaceuticals North America LLC) — originally developed by Amgen Inc. (co-developed with AstraZeneca); see regulatory history below.
pivotal_trial: AMAGINE-2, NCT01708603, and AMAGINE-3, NCT01708629 (identically designed, placebo- and ustekinumab-active-comparator-controlled); supportive placebo-only AMAGINE-1, NCT01708590.
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator (ustekinumab)-controlled, parallel-group trials (AMAGINE-2/3); randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AMAGINE-1)

pivotal_trial: SOLO 1 (Study R668-AD-1334), NCT02277743, and SOLO 2 (Study R668-AD-1416), NCT02277769 — identically designed co-primary monotherapy registration trials; supportive combination-with-topical-corticosteroids trial CHRONOS (Study R668-AD-1224), NCT02260986.
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter Phase 3 trials (SOLO 1 and SOLO 2 monotherapy; CHRONOS as dupilumab + topical corticosteroids vs. placebo + topical corticosteroids)

pivotal_trial: MOBILITY (SARIL-RA-MOBILITY, Study EFC11072), NCT01061736 — methotrexate-inadequate-responder population; TARGET (SARIL-RA-TARGET, Study EFC10832), NCT01709578 — TNF-inadequate-responder/intolerant population.
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, international add-on trials (MOBILITY: add-on to background methotrexate; TARGET: add-on to background non-biologic DMARD in TNF-inadequate-responders); MOBILITY was an operationally seamless two-part dose-ranging-and-confirmatory design

pivotal_trial: VOYAGE 1 (Trial 3001), NCT02207231, and VOYAGE 2 (Trial 3002, with a randomized-withdrawal-and-retreatment period), NCT02207244 — both placebo- and adalimumab-active-comparator-controlled.
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator (adalimumab)-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials; VOYAGE 2 added a randomized-withdrawal-and-retreatment period (Week 28-76) for Week-28 PASI90 responders

pivotal_trial: SIROCCO (Study D3250C0017), NCT01928771, and CALIMA (Study D3250C0018), NCT01914757 (both exacerbation-reduction trials); ZONDA (Study D3250C0020), NCT02075255 (oral-corticosteroid-sparing trial).

sponsor: Merck Sharp & Dohme Corporation (sponsor of record at original approval; rights later transferred to Sun Pharmaceutical Industries post-approval).
pivotal_trial: reSURFACE 1 (Protocol MK-3222-010), NCT01722331, and reSURFACE 2 (Protocol MK-3222-011, with an etanercept active-comparator arm), NCT01729754.

sponsor: Eli Lilly and Company (co-developed with Incyte).
pivotal_trial: RA-BEAM, NCT01710358 (MTX-inadequate-responders, active comparator adalimumab) — FDA's primary efficacy/statistical source; supportive RA-BUILD, NCT01721057 (cDMARD-inadequate-responders), and RA-BEACON, NCT01721044 (TNF-inadequate-responders, the population matching the approved indication).
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator (adalimumab)-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trial (RA-BEAM), add-on to background methotrexate

sponsor: Dyax Corporation (a Shire/Takeda subsidiary at the time of approval; Dyax is the applicant of record on the BLA).
pivotal_trial: HELP Study (DX-2930-03), NCT02586805.
