sponsor: Allergan, Inc. (originator/co-developer Almirall, S.A., which holds the ClinicalTrials.gov sponsor registration and ran the pivotal trials).
pivotal_trial: SC1401, NCT02320149, and SC1402, NCT02322866 — identically designed 12-week Phase 3 trials.
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, identically designed twin Phase 3 trials in facial acne vulgaris (ages 9-45)

sponsor: AbbVie Inc. (originally co-developed with Boehringer Ingelheim, compound code BI 655066/ABBV-066).
pivotal_trial: ultIMMa-1 (Trial 1311.3/M16-008), NCT02684370, and ultIMMa-2 (Trial 1311.28/M15-995), NCT02684357 — both placebo- and ustekinumab-active-comparator-controlled.
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo- and ustekinumab-active-comparator-controlled, 52-week Phase 3 trials; randomization stratified by body weight (≤100 kg vs. >100 kg) and prior TNF-antagonist exposure

pivotal_trial: SELECT-COMPARE (M14-465), NCT02629159
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (adalimumab), multicenter, phase 3 trial; 2:2:1 randomization (placebo : upadacitinib 15 mg QD : adalimumab 40 mg every-other-week), stratified by prior biologic-DMARD exposure; treat-through design with blinded rescue/crossover for inadequate responders at Weeks 14/18/22 — patients on any arm meeting a pre-specified non-response rule (≤20% improvement in tender/swollen joint counts) were blindly switched to a different randomized arm rather than simply continuing or being classified as failures in place ("Blinded rescue-crossover (treat-through) design," distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Crossover permitted at progression," which is unblinded and post-progression only)

pivotal_trial: Study 1, NCT02566369, and Study 2, NCT02556788 (per the FDA-approved label; these two identically-designed trials are not given a named acronym in the label, SAP, ClinicalTrials.gov, or the pivotal publication — a "PERFECT 1/2" name sometimes attached to this program in secondary sources could not be verified against any primary source and should not be used)
design_text: two identically-designed, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group phase 3 trials; 1:1 randomization stratified by clinical trial center; approximately 1,200 subjects planned per trial (612/596 and 602/610 randomized to trifarotene/vehicle respectively)

pivotal_trial: OPTIC (Study 301/HZNP-TEP-301), NCT03298867; supported by Phase 2 Study TED01RV (RV 001), NCT01868997
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group phase 2 and phase 3 trials of identical design; 1:1 randomization stratified by tobacco/smoking status; 8 IV infusions (10 mg/kg Day 1, then 20 mg/kg q3W) over a 24-week double-masked treatment period, in a rare-disease-scale population (N=87 Phase 2, N=83 Phase 3)

sponsor: Cassiopea SpA (c/o Ground Zero Pharmaceuticals, Inc.) — sponsor of record at approval; Sun Pharmaceutical acquired Cassiopea after this original 2020 approval and was not the sponsor of record at the time
design_text: two identically-designed, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group phase 3 trials; 1:1 randomization (no stratification factor beyond site); 708 and 732 subjects randomized respectively

randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, three-part phase 3 trial in a rare disease (type I/II HAE); 1:1:1 randomization to berotralstat 110 mg, 150 mg, or placebo QD, stratified by baseline attack rate (≥2 vs. <2 attacks/month); Part 1 = 24-week blinded RCT (primary efficacy), Part 2 = 24-week blinded safety extension, Part 3 = 48-week open-label safety

sponsor: Athenex (originator, sponsor of record in the FDA review); Almirall (subsequent commercial licensee, now listed as the ClinicalTrials.gov organization of record)
design_text: two identically-designed, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter phase 3 trials; 1:1 randomization stratified by treatment location (face vs. scalp) and site; 5 consecutive once-daily doses (first in-clinic, remaining 4 self-administered); 351 subjects randomized per trial

pivotal_trial: AURORA 1, NCT03021499; supported by Phase 2 AURA-LV, NCT02141672
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter (142 sites/27 countries), phase 3 trial; 1:1 randomization to voclosporin 23.7 mg BID or placebo, both arms on background mycophenolate mofetil plus a rapid oral corticosteroid taper, in biopsy-proven Class III, IV, or V lupus nephritis; single pivotal phase 3 trial accepted with a Phase 2 trial (AURA-LV) as confirmatory evidence

pivotal_trial: TULIP-2 (study 04), NCT02446899; TULIP-1 (study 05), NCT02446912, a first phase 3 trial that failed its pre-specified primary endpoint; Phase 2 study 1013 (CD-IA-MEDI-546-1013) as additional supportive evidence
design_text: two independent randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 3 trials plus a supportive phase 2 dose-ranging trial; TULIP-1 randomized 1:2:2 (placebo:150mg:300mg, N=457) and TULIP-2 randomized 1:1 (placebo:300mg, N=362), both stratified by screening SLEDAI-2K (<10 vs. ≥10), baseline OCS dose (<10 vs. ≥10 mg/day), and type I IFN gene-signature test result (high vs. low); mid-program primary-endpoint switch, made via a protocol/SAP amendment to the second (not-yet-unblinded) trial before its database lock

sponsor: ChemoCentryx (acquired by Amgen in 2022; NDA now held as "ChemoCentryx, Inc., a subsidiary of Amgen")
pivotal_trial: ADVOCATE (CL010_168), NCT02994927
design_text: single randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (prednisone taper), multicenter, phase 3 trial, complement C5a-receptor inhibitor added on to standard induction therapy (rituximab or cyclophosphamide/azathioprine); a genuinely contentious FDA Advisory Committee review with a dead-even efficacy vote

pivotal_trial: NAVIGATOR, NCT03347279; supported by Phase 2 PATHWAY; a third trial, SOURCE (steroid-sparing), failed its primary endpoint and was not part of the effectiveness basis
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, global phase 3 trial (297 sites/18 countries); enrollment deliberately not restricted by baseline eosinophil count, with enrollment quotas targeting similar proportions of <300 and ≥300 eosinophils/µL subjects, so the phenotype-agnostic efficacy claim was a planned analysis from the outset rather than a post hoc finding

pivotal_trial: ECZTRA 1, NCT03131648; ECZTRA 2, NCT03160885; ECZTRA 3, NCT03363854 (ECZTRA 1/2 are identically designed 52-week monotherapy trials; ECZTRA 3 is a 32-week trial of tralokinumab as add-on to topical corticosteroids; all three were co-pivotal for the BLA)
design_text: multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel-group phase 3, two identically-designed monotherapy trials plus one TCS-combination trial, ICH E9(R1) estimand framework, initial-treatment/re-randomized-maintenance design (ECZTRA 1/2), initial/continuation-treatment design (ECZTRA 3)

pivotal_trial: JADE MONO-1 (B7451012), NCT03349060; JADE MONO-2 (B7451013), NCT03575871; JADE COMPARE (B7451029), NCT03720470 (JADE MONO-1/2 are identically designed 12-week monotherapy trials in ages ≥12; JADE COMPARE is an adults-only trial adding placebo/dupilumab arms on background topical therapy)
design_text: multicenter randomized double-blind (double-dummy in JADE COMPARE) placebo-controlled parallel-group phase 3, two identically-designed monotherapy trials plus one active/placebo-controlled combination-therapy trial, adolescents included in monotherapy trials (age ≥12), external Data Monitoring Committee (E-DMC) for safety

pivotal_trial: PSOARING 1 (Protocol DMVT-505-3001), NCT03956355; PSOARING 2 (Protocol DMVT-505-3002), NCT03983980 — two identically designed replicate Phase 3 trials, per the FDA statistical review: "The Applicant conducted two identically designed Phase 3 trials"
design_text: replicate randomized double-blind vehicle-controlled trials, parallel-group, topical dermatology cream, stratified randomization

pivotal_trial: Effisayil 1 (BI Trial No. 1368-0013), NCT03782792 — "Effisayil™ 1: Multi-center, Double-blind, Randomised, Placebo-controlled, Phase II Study to Evaluate Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of a Single Intravenous Dose of Spesolimab (BI 655130) in Patients With Generalized Pustular Psoriasis (GPP) Presenting With an Acute Flare of Moderate to Severe Intensity"
design_text: small-N single-dose randomized placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial, rare-disease pivotal trial, single adequate and well-controlled trial supporting approval, orphan drug, breakthrough therapy

pivotal_trial: POETYK PSO-1 (Trial IM011046), NCT03624127; POETYK PSO-2 (Trial IM011047), NCT03611751
design_text: two identically-designed 52-week phase 3 RCTs, multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo- and active-comparator-controlled (apremilast), 2:1:1 randomization, stratified randomization, first-in-class allosteric TYK2 inhibitor, randomized withdrawal and re-treatment period (PSO-2 only), blinded switch of placebo arm at Week 16

pivotal_trial: Study CCDZ173X2201, Part 2 ("Study 2201, Part 2"), NCT02435173
design_text: ultra-rare-disease trial, single pivotal phase 2/3 study with an internal two-part structure (Part 1: open-label, non-randomized within-subject dose-finding, n=6; Part 2: the pivotal 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial, n=31), 2:1 randomization, first-in-class PI3Kδ inhibitor, approval based on a single adequate and well-controlled trial plus mechanistic confirmatory evidence (small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population, Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1)

pivotal_trial: ALLEGRO-2b/3 (Study B7981015), NCT03732807
design_text: randomized, double-blind, dose-ranging, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 2b/3 trial; seven parallel arms (five ritlecitinib dosing regimens plus two placebo-to-active switch arms) allocated 2:2:2:2:1:1:1; randomization stratified by age group (<18 vs. ≥18 years) and alopecia totalis/universalis (AT/AU) status; 24-week placebo-controlled period followed by a 24-week active-treatment extension

pivotal_trial: Three phase 3 trials supported the original efficacy demonstration — BE VIVID (PS0009), NCT03370133; BE READY (PS0013), NCT03410992; and BE SURE (PS0008), NCT03412747. Only BE VIVID and BE READY (both placebo-controlled) contributed the labeled placebo-controlled efficacy comparison; BE SURE (active-comparator-only, no placebo arm) is described in labeling's trial-design narrative but its head-to-head adalimumab data were not included in the approved label. BE RADIANT (PS0015), NCT03536884, an active-comparator (secukinumab) trial, was not part of the original efficacy package — it was submitted only as new safety data during the Complete-Response resubmission
design_text: three multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group phase 3 trials — BE VIVID (placebo- and ustekinumab-controlled), BE READY (placebo-controlled with randomized-withdrawal maintenance period), and BE SURE (adalimumab-controlled, no placebo arm) — randomization stratified by geographic region and prior biologic exposure; resubmission after a Complete Response Letter driven by manufacturing-facility (GMP) deficiencies unrelated to the efficacy/safety data package

sponsor: Amryt Pharmaceuticals DAC (c/o Amryt Pharmaceuticals Inc., Boston, MA) — this is the applicant named in both the December 18, 2023 approval letter and its February 26, 2024 "corrected" reissue (which fixed an "incorrect applicant name" error) and in the approved label's adverse-event contact information; Chiesi Farmaceutici S.p.A. acquired Amryt Pharma plc in September 2023, before approval, and FDA's live Drugs@FDA record for NDA 215064 currently lists the company of record as Chiesi, reflecting a subsequent administrative transfer of the application rather than the applicant named in the approval action itself
pivotal_trial: EASE (Study BEB-13), NCT03068780 — "Double-blind, Randomised, Vehicle-controlled, Phase III, Efficacy and Safety Study With 24-month Open-label Follow-up of Oleogel-S10 in Patients With Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa"
design_text: single pivotal Phase 3 randomized, triple-masked (participant/care provider/investigator), vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trial plus mechanistic confirmatory evidence from separate open-label intra-patient (split-wound) trials in non-EB partial-thickness wounds; rare-disease "one adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence" evidentiary pathway; adaptive group-sequential design with unblinded sample-size re-estimation

sponsor: LNHC, Inc. (c/o Therapeutics Inc., San Diego, CA) — this is the applicant named in FDA's January 5, 2024 approval letter; LNHC, Inc. is Novan, Inc.'s post-restructuring corporate successor. The approved label lists the manufacturing/distribution entity as EPIH SPV, LLC, Wilmington, Delaware
pivotal_trial: Two trials provided the substantial evidence of effectiveness — NI-MC304 ("B-SIMPLE4"), NCT04535531, and NI-MC302 ("B-SIMPLE2"), NCT03927703. A third, identically designed trial, NI-MC301 ("B-SIMPLE1"), NCT03927716, did not reach statistical significance on its primary endpoint and was used only as supportive/safety data
design_text: three co-designed, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials, with household-clustered randomization (1 or 2 randomized subjects per household, assigned the same treatment); NI-MC301/NI-MC302 randomized 2:1 (active:vehicle), NI-MC304 randomized 1:1 with an added baseline-inflammation stratification factor

sponsor: Hugel, Inc. (Chuncheon, Gangwon, Republic of Korea), U.S. License No. 2237; correspondence handled via Strategic Drug Development Services, LLC (Hillsborough, NC). Croma-Pharma GmbH (Austria) is listed as the ClinicalTrials.gov "lead sponsor" for all three pivotal trials — likely Hugel's ex-US development partner for these studies — but is not the BLA applicant of record.
pivotal_trial: Three identically-designed Phase 3 trials — BLESS I (NCT02677298), BLESS II (NCT02677805), and BLESS III (NCT03985982).
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trials, 3:1 active:placebo randomization, with an open-label extension permitting up to three retreatments (last retreatment ≤Week 48)

sponsor: Botanix SB Inc. (King of Prussia, PA); the drug was originally developed by Kaken Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Japan) — the FDA Multi-Discipline Review confirms a Kaken/Botanix development relationship but does not itself document the specific licensing chain (reported elsewhere as Kaken → Brickell Biotech → Botanix), so that chain is noted here as general industry background, not independently verified in FDA or ClinicalTrials.gov primary sources.
pivotal_trial: Cardigan I (protocol BBI-4000-CL-301, NCT03836287) and Cardigan II (protocol BBI-4000-CL-302, NCT03948646); a related long-term safety study, protocol BBI-4000-CL-303 (NCT03627468), was not part of the primary efficacy basis.
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trials, 1:1 randomization stratified by site, once-daily topical application to each axilla for 42 days; ages 9 and older eligible, though the ≥12-year instrument (HDSM-Ax-7 Adult) drove the primary analysis because only 5 subjects aged 9–<12 were enrolled/evaluable across both trials

sponsor: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Inc. Concert Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was the original sponsor for both pivotal trials and merged with Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Inc. on March 31, 2023, becoming the Applicant of record for this NDA.
pivotal_trial: THRIVE-AA1 (protocol CP543.3001, NCT04518995) and THRIVE-AA2 (protocol CP543.3002, NCT04797650).
design_text: Randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials; THRIVE-AA1 randomized 3:5:2 (12 mg:8 mg:placebo), THRIVE-AA2 randomized 1:2:1, stratified by baseline scalp hair loss category (partial, SALT 50–<95, vs. complete/near-complete, SALT ≥95); the 12 mg dose was placed on partial clinical hold May 17, 2023 for a potential dose-dependent thrombosis safety signal, and the approved NDA ultimately covers only the 8 mg twice-daily dose (partial clinical hold restricting an otherwise dual-dose NDA submission to its lower dose only); FDA rescinded the drug's Breakthrough Therapy Designation in a two-step process (Intent to Rescind, September 21, 2023; final rescission, March 14, 2024) after two competing JAK inhibitors (baricitinib, ritlecitinib) were approved for the same indication and removed the "substantial improvement over available therapy" basis for the designation (Breakthrough Therapy Designation rescinded due to intervening competitor approvals)

pivotal_trial: ARCADIA 1 (NCT03985943) and ARCADIA 2 (NCT03989349).
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trials with background topical corticosteroid and/or calcineurin-inhibitor therapy in both arms, approximately 2:1 randomization (1,728 subjects total across both trials, ages ≥12); a responder re-randomization at Week 16 (nemolizumab every 4 weeks, nemolizumab every 8 weeks, or placebo every 4 weeks) extended the controlled comparison through Week 48

sponsor: Eli Lilly and Company (the three pivotal trials were originally sponsored by Dermira, Inc., which Lilly acquired in January 2020; ClinicalTrials.gov records still carry Dermira protocol numbers DRM06-AD04/-AD05/-AD06 alongside Lilly's J2T-DM-KGAB/-KGAC/-KGAD numbering).
pivotal_trial: ADvocate1 (Study J2T-DM-KGAB / DRM06-AD04, NCT04146363) and ADvocate2 (Study J2T-DM-KGAC / DRM06-AD05, NCT04178967) — identically designed 16-week monotherapy trials with a Week-16-to-52 randomized-withdrawal maintenance period; ADhere (Study J2T-DM-KGAD / DRM06-AD06, NCT04250337) — a 16-week trial of lebrikizumab added to background topical corticosteroids (TCS).
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trials; ADvocate1 (N=424) and ADvocate2 (N=445) randomized 2:1 (lebrikizumab:placebo) as monotherapy through Week 16, with Week-16 responders (IGA 0/1 or EASI-75) re-randomized to lebrikizumab Q2W, lebrikizumab Q4W, or placebo through Week 52; ADhere (N=228) randomized 2:1 with background TCS in both arms through Week 16 only; randomization stratified by geographic region (US vs. EU vs. rest of world), age (adolescent 12–<18 years vs. adult ≥18 years), and baseline disease severity (IGA 3 vs. 4) in all three trials; a Good Clinical Practice misconduct finding at a site shared by ADvocate2 and ADhere (same investigator, "implausible homogeneity" of IGA scores) led to a mid-conduct SAP amendment defining a modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population, excluding 18 subjects from ADvocate2 and 17 from ADhere, as the primary efficacy population for those two trials

pivotal_trial: VANGUARD (protocol CSL312_3001, NCT04656418).
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm trial, 3:2 active:placebo randomization, with a prospective 1-2-month Run-in Period (no prophylaxis permitted) used to confirm disease activity and establish each subject's baseline HAE attack rate before randomization into a 6-month double-blind Treatment Period; randomization required experiencing ≥2 attacks during the Run-in Period (a prospective observation/run-in period establishing a within-subject baseline attack rate as an eligibility gate for randomization, distinct from any run-in design already catalogued, and directly comparable to the run-in design used in donidalorsen/Dawnzera's OASIS-HAE trial below)

pivotal_trial: KONFIDENT (protocol KVD900-301, NCT05259917); a long-term open-label extension, KONFIDENT-S (protocol KVD900-302, NCT05505916), provided supportive safety data.
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-treatment, three-period complete crossover trial — each of 136 enrolled patients was randomized to a sequence covering all three treatments (placebo, 300 mg, 600 mg sebetralstat), treating one qualifying HAE attack per period (a complete crossover design for an acute/episodic on-demand indication, in which each patient treats multiple independent qualifying attacks under a randomized treatment sequence, rather than the parallel-group or simple two-period crossover designs already catalogued)

sponsor: LEO Pharma A/S (c/o LEO Pharma Inc., Madison, NJ).
pivotal_trial: DELTA 1 (protocol LP0133-1401, NCT04871711) and DELTA 2 (protocol LP0133-1402, NCT04872101) — not "DELTA FORCE," despite that name appearing in some secondary sources; a long-term extension, DELTA 3 (NCT04949841), followed completers of DELTA 1/2.
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trials, 2:1 randomization (delgocitinib cream 20 mg/g : cream vehicle), stratified by region (Europe/North America) and baseline Investigator's Global Assessment for Chronic Hand Eczema (IGA-CHE) score (3 or 4), ~55 sites across Europe and Canada, 16-week treatment period; eligibility required IGA-CHE 3 or 4 and a Hand Eczema Symptom Diary (HESD) itch score ≥4, not the Hand Eczema Severity Index (HECSI) as sometimes assumed — HECSI is a secondary endpoint only, not an eligibility criterion

pivotal_trial: OASIS-HAE (NCT05139810); a related open-label extension, OASISplus (NCT05392114), provided long-term safety/immunogenicity follow-up.
design_text: Randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel trial with a prospective 8-week Run-in/screening period requiring ≥2 investigator-confirmed HAE attacks for eligibility (the same run-in-to-establish-baseline-attack-rate design used in garadacimab/Andembry's VANGUARD trial above); 2:1 randomization overall between two dosing-regimen cohorts (80 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks, n=45; every 8 weeks, n=23) and a pooled placebo group (n=22)

pivotal_trial: REMIX-1 (protocol CLOU064A2301, NCT05030311) and REMIX-2 (protocol CLOU064A2302, NCT05032157).
design_text: Two identical, randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 52-week trials (24-week double-blind placebo-controlled period followed by 28-week open-label extension), 2:1 randomization (remibrutinib 25 mg twice daily : placebo); 925 total randomized (REMIX-1 n=462, REMIX-2 n=450), with 912 in the efficacy analysis from the 24-week controlled period; eligibility required CSU ≥6 months, UAS7 ≥16, ISS7 ≥6, and HSS7 ≥6 in the 7 days before randomization

pivotal_trial: Trial 271-102-00007 (NCT03908970, adult/adolescent, Japan) and Trial 271-102-00008 (NCT03911401, pediatric ages 2–14, Japan) — both conducted in Japan, not the United States; a US-based trial, MEDI-MM36-301, was terminated early "for business reasons" after enrolling 153 of 336 planned subjects and was explicitly excluded from the efficacy analysis.
design_text: Approval based on foreign (Japanese) pivotal Phase 3 trials with a concurrently-run, terminated, and excluded US trial (a hybrid approval strategy relying on non-US pivotal data plus an explicit generalizability/bridging argument, where a domestic trial exists but was terminated and excluded from the efficacy claim rather than analyzed, is distinct from a straightforward foreign-data bridging study or a standard multi-region trial); both Japanese pivotal trials were randomized, triple-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group

pivotal_trial: Four Phase 3 trials formed the efficacy basis: ICONIC-LEAD (Protocol 77242113PSO3001, NCT06095115), ICONIC-ADVANCE 1 (Protocol 77242113PSO3002, NCT06143878), ICONIC-ADVANCE 2 (Protocol 77242113PSO3004, NCT06220604), and ICONIC-TOTAL (Protocol 77242113PSO3003, NCT06095102)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (ICONIC-LEAD, ICONIC-TOTAL); randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator-controlled versus deucravacitinib (ICONIC-ADVANCE 1, ICONIC-ADVANCE 2); approval basis built from four independently protocoled, differently-enrolled Phase 3 trials analyzed and reported as a single coordinated evidentiary package rather than pooled into one dataset (closest existing taxonomy analogue is "Cross-trial pooled/integrated analysis," but here each trial retains its own separate primary analysis rather than being statistically pooled: a "multi-trial coordinated-SAP approval basis, each trial independently analyzed"); embedded randomized-withdrawal-and-retreatment sub-design within ICONIC-LEAD from Week 24 through Week 52, with retreatment triggered by a pre-specified ≥50% loss of Week-24 PASI improvement (not the same construct as "Early-stopped for efficacy"); novel mechanistic class — icotrokinra is an oral 13-amino-acid peptide IL-23 receptor antagonist, the first oral therapy in the IL-23 inhibitor class (prior approved IL-23 inhibitors — guselkumab, risankizumab, tildrakizumab, and the related IL-12/23 inhibitor ustekinumab — are all injectable monoclonal antibodies)

sponsor: Priovant Therapeutics, Inc. (a Roivant Sciences company)
pivotal_trial: VALOR (Protocol PVT-2201-301), NCT05437263 — Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of oral brepocitinib in adults with dermatomyositis
control: Placebo; Dose comparison; Standard of care; None
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm dose-comparison trial (two active dose levels of the same drug versus a shared placebo arm — distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design," which describes randomization across regimens of the same drug without a placebo arm); 52-week double-blind primary treatment period with background standard-of-care therapy (corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine, and/or a non-steroid immunosuppressant) continued at stable dose and glucocorticoids tapered per protocol, followed by an optional 52-week open-label extension; ultra-rare autoimmune disease population (dermatomyositis prevalence on the order of 1 in 20,000-25,000); first-in-class oral TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor mechanism in this indication

pivotal_trial: SPN-301-07 (NCT00545753) and SPN-302-07 (NCT00545168), two identically protocoled Phase 3 trials; supportive Phase 2 dose-ranging trial SPN-202-06 (NCT00311779)
design_text: randomized, evaluator/investigator-blinded (intended double-blind, but compromised by product-identifiable packaging — see Missing data/bias), active-controlled, three-arm household/cluster-unit randomization stratified by study site, allocation ratio 4:4:1 (NatrOVA without nit combing : NIX with nit combing : NatrOVA with nit combing) (household/cluster-unit randomization with a designated "primary subject" per household); supportive Phase 2 dose-ranging, vehicle(placebo)-controlled trial (SPN-202-06) used only to assess the topical vehicle's own contribution to efficacy, not as a pivotal study in its own right

pivotal_trial: Study 310123 (NCT00709852) and Study 310124 (no registered NCT identified), two Phase 3 within-patient paired-comparison diagnostic-accuracy trials

sponsor: Wyeth Pharmaceuticals Inc. (a wholly owned subsidiary of Pfizer Inc.)

control: Placebo; Active; Dose comparison; Reference standard; None

pivotal_trial: POL-Xe-001, NCT03417687 (lung resection population), and POL-Xe-002, NCT03418090 (lung transplant population)
design_text: two randomized, open-label, crossover, multicenter phase 3 studies, each comparing hyperpolarized Xe-129 MRI against the FDA-approved reference standard, Xe-133 radionuclide ventilation scintigraphy, in a within-patient paired design — Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison); every patient received both imaging modalities in a randomized order (Xe-129-then-Xe-133 or the reverse); POL-Xe-001 (n=34 dosed, 3 US centers) enrolled patients being evaluated for possible lung resection surgery (segmentectomy, lobectomy, pneumonectomy); POL-Xe-002 (n=49 dosed, 2 US centers) enrolled patients being evaluated for lung transplant surgery

randomized, three-arm (NexoBrid gel : standard-of-care (SOC) : vehicle gel, 3:3:1), multicenter, multinational, assessor-blinded phase 3 trial in adults with thermal burns ≤30% total body surface area (TBSA); blinding was partial by necessity — treating investigators were unblinded (NexoBrid gel is gold-colored, vehicle is clear) but a dedicated assessor blinded to treatment (NexoBrid vs. vehicle) evaluated eschar removal, and a second assessor blinded to all arms conducted weekly wound-closure and long-term cosmesis/function evaluations; conducted under three successive protocol amendments (Amendments 8, 9, 11) that changed the maximum enrollable %TBSA (15%→30%), the randomization method (minimization→block randomization), and the stratification factors

sponsor: Verona Pharma, Inc. (acquired by Merck & Co./MSD in a deal that closed shortly after this approval)
pivotal_trial: ENHANCE-1, NCT04535986, and ENHANCE-2, NCT04542057
design_text: two replicate randomized, quadruple-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter phase 3 trials (250 sites, 17 countries), 24 weeks; nebulized ensifentrine 3 mg twice daily vs. placebo; ENHANCE-1 N=760 randomized/treated, ENHANCE-2 N=789; population aged 40-80y, ≥10 pack-year smoking history, moderate-to-severe symptomatic COPD (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC<0.70, FEV1 30-70% predicted); stratified by region, background LAMA/LABA maintenance-therapy strata (capped so no more than ~50-70% of enrollment was on background triple/dual therapy), and smoking strata

sponsor: Bracco Diagnostics Inc. — approved as two co-filed 505(b)(2) NDAs (216016 and 216017), reflecting different concentrations/routes of the same active ingredient
pivotal_trial: No single dedicated pivotal RCT; approval rests on a legacy multi-study evidentiary package (no unifying ClinicalTrials.gov registration/NCT number identified for a single US registration trial)
design_text: diagnostic-accuracy study package (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison against a reference standard, and independent multi-reader blinded-read studies), reusing the taxonomy's existing "Diagnostic-accuracy study" and "Retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis" categories — intra-arterial indications supported by three blinded-read study programs, each itself comprising 2-4 prospective, randomized, double-blind, multicenter sub-studies (cerebral arteriography N=61; visceral/peripheral arteriography N=60; coronary arteriography/ventriculography N=59 and N=59 across two concentrations); intravenous indications supported by separate blinded-read CT head/body studies (N=59 and N=59), prospective CT-angiography studies against digital subtraction angiography as reference standard (2 studies, N=262), coronary CTA studies against invasive coronary angiography (2 studies, N=301), and two retrospective single-center CT-urography visualization-quality studies (N=185, no reference-standard comparator)

pivotal_trial: Bunionectomy trial (Protocol VX22-548-104), NCT05553366, and Abdominoplasty trial, NCT05558410
design_text: two phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo- and active-controlled trials in acute postsurgical pain; bunionectomy trial N=1,073 (2:2:1 to suzetrigine/hydrocodone bitartrate-acetaminophen [HB-APAP]/placebo) following unilateral bunionectomy with Austin osteotomy under regional block; abdominoplasty trial N=1,118, same 2:2:1 design and dosing; randomization triggered post-block-removal when the subject requested analgesia with moderate-or-severe pain (verbal rating scale) and a numeric pain rating scale (NPRS) score ≥4 within a 9-hour eligibility window; stratified by site and baseline NPRS (<8 vs. ≥8)

pivotal_trial: ASPEN (Insmed Study INS1007-301), NCT04594369
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1:1, phase 3 trial in adults and adolescents (≥12y) with NCFB; arms brensocatib 10 mg once daily, 25 mg once daily, placebo; N randomized=1,767 (ITT population 1,721, after excluding 44 subjects in Ukraine for war-related reasons and 2 subjects at one US site for GCP noncompliance); 52-week treatment duration; stratified by sputum *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* status, prior pulmonary-exacerbation count (<3 vs. ≥3), region (North America/Europe/Japan/rest-of-world), and age group

pivotal_trial: FIBRONEER-IPF (Boehringer Study 1305-0014), NCT05321069
design_text: randomized 1:1:1, quadruple-blind (participant/care provider/investigator/outcomes assessor), placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in adults ≥40y with IPF (2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT diagnostic criteria), FVC≥45% predicted, DLCO≥25% predicted, with or without background antifibrotic therapy (nintedanib or pirfenidone); arms nerandomilast 9 mg twice daily, 18 mg twice daily, placebo; 1,177 randomized (392/392/393); stratified by background antifibrotic-therapy use; two-part design (Part A, ≥52 weeks, primary analysis at Database Lock 1; Part B, variable-duration blinded extension, primarily safety-focused, Database Lock 2 approximately 4 months later)

pivotal_trial: SWIFT-1 (GSK Study 206713), NCT04719832, and SWIFT-2 (GSK Study 213744), NCT04718103
design_text: two independent randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials in adults and adolescents (≥12y) with severe eosinophilic asthma on medium-or-high-dose inhaled corticosteroids plus another controller; depemokimab-ulaa 100 mg subcutaneously once every 6 months vs. placebo; SWIFT-1 N=250/132 (depemokimab/placebo), SWIFT-2 N=252/128 (2:1 allocation); 52-week duration; stratified/adjusted for exacerbation history (2, 3, ≥4 in the prior year), baseline ICS dose (medium/high), region (Europe/US/rest-of-world), and baseline pre-bronchodilator percent-predicted FEV1

sponsor: Vanda Pharmaceuticals Inc. (compound originally developed by Eli Lilly as LY686017; IND 141315)
pivotal_trial: Study 3401 "Motion Syros," NCT04327661, and Study 3404 "Motion Serifos," NCT05903924
design_text: two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1:1 phase 3 trials; single oral dose of tradipitant 85 mg, 170 mg, or placebo given approximately 60 minutes before a boat-trip motion-sickness travel challenge (120-300 minutes); randomization stratified by pooled site/port; Study 3401 N=365 (123/120/122 across 170 mg/85 mg/placebo, approximately), Study 3404 N=316 (104/106/106)

sponsor: Haisco-USA Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Bridgewater, NJ; a US subsidiary of Haisco Pharmaceutical Group). The compound (code HSK3486) is separately marketed in China as "ciprofol"; the extensive Chinese ciprofol literature reflects a different regulatory record and is not cited here as part of the US pivotal evidentiary basis
design_text: three randomized, double-blind, propofol-active-controlled phase 3 trials, allocation ratio 2:1 (cipepofol:propofol), stratified by ASA physical-status class, age, and BMI; HSK3486-304 N=255 (US/EU), HSK3486-305 N=400, HSK3486-309 N=465 (a broader multiregional trial including US, Poland, and Spain sites); combined primary pivotal-trial enrollment >1,100, within a total controlled-trial safety database of 1,329 subjects across 9 trials (723 in the three pivotal trials)

pivotal_trial: QUANTI CNS (Study 21181), NCT05915702, and QUANTI OBR ("other body region," Study 21197), NCT05915728 (supported by a pediatric PK/safety bridging study, QUANTI Pediatric/Study 21196, NCT05915026)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, crossover diagnostic-accuracy trials — every subject received both gadoquatrane and an approved macrocyclic comparator GBCA (gadobutrol-class) in randomized order, with independent reads by 3 blinded central readers plus a 4th reader performing lesion-matching and a ~10% intra-reader-variability re-read subsample; QUANTI CNS enrolled/screened 321 subjects at 71 centers in 15 countries, randomized 305 (151/154 by administration order), safety population 303, primary Full Analysis Set (≥1 matched lesion) 237; QUANTI OBR primary analysis population 312 (from an overall enrollment of 410)

sponsor: ApoPharma, Inc. (Cato Research Ltd. acted as U.S. agent on the NDA)
pivotal_trial: Study LA36-0310 — a retrospective, non-randomized, pooled patient-level reanalysis of pre-existing data from 12 of 17 previously conducted ApoPharma studies (no new patients or new data collection; no NCT number, as none of the underlying studies were registered/conducted under a US IND); supportive randomized trial LA16-0102 (no NCT number; predates ClinicalTrials.gov registration norms), published as Pennell et al., *Blood* 2006
design_text: accelerated-approval resubmission (21 CFR 314.500) following a 2009 Complete Response Letter that rejected the sponsor's original single randomized controlled trial (LA16-0102, cardiac MRI T2* endpoint) because FDA considered that endpoint an unvalidated surrogate for clinical utility; post-hoc pooled reanalysis of patient-level data from multiple previously completed, independently conducted single-arm and randomized studies, with patient eligibility for the pooled analysis determined by an Independent Committee applying pre-agreed inclusion/exclusion criteria rather than by prospective trial enrollment (closest existing taxonomy entries, "Post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts into one primary analysis population" and "Retrospective/non-prospective diagnostic evidentiary basis," each describe an adjacent but distinct scenario); supportive randomized, open-label, active (deferoxamine)-controlled trial (LA16-0102, 1:1 randomization) conducted outside a US IND with no FDA input on design

sponsor: Affymax, Inc. (co-developed and commercialized in the US under a collaboration with Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited/Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc., which became sole NDA holder after Affymax exited the partnership in 2013)
pivotal_trial: EMERALD 1 (Study AFX01-12, NCT00597753) and EMERALD 2 (Study AFX01-14, NCT00597584) — two identically designed Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active (epoetin alfa)-controlled non-inferiority trials in hemodialysis patients; companion PEARL 1 (Study AFX01-11, NCT00598273) and PEARL 2 (Study AFX01-13, NCT00598442) trials in non-dialysis CKD patients were conducted and reviewed for safety, but the sponsor did not seek that indication after PEARL showed a numerically worse cardiovascular composite safety signal for peginesatide vs. darbepoetin alfa
design_text: two identically protocoled randomized, open-label, active-controlled non-inferiority trials (EMERALD 1/2) in dialysis patients, 2:1 randomization (peginesatide:epoetin alfa), stratified by mean screening hemoglobin (≤11.4 vs. ≥11.5 g/dL) and NYHA heart-failure class; four-period design (≤6-week screening, 28-week titration, 8-week evaluation, long-term-safety-and-efficacy follow-up to week 52+); companion randomized, open-label, active (darbepoetin alfa)-controlled non-inferiority trials in non-dialysis CKD patients (PEARL 1/2), conducted under the same program but reviewed for safety only, since the sponsor never pursued that indication; prespecified cross-trial pooled cardiovascular composite-safety-endpoint (CSE) analysis spanning all four Phase 3 trials (dialysis + non-dialysis), independently adjudicated by a blinded Event Review Committee ("Prespecified cross-trial pooled composite cardiovascular safety-endpoint analysis, independently adjudicated, run alongside separately-populated non-inferiority efficacy trials")

sponsor: Gentium S.r.L. (an Italian biotech acquired by Jazz Pharmaceuticals in 2014; Jazz Pharmaceuticals, Inc. served as U.S. agent/co-applicant on the NDA)
pivotal_trial: Study 2005-01 (NCT00358501) — a multicenter, open-label, non-randomized historical-control study comparing a prospectively enrolled defibrotide-treated cohort (n=102) against a retrospectively assembled historical-control cohort (n=32) drawn from 6,867 HSCT recipients at 35 centers; supported by Study 99-118, a randomized, open-label, dose-finding Phase 2 trial (n=150, two defibrotide dose arms, no control arm) and Study 2006-05, an ongoing US expanded-access/Treatment IND protocol
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Single-arm; External/historical control; Dose-ranging
design_text: multicenter, open-label, historical-control (non-randomized) trial as the pivotal efficacy study, with propensity-score stratified weighting (quintile/quartile) used to adjust for four pre-specified baseline prognostic covariates (ventilator/dialysis dependence, age ≤16, allogeneic vs. autologous transplant, prior stem cell transplant) — an unusually scrutinized use of a historical-control design for a pivotal registration trial, where the historical-control cohort was itself re-selected twice (86→32 patients) after a Data Safety Monitoring Board reviewed unblinded interim efficacy results and found the initial control cohort's response/survival rates "unexpected" (a historical-control cohort re-selected mid-study after an unblinded interim look, not currently in Keyword_Taxonomy.md); supportive randomized (1:1), open-label, dose-finding Phase 2 trial (Study 99-118) comparing two defibrotide dose levels with no untreated/placebo arm; supportive single-arm expanded-access/Treatment IND cohort (Study 2006-05) and a compassionate-use program dataset (Study DF-CUP) running since 1997

sponsor: Genentech, Inc. (a member of the Roche Group; molecule originated by Chugai Pharmaceutical)
pivotal_trial: HAVEN 1 (Study BH29884, NCT02622321), a randomized, open-label, Phase III trial in adults/adolescents (≥12 years) with hemophilia A and FVIII inhibitors, with supportive single-arm evidence from HAVEN 2 (Study BH29992, pediatric <12 years, interim analysis)
design_text: randomized, open-label, multi-arm trial combining a randomized concurrent comparison (Arm A: emicizumab prophylaxis, N=35; Arm B: no prophylaxis/continued episodic bypassing-agent treatment, N=18, 2:1 allocation) with two non-randomized arms (Arm C: emicizumab prophylaxis in patients previously on bypassing-agent prophylaxis, N=49; Arm D: patients from the sponsor's non-interventional study unable to enroll in Arms A/B/C before closure, N=7); intra-patient (within-subject) comparison against each patient's own prospectively collected bleed-rate data from a separate non-interventional study (NIS BH29768) conducted before trial enrollment, layered onto the concurrent randomized comparison as pre-specified secondary endpoints rather than as the primary evidentiary basis (adapted from Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1 "Retrospective natural-history/genotype-matched external-control comparison" — but here the comparator is each subject's own prior bleed history, not a separate matched cohort; **intra-patient historical bleed-rate comparison layered onto a concurrent randomized arm, analyzed via a repeated-measures negative-binomial model**); supportive single-arm trial (HAVEN 2) in a pediatric population where randomization was not conducted; small trial in a rare inherited bleeding disorder population with FVIII inhibitors (a subset of an already-rare disease)

pivotal_trial: Two identically designed Phase III trials, Study C788-047 (FIT1, NCT02076412) and Study C788-048 (FIT2, NCT02076399), both randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
design_text: two identically designed, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase III trials (2:1 fostamatinib:placebo allocation) in adults with persistent/chronic ITP refractory to at least one prior ITP therapy; supportive long-term open-label extension trial (Study C788-049)

sponsor: Dova Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NDA held through subsidiary AkaRx, Inc.)
pivotal_trial: Two identically designed Phase III trials, ADAPT-1 (Study E5501-G000-310, NCT01972529) and ADAPT-2 (Study E5501-G000-311, NCT01976104), both randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
design_text: two identically designed, randomized (2:1 avatrombopag:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase III trials, each further divided into two dose/baseline-severity cohorts (Low Baseline Platelet Count Cohort, <40,000/mcL, treated with 60 mg once daily; High Baseline Platelet Count Cohort, 40,000-<50,000/mcL, treated with 40 mg once daily) with randomization stratified by hepatocellular carcinoma status (safety stratification only) and procedure-related bleeding risk (low/moderate/high, efficacy stratification); mid-trial sample-size reduction from a planned 300 to 200 patients per trial via protocol amendment

pivotal_trial: L-PLUS 2 (Study 1423M0634, NCT02389621), a multinational phase 3 trial; supported by pivotal trial L-PLUS 1 (Study 1304M0631), a Japan-only phase 3 trial with no ClinicalTrials.gov registration identified
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; two near-identical phase 3 trials in the same drug-development program, one conducted only in Japan (L-PLUS 1) and one multinational (L-PLUS 2); randomization stratified by planned invasive-procedure type (liver ablation/coagulation vs. other) and baseline/screening platelet count threshold

pivotal_trial: Study ALXN1210-PNH-301 (NCT02946463, complement-inhibitor-naive population) and Study ALXN1210-PNH-302 (NCT03056040, eculizumab-to-ravulizumab switch population)
design_text: randomized, open-label, active-controlled, non-inferiority design against eculizumab, run as two phase 3 trials in complementary populations — treatment-naive (Study 301) and clinically stable patients switching from chronic eculizumab therapy (Study 302); randomization stratified by transfusion history and screening LDH level (Study 301); single-pivotal-trial-plus-switch-trial program agreed with FDA at an End-of-Phase-2 meeting

pivotal_trial: HERCULES (Study ALX0681-C301, NCT02553317); supportive phase 2 trial TITAN (NCT01151423)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial with background standard-of-care add-on design (both arms received plasma exchange and immunosuppressive therapy); randomization stratified by neurological-involvement severity (Glasgow Coma Scale ≤12 vs. 13-15); preceded by a positive randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial (TITAN) in the same indication, add-on to plasma exchange

pivotal_trial: Two identically protocoled phase 3 trials, AEGIS 1 (Study ST10-01-301, NCT01340872, quiescent ulcerative colitis) and AEGIS 2 (Study ST10-01-302, NCT01352221, quiescent Crohn's disease), pooled for efficacy review; supported by a third pivotal phase 3 trial, Study ST10-01-303 (NCT02968368), in non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease (CKD)
design_text: three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 3 trials across two distinct IDA-etiology populations (inflammatory bowel disease and chronic kidney disease); AEGIS 1/AEGIS 2 were identically protocoled and pooled for the efficacy and safety review; all three double-blind phases were followed by a single-arm open-label extension in which placebo subjects crossed over to ferric maltol

sponsor: Impact Biomedicines, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Celgene Corporation (the original molecule, then SAR302503/TG101348, was developed by TargeGen and then Sanofi/Genzyme, which terminated the program in 2013; Impact Biomedicines acquired global rights in 2016 and Celgene acquired Impact Biomedicines in 2018, before the 2019 NDA approval; Celgene was itself acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb in November 2019, three months after this approval)
pivotal_trial: JAKARTA (Study EFC12153), NCT01437787; supported by the single-arm JAKARTA2 (Study ARD12181), a Phase 2 study in patients previously exposed to ruxolitinib
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1; JAKARTA was a 3-arm trial randomizing 1:1:1 to fedratinib 400 mg, fedratinib 500 mg, or placebo, with placebo patients permitted to cross over to either active-dose arm after completing 6 cycles or upon protocol-defined progression); single-arm, open-label trial (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1; JAKARTA2, in ruxolitinib-pretreated patients); program-terminating full clinical hold followed by change of sponsor and a later stand-alone NDA built on the pre-hold pivotal-trial data (the entire fedratinib clinical development program, including an ongoing JAKARTA, was placed on full clinical hold by FDA on November 15, 2013 for reports of Wernicke's encephalopathy and heart failure; Sanofi terminated development three days later and permanently discontinued all patients worldwide from study drug; the hold was not lifted until August 2017, after which Impact Biomedicines/Celgene resubmitted the same pre-hold trial data, plus new safety analyses and a thiamine-supplementation follow-up period, in a 2019 NDA)

sponsor: Clinuvel Inc. (US subsidiary of Clinuvel Pharmaceuticals Limited, Australia)
pivotal_trial: Study CUV039, NCT01605136 (randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, the sole trial FDA designated adequate and well-controlled); supported by Study CUV029, NCT00979745, and Study CUV030, NCT01097044, both earlier vehicle-controlled trials of nearly identical design
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1; CUV039, vehicle rather than inert-placebo-implant control, randomized 1:1 within center using blocks of size 4); small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1; CUV039 randomized only 94 subjects, and 26 subjects randomized to vehicle in the earlier failed CUV030 were permitted to re-enroll and be randomized again in CUV039); approval program with a substantial proportion of negative/failed pivotal trials (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1 — the first two prospectively designed primary endpoints, based on severity of phototoxic reactions, failed in both CUV029 and CUV030, leading the sponsor to redesign the endpoint entirely for CUV039 around pain-free sun-exposure hours); sponsor-identified post-submission data-transcription error that reversed the primary endpoint's statistical significance (a treatment-allocation coding error for 2 subjects, discovered by the sponsor during EMA GCP-inspection preparation, changed the primary analysis p-value from 0.107 (not significant) in the original 2013 study report to 0.044 (significant) in a corrected 2014 version)

sponsor: Celgene Corporation (acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb in a deal that closed November 20, 2019, 12 days after the original approval)
pivotal_trial: BELIEVE (ACE-536-B-THAL-001), NCT02604433, for the original beta-thalassemia indication; MEDALIST (ACE-536-MDS-001), NCT02631070, for the supplemental MDS-RS indication
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) for both BELIEVE (2:1 randomization, stratified by geographic region) and MEDALIST (2:1 randomization, stratified by baseline RBC transfusion burden [≥6 vs. <6 units/8 weeks] and IPSS-R risk category); event-driven fixed-interval responder-rate design in both trials (efficacy is assessed as a binary transfusion-burden-reduction or transfusion-independence responder rate over a fixed on-study window, rather than a continuous or time-to-event primary endpoint); reviewer-flagged blinding-integrity limitation in MEDALIST (the sponsor did not supply a matching placebo, sourcing it locally by site instead, and the investigational product's "clear to slightly opalescent" appearance meant it "could be differentiated from the placebo visually," with masking procedures otherwise undefined)

pivotal_trial: SUSTAIN (Study A2201), NCT01895361 — described throughout FDA's review as a Phase 2, not Phase 3, trial, despite serving as the sole basis for a full BLA approval; the post-marketing confirmatory trial STAND (Study A2301), NCT03814746, later returned a negative result (see below)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1; SUSTAIN randomized 1:1:1 to crizanlizumab 5.0 mg/kg, 2.5 mg/kg, or placebo over 52 weeks, stratified by hydroxyurea use and VOC-history category); regular approval based on a single, explicitly Phase 2, randomized trial (FDA's own review repeatedly labels SUSTAIN "a phase 2, double blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study" and states substantial evidence of effectiveness rested on results from that single trial, with no second confirmatory trial available at the time of approval); mid-trial SAP amendment correcting an inadvertent statistical-method omission (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, adapted — 2016 Amendment 4 added the previously-omitted randomization strata to the primary-endpoint analysis, which FDA's review states "do[es] not appear to have had an impact on the integrity of the trial or interpretation of the results")

pivotal_trial: ENVISION (Study ALN-AS1-003), NCT03338816 (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1), enrolling across acute hepatic porphyria (AHP) broadly (94 patients) with a pre-specified primary analysis restricted to the acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) subtype (89 patients) — a disease-subtype-restricted primary analysis population nested within a broader trial-eligible population, distinct from the taxonomy's existing biomarker-cohort entries in that AHP/AIP is a clinical diagnostic subtyping rather than a molecular biomarker split ("primary analysis restricted to a clinical disease-subtype subgroup within a broader trial-eligible population"); randomization stratified by baseline hemin-prophylaxis use and a historical annualized attack rate (AAR) threshold that itself varied depending on hemin-prophylaxis status (two different AAR cutoffs, <7/≥7 for hemin-prophylaxis patients and <12/≥12 for non-prophylaxis patients)

sponsor: Global Blood Therapeutics, Inc. (acquired by Pfizer, Inc., October 5, 2022)
pivotal_trial: HOPE (Study GBT440-031), NCT03036813 — a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1; HOPE randomized 274 patients 1:1:1 to voxelotor 1,500 mg, voxelotor 900 mg, or placebo, stratified by hydroxyurea use, geographic region, and age group [12-<18 vs. 18-65]); accelerated approval on a surrogate hematologic endpoint later followed by voluntary worldwide market withdrawal after a post-marketing safety signal (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §7, "Voluntary withdrawal of an accelerated-approval indication after confirmatory-trial failure," adapted — here the withdrawal was driven not by confirmatory-trial failure to show benefit but by an emerging excess-mortality/VOC signal across the confirmatory pediatric trial, a separate leg-ulcer trial, and two post-marketing real-world registries)

pivotal_trial: APL2-302 / PEGASUS, NCT03500549 (randomized, open-label, active-comparator [eculizumab])
design_text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) in an eculizumab-switch/add-on population — all subjects first completed a 4-week run-in receiving pegcetacoplan on top of their existing eculizumab, then were randomized 1:1 to switch fully to pegcetacoplan monotherapy or remain on eculizumab monotherapy for a 16-week randomized comparison period (RCP), followed by a 32-week open-label period in which all patients (including former eculizumab-arm patients) received pegcetacoplan (a randomized run-in-then-switch design against an active comparator, distinct from any existing taxonomy design entry); small trial in a rare-disease population (80 randomized: 41 pegcetacoplan, 39 eculizumab)

sponsor: Kadmon Pharmaceuticals, LLC (a Kadmon Holdings company; Sanofi announced its acquisition of Kadmon Holdings on September 8, 2021 for approximately $1.9 billion, roughly seven weeks after this approval, with the deal closing later that year — Kadmon was the sponsor of record at approval)
pivotal_trial: ROCKstar (Study KD025-213), NCT03640481 (randomized, open-label, two-dose-arm, single-arm-per-dose comparison against a fixed performance goal); supported by KD025-208 (dose-escalation trial)
design_text: Randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1 — matches the existing Brigatinib/ALTA entry's structure: randomization used only to allocate patients across two dosing regimens of the same drug, each analyzed independently against a fixed performance goal rather than compared to the other arm); single-arm, open-label trial (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) at the level of each dose arm's efficacy analysis; small trial in a treatment-refractory rare-disease population (132 randomized, 65-66 per arm, all having failed 2-5 prior lines of systemic cGVHD therapy)

pivotal_trial: This entry documents an unusual, three-study evidentiary structure — the trial FDA ultimately designated as the "adequate and well-controlled" (AWC) study supporting approval was PEGINVERA, NCT01193699 (open-label, single-arm, dose-escalation, historically/externally controlled, N=51), NOT the larger randomized Phase 3 trial. That randomized trial, PROUD-PV, NCT01949805 (randomized, open-label, active-controlled versus hydroxyurea), explicitly failed its primary non-inferiority endpoint per FDA's own statistical review, and — together with its non-randomized open-label extension, CONTINUATION-PV, NCT02218047 — was instead treated only as "confirmatory evidence"
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Single-arm; External/historical control; Pooled/basket; Dose-ranging
design_text: Approval based on re-designating a small single-arm, externally/historically-controlled dose-finding study as the "adequate and well-controlled" (AWC) trial under FDAMA §115(a)/21 CFR 314.126, after the sponsor's actual randomized pivotal trial (PROUD-PV) failed its pre-specified non-inferiority endpoint, with the failed randomized trial's non-comparative biomarker changes (not its primary comparative result) serving as the "confirmatory evidence" for the single-AWC pathway — closely related to but materially distinct from Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1's existing "Regular approval supported by same-pharmacologic-class precedent as confirmatory evidence" (Repotrectinib) entry, because here the confirmatory evidence is drawn from the sponsor's own failed randomized trial in the same development program, not from other already-approved drugs; post-hoc, unblinded-data-informed change of a trial's primary hypothesis from superiority to non-inferiority, made after database completion while the sponsor (in an open-label trial) had access to descriptive pooled-arm data, explicitly flagged by FDA's reviewer as a potential integrity violation (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §7 has no entry for a post-hoc superiority-to-non-inferiority hypothesis switch made with sponsor access to unblinded/pooled data after trial completion — distinct from the existing "SPA rescinded" and "mid-trial SAP amendment" entries, which involve FDA-agreed or blinded changes); non-randomized, non-blinded open-label extension study (CONTINUATION-PV) with a control arm assembled from patients who happened to be on hydroxyurea, used only for exploratory long-term comparison, not formal hypothesis testing

sponsor: Sanofi (via Bioverativ Therapeutics Inc., a Sanofi subsidiary since 2018); post-approval commercial rights for the CAD indication were later transferred to Recordati Rare Diseases
pivotal_trial: CARDINAL (Study BIVV009-03, Part A), NCT03347396 — single-arm, open-label trial

pivotal_trial: ACTIVATE (Study AG-348-C-006, NCT03548220) and ACTIVATE-T (Study AG-348-C-007, NCT03559699)

pivotal_trial: ASCEND-D (Study 200807, NCT02879305), with supportive programs ASCEND-ND (Study 200808, NCT02876835, non-dialysis — did not support approval), ASCEND-NHQ (Study 205270), and ASCEND-ID (Study 201410, NCT03029208)
design_text: Randomized, open-label (sponsor-blinded), active-controlled (epoetin alfa for hemodialysis, darbepoetin alfa for peritoneal dialysis), event-driven, parallel-group trial (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, §4); co-primary endpoints (§1) combining an efficacy non-inferiority margin (mean Hb change) and a safety non-inferiority margin (MACE hazard ratio) within a single trial pair — no existing taxonomy entry captures a design where the *second* co-primary is itself a safety-only non-inferiority margin rather than an efficacy or symptom endpoint ("Co-primary non-inferiority margins on both an efficacy biomarker and a safety composite (dual risk-margin design)")

sponsor: BioLineRx, Ltd. (US commercialization now under Ayrmid Pharma)
pivotal_trial: GENESIS (Study BL-8040.SCM.301, NCT03246529)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) trial with an open-label, DMC-monitored dose-confirmation lead-in (Part 1, single-arm) preceding a separately randomized Part 2 — no existing taxonomy term captures a single-arm dose-confirmation stage that gates entry into, rather than internally adapting within, a subsequent randomized trial part ("Open-label dose-confirmation lead-in followed by a separately randomized, placebo-controlled trial part"); triple-masked (participant/care provider/investigator), permuted-block randomization stratified by remission status and baseline platelet count

sponsor: GlaxoSmithKline (development conducted by Sierra Oncology, Inc. prior to GSK's 2022 acquisition)
pivotal_trial: MOMENTUM (Study SRA-MMB-301, NCT04173494)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, vs. danazol) trial, quadruple-masked, using a non-deterministic biased-coin covariate-adaptive minimization randomization scheme (Pocock 1975; Han 2009) with non-1.0 allocation probabilities (0.9/0.8) — distinct from the ad hoc "stochastic-minimization" language used for icatibant's FAST-3 trial and possibly warranting its own taxonomy row if this method recurs ("Non-deterministic biased-coin covariate-adaptive minimization randomization (Pocock-Han)"); FDA-directed trial redesign following an earlier failed pivotal program (SIMPLIFY-1/SIMPLIFY-2)

Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, GC-627-05, vs. pegfilgrastim/Neulasta) non-inferiority trial, supported by a randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled trial (GC-627-04) in which all subjects received open-label study drug from cycle 2 onward; this is a novel (351(a)) BLA, not a biosimilar, but FDA applied biosimilar-development "biocreep" reasoning to tighten its non-inferiority margin — no existing taxonomy term captures this cross-pollination of biosimilar NI-margin discipline onto a novel BLA in a crowded me-too drug class ("FDA imports biosimilar-development 'biocreep' non-inferiority-margin discipline onto a novel (non-biosimilar) BLA in a crowded me-too drug class")

pivotal_trial: APPLY-PNH (Study CLNP023C12302, NCT04558918) and APPOINT-PNH (Study CLNP023C12301, NCT04820530)
design_text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, APPLY-PNH, 8:5 randomization, switch design vs. continued anti-C5 antibody therapy) paired with a single-arm, open-label trial (§1, APPOINT-PNH, complement-inhibitor-naive) as a two-trial pivotal program; small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (§1, N=97 and N=40)

pivotal_trial: INNO2VATE program — Study AKB-6548-CI-0016 (incident dialysis, NCT02865850) and Study AKB-6548-CI-0017 (prevalent dialysis, NCT02892149); the co-developed PRO2TECT program (non-dialysis) — Study AKB-6548-CI-0014 (NCT02648347) and Study AKB-6548-CI-0015 (NCT02680574) — did NOT support approval
design_text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, vs. darbepoetin alfa), event-driven trial design, run as two co-designed programs (dialysis: INNO2VATE; non-dialysis: PRO2TECT) sharing an identical co-primary-endpoint structure; Complete Response Letter resolved via Formal Dispute Resolution Request Appeal-Denied-with-path-forward, followed by indication-narrowing resubmission — a materially more specific regulatory sequence than the existing "CRL followed by resubmission and approval" row ("Complete Response Letter resolved via Formal Dispute Resolution Request Appeal-Denied-with-path-forward, followed by indication-narrowing resubmission")

pivotal_trial: ALPHA (Study ALXN2040-PNH-301, NCT04469465)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) add-on trial — danicopan or placebo added to stable background eculizumab/ravulizumab, with all placebo patients crossing over to danicopan at Week 12 — an add-on-to-background-therapy structure distinct from the existing "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment design" row (Pegvaliase); small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population (§1, N=86, PNH prevalence ~1-1.5 per million); randomization used stochastic dynamic allocation (minimization) via interactive response technology, stratified by transfusion history, screening Hb, and Japanese ancestry

pivotal_trial: IMerge (Study MDS3001, NCT02598661)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1) Phase 3 trial (Part 2) preceded by a single-arm, open-label Phase 2 dose-finding/safety phase (Part 1) within the same overall study; first-in-class telomerase-inhibitor mechanism (novel oligonucleotide targeting the RNA template of telomerase, not currently distinguished in the taxonomy as a mechanism-class tag)

pivotal_trial: COMMODORE 2 (Study BO42162, NCT04434092), with COMMODORE 1 (Study BO42161, NCT04432584) and COMMODORE 3 (Study YO42311, NCT04654468) as supportive-only trials
design_text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, vs. eculizumab), non-inferiority, complement-inhibitor-naive trial; early enrollment cessation converting a co-developed randomized trial part to exploratory/descriptive-only status, used solely as mechanistic/PD confirmatory evidence (COMMODORE 1, stopped at ~64% of target enrollment when eculizumab-pretreated patients became difficult to recruit given the evolving PNH treatment landscape) — the opposite direction from the existing "Early-stopped for efficacy" row (PARADIGM-HF), warranting a distinct new term ("Early enrollment cessation converting a co-pivotal randomized trial part to exploratory/descriptive-only status, used solely as mechanistic/PD confirmatory evidence")

pivotal_trial: BASIS (Study B7841005), NCT03938792
design_text: Open-label, non-randomized, sequential two-phase within-patient design — a 6-month prospective observational phase (OP) on the patient's pre-existing treatment (on-demand factor or factor prophylaxis) followed by a single-arm 12-month active treatment phase (ATP) with marstacimab, used as the primary efficacy comparison in place of a concurrent randomized/placebo arm ("prospective observational-phase-vs-single-arm-active-treatment-phase, within-patient, non-randomized primary comparison" — distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Staggered-entry Blind Start crossover design," which staggers entry timing rather than sequencing a fixed observational period against a later single-arm treatment period); two separately-enrolled, separately-powered non-inhibitor cohorts (OP-OD: prior on-demand treatment, N=33; OP-PPX: prior factor prophylaxis, N=83) analyzed as independent substudies under one protocol

pivotal_trial: explorer7 (NN7415-4311), NCT04083781 (patients with inhibitors — basis for this approval); explorer8 (NN7415-4307), NCT04082429 (patients without inhibitors — conducted under the same clinical program but not completed/not part of this approval's efficacy basis)
design_text: Randomized, open-label, multi-arm trial (Arm 1: no prophylaxis/on-demand bypassing-agent treatment; Arm 2: concizumab prophylaxis, randomized comparison to Arm 1; Arm 3: patients already stable on concizumab from a prior non-interventional study continuing under the trial; Arm 4: patients originally randomized to Arms 1/2 before an October 2020 sponsor-initiated safety pause who re-entered after trial restart); mid-trial safety pause and restart following a voluntary sponsor-initiated clinical hold for thromboembolic events, with revised bleed-management guidance implemented before restart and accepted by the external independent Data Monitoring Committee ("mid-trial safety pause and restart with revised risk-mitigation procedures, following a voluntary sponsor-initiated clinical hold for thromboembolic events" — distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Early-stopped for efficacy" and interim-monitoring entries, none of which cover a paused-then-restarted trial under revised safety procedures)

sponsor: medac GmbH (Germany); US marketing rights held by Medexus Pharma, Inc.
pivotal_trial: MC-FludT.14/L Trial II, NCT00822393
design_text: Multicenter, randomized, active-controlled, event-driven, group-sequential Phase 3 non-inferiority trial (treosulfan+fludarabine vs. busulfan+fludarabine as alloHSCT conditioning) in adults 18–70 years old with AML in complete remission or MDS considered ineligible for standard-intensity conditioning; non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy (event-free survival [EFS] tested for non-inferiority first, then superiority if non-inferiority was met); full extrapolation of adult efficacy to pediatric patients ≥1 year based on disease biology/mechanism-of-action similarity plus population-PK modeling

pivotal_trial: ATLAS-A/B (EFC14768), NCT03417245 (without inhibitors) and ATLAS-INH (EFC14769), NCT03417102 (with inhibitors), with efficacy for the approved dosing regimen ultimately assessed using pooled data including the long-term-extension study ATLAS-OLE (LTE15174)
design_text: Randomized, open-label, active/no-prophylaxis-controlled Phase 3 trials (2:1 randomization to fitusiran fixed-dose 80 mg SC once-monthly prophylaxis vs. on-demand bypassing-agent/factor treatment) — but the fixed 80 mg once-monthly regimen studied in the original randomized trials was withdrawn after a clinical hold, and the regimen ultimately approved (antithrombin-activity-guided dosing, "AT-DR") was instead assessed via a cross-study, cross-period pooled comparison: the treatment period for the AT-DR regimen comes from the long-term-extension study (LTE15174), compared against the "control period" from the original parent randomized trial's on-demand/prior-prophylaxis arm, linked only by the same patients' sequential participation rather than a concurrent randomized comparison ("cross-study/cross-period pooled comparison assessing an approved dosing regimen that was itself never randomized against a concurrent comparator, following a safety-driven regimen change mid-program" — distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts" and "Mid-trial SAP amendment" entries, neither of which involves splicing a treatment period from a separate extension study onto a control period from the original parent RCT)

pivotal_trial: LUNA 3, NCT04562766
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 3 trial with an open-label extension, in adults/adolescents with persistent or chronic ITP refractory/relapsed after standard-of-care therapy (IVIg, anti-D, or corticosteroids), stratified by splenectomy status and severity of thrombocytopenia

pivotal_trial: Study OMS721-TMA-001 ("Study TMA-001"), NCT02222545, with confirmatory evidence from an Expanded Access Program (EAP) patient-level subgroup
design_family: Single-arm; External/historical control; Pooled/basket; Literature-based; Dose-ranging
design_text: Single-arm, open-label, uncontrolled, three-stage dose-escalation-then-fixed-dose Phase 2 trial in adults with TA-TMA, with effectiveness assessed against a historical control response rate derived from pooled published literature rather than a concurrent comparator arm (closest existing taxonomy match: "Non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical-control threshold (no concurrent comparator arm)," though this design used a literature-pooled response-rate benchmark with non-overlapping confidence intervals rather than a pre-specified non-inferiority margin) ("single-arm trial with a literature-pooled historical-control response rate as primary comparator, corroborated by a second independent data source (an expanded-access program's patient-level data) serving as confirmatory evidence in lieu of a second pivotal trial" — distinct from the taxonomy's matched-historical-control entries, which use patient-level genotype/natural-history matching rather than a literature-pooled aggregate rate); a prior (2021) Complete Response Letter and full resubmission with new external-control data

sponsor: Takeda Pharmaceuticals (Takeda Pharmaceuticals America, Inc.; rusfertide originated at Protagonist Therapeutics)
pivotal_trial: VERIFY, NCT05210790
design_text: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial (add-on to each patient's ongoing PV standard of care — phlebotomy alone or phlebotomy plus one or more cytoreductive agents), 1:1 randomization for a 32-week blinded period, followed by open-label rusfertide for all patients through Week 156

pivotal_trial: Study MCP-103-302 (NCT00938717, 26-week, US, 111 sites) and Study LIN-MD-31 (NCT00948818, 12-week treatment plus 4-week randomized-withdrawal period, US/Canada, 118 sites)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group (both trials); LIN-MD-31 added a 4-week double-blind randomized-withdrawal period after the 12-week treatment period, a "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment"-adjacent design though here applied to the whole randomized population rather than a run-in-selected responder subset, so distinct from the taxonomy's existing randomized-withdrawal-enrichment entry (Palynziq/PRISM-2); 5-step serial gatekeeping multiplicity procedure across 4 co-primary and 9 secondary efficacy parameters, combining a fixed-sequence first step with Hochberg procedures within later steps

sponsor: NPS Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (acquired by Shire in 2015, after this approval)

pivotal_trial: GEMINI I, Study C13006, NCT00783718 (ulcerative colitis, co-pivotal); GEMINI II, Study C13007, NCT00783692 (Crohn's disease, co-pivotal); supportive GEMINI III, Study C13011, NCT01224171 (Crohn's disease, induction-only)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multinational trials combining an induction phase and a maintenance phase within one protocol; induction-responder re-randomization design in which patients who achieve clinical response to induction (whether from blinded randomized or open-label induction) are freshly re-randomized into two or more maintenance dosing arms plus placebo, with the maintenance phase's sample size, endpoints, and multiplicity structure powered and analyzed independently of the induction phase (**"Induction-responder re-randomization design (into multiple maintenance-dose arms)"**; distinct from the existing "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment design" entry, which is a simpler two-arm continue-vs.-switch-to-placebo structure)

sponsor: AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP (compound originated at Nektar Therapeutics as NKTR-118, licensed to AstraZeneca)

pivotal_trial: POISE, Study 747-301, NCT01473524 (accelerated-approval basis); confirmatory outcomes trial COBALT, Study 747-302, NCT02308111 (post-marketing requirement, statistically null, terminated early)
