pivotal_trial: Trial 1 (Study C2009-0201, NCT01142089), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority trial, as the primary basis for efficacy; Trial 2 (RIT-1/AID, NCT01208922), a randomized, double-blind, active (ciprofloxacin)-controlled non-inferiority trial, as supportive evidence
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority trial (Trial 1, 3:1 randomization to rifamycin:placebo, 8 sites in Guatemala/Mexico, stratified by site) as the primary efficacy basis; supportive randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, adaptive 3-stage group-sequential non-inferiority trial (Trial 2, 1:1, 19 sites in India/Ecuador/Guatemala) that was independently conceived, sponsored, and conducted by a different company (Dr. Falk Pharma GmbH) outside a U.S. IND, with sponsorship of the trial only later transferred to Cosmo after completion — **"Cross-sponsor reliance on an independently conducted, non-IND supportive trial with post-hoc sponsorship transfer"**, distinct from existing taxonomy entries describing pooling within one sponsor's own program

sponsor: Shire Development LLC (acquired by Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited in January 2019, shortly after approval)
pivotal_trial: two FDA-designated pivotal trials — Study 3001/PRU-CRC-3001 (NCT01116206), conducted in the Asia-Pacific region, and Study 302/SPD555-302 (NCT01147926), conducted in Europe — supported by three 1999-era "legacy" Phase 3 trials (PRU-INT-6, PRU-USA-11, PRU-USA-13) and one Phase 4 European trial (SPD555-401) that did not reach statistical significance
design_text: two non-US, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials designated by FDA as the pivotal basis for a 2018 US approval of a molecule first approved in the EU (as Resolor) in 2009 — Study 3001 enrolled a predominantly female, Asian/Australian population, while Study 302 enrolled an all-male European population — plus three supportive 1999-era Phase 3 trials and one supportive Phase 4 trial (SPD555-401) that failed to reach significance (25% vs. 20% responders, p=0.34); reliance on trials designed and completed years to over a decade before the NDA was filed, none of whose SAPs had been submitted to FDA prior to the 2017 NDA submission

pivotal_trial: T3MPO-1 (sponsor protocol TEN-01-301, NCT02621892) and T3MPO-2 (TEN-01-302, NCT02686138); supportive open-label 52-week safety-extension trial T3MPO-3 (TEN-01-303)
design_text: two Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trials using Rome III (not Rome IV) IBS-C diagnostic criteria — T3MPO-1 (12-week double-blind treatment period followed by a 4-week randomized-withdrawal period, 122 US sites, N=606) and T3MPO-2 (26-week double-blind treatment period, no randomized-withdrawal period, 92 US sites, N=593); note the approved label's internal "Trial 1"/"Trial 2" numbering is inverted relative to the published T3MPO nomenclature (label's Trial 1 = TEN-01-302/T3MPO-2; label's Trial 2 = TEN-01-301/T3MPO-1)

pivotal_trial: Study BLI400-302 (Study 302, NCT02819297), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled — the sole trial FDA relied upon as an adequate, well-controlled trial; supportive non-inferiority trial Study BLI400-301 (Study 301, NCT02481947, active [Amitiza/lubiprostone]-controlled) and open-label long-term safety trial Study BLI400-303 (Study 303, NCT02819310)
design_text: one large, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (Study 302, 6-month duration) that FDA treated as the sole adequate, well-controlled trial; a second randomized, non-inferiority, active(lubiprostone)-controlled trial (Study 301) that FDA explicitly declined to rely upon as one of the two required adequate, well-controlled trials, because of a flawed non-inferiority margin derivation; to compensate, FDA requested and relied in part on a sponsor-submitted summary of published literature trials plus a post-hoc meta-analysis comparing Study 301's lactitol-arm response rate against historical placebo data from other CIC trials — closest existing taxonomy concept is "Non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical-control threshold," but here the historical comparison was constructed as a *supplement* to a rejected concurrent-comparator non-inferiority trial rather than as the primary design itself; propose **"Post-hoc historical-placebo meta-analysis constructed to rehabilitate an already-rejected non-inferiority trial's evidentiary value"**

drug: Vonoprazan/amoxicillin/clarithromycin (Voquezna Triple Pak and Voquezna Dual Pak)
pivotal_trial: Study HP-301, NCT04167670 — a Phase 3, randomized, quadruple-masked (triple-therapy arms fully blinded; dual-therapy arm masked to outcome assessors only), active-controlled (lansoprazole-based triple therapy) non-inferiority/superiority trial
design_text: randomized (1:1:1), partially masked, active-controlled non-inferiority (with superiority follow-up) trial comparing two experimental regimens (vonoprazan dual therapy; vonoprazan triple therapy) against a single active-control regimen (lansoprazole triple therapy) within one trial, each experimental regimen carrying its own dedicated alpha allocation

pivotal_trial: CONFIRM, NCT02770716
design_text: randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial on top of standard of care (including albumin), in patients with HRS-1/HRS-AKI; the fourth and largest of four sequential registration-directed trials submitted for this NDA over a 13-year regulatory history (OT-0401, REVERSE, then CONFIRM), following two prior Complete/Incomplete Response Letters, with the primary endpoint definition itself renegotiated between sponsor and FDA via a Special Protocol Assessment before CONFIRM began

sponsor: Pfizer Inc. (originally developed by Arena Pharmaceuticals, acquired by Pfizer in 2022)
pivotal_trial: ELEVATE UC 52 (Study APD334-301, NCT03945188) and ELEVATE UC 12 (Study APD334-302, NCT03996369) — two Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials
design_text: two randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trials — ELEVATE UC 52 a 52-week trial with co-primary endpoints at Weeks 12 and 52 (an initial 12-week induction period followed, for non-worsening subjects, by 40 further weeks on the original randomized assignment), ELEVATE UC 12 a stand-alone 12-week induction-only trial with a single primary endpoint at Week 12; randomization in both trials stratified by prior biologic/JAK-inhibitor failure status, baseline corticosteroid use, and baseline disease activity (modified Mayo Score [mMS] 4-6 vs. 7-9)

pivotal_trial: LUCENT-1 (Study I6T-MC-AMAN, NCT03518086, induction) and LUCENT-2 (Study I6T-MC-AMBG, NCT03524092, maintenance) — a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled induction trial followed by a randomized-withdrawal-style maintenance trial in induction responders
design_text: single Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled induction trial (LUCENT-1, 3:1 randomization) — the Applicant conducted only one induction trial, with FDA accepting a single induction study specifically because its pre-specified two-sided alpha of 0.00125 was designed to provide "the same statistical evidence against the null hypothesis as achieving statistical significance on two independent induction studies that are each tested at a 2-sided alpha level of 0.05" (a single-trial-substitutes-for-two-trials justification grounded in an extreme alpha threshold rather than a rare-disease/mechanistic-precedent argument, distinct from the somatrogon entry's single-trial justification elsewhere in this batch); LUCENT-2 (maintenance) re-randomized (2:1) only the induction-trial mirikizumab responders to continued mirikizumab or withdrawal-to-placebo, while separately continuing placebo-responders on blinded placebo and re-inducing induction nonresponders open-label — a three-cohort maintenance-trial structure combining randomized-withdrawal (for induction responders) with open-label re-induction (for nonresponders) in a single protocol, an elaboration of Keyword_Taxonomy.md's "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment design" entry (Pegvaliase-pqpz) that adds a third, non-randomized re-induction arm

pivotal_trial: MAESTRO-NASH (Study MGL-3196-11, NCT03900429), a Phase 3, multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial; supportive Phase 3 safety trial MAESTRO-NAFLD-1 (Study MGL-3196-14, NCT04197479) and supportive Phase 2 trial MGL-3196-05
design_text: randomized (1:1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of resmetirom 80mg vs. 100mg vs. placebo, stratified by type 2 diabetes status and baseline fibrosis stage (F1B/F2 vs. F3); approval rests on a pre-specified **Week 52 interim histology analysis** of an ongoing, longer trial whose final analysis (a clinical-outcomes composite at Month 54) will serve as the required accelerated-approval confirmatory endpoint — i.e., the same trial supplies both the surrogate basis for accelerated approval and its own eventual confirmatory verification (matching Keyword_Taxonomy.md's "Accelerated approval based on an interim analysis, confirmed by the same trial's own final analysis," previously seen only in atacicept-vymj); dual co-primary histologic endpoints, each requiring a **paired liver biopsy** (baseline and Week 52, read by two independent masked pathologists) — an unusually invasive procedural requirement for a primary efficacy endpoint, layered on a post-unblinding-finalized consensus-read adjudication process for pathologist disagreements that FDA's reviewer could not confirm was adequately prespecified (see SAP excerpts below) ("invasive paired-biopsy dual-histology surrogate endpoint with a post-hoc/near-unblinding-finalized consensus-adjudication process for reader disagreement")

sponsor: Ipsen Biopharmaceuticals, Inc. (elafibranor was originally developed by Genfit; Ipsen licensed global rights in 2021)
pivotal_trial: ELATIVE (Study GFT505B-319-1, NCT04526665), a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
design_text: randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of elafibranor 80mg vs. placebo in PBC patients with inadequate UDCA response or UDCA intolerance, stratified by (1) ALP >3×ULN or total bilirubin (TB) >ULN, and (2) baseline PBC Worst Itch Numeric Rating Scale (WI-NRS) score ≥4; a 52-week common double-blind period followed by a variable-duration double-blind period (up to 104 weeks total) and an open-label long-term extension

sponsor: GlaxoSmithKline LLC (GSK) — **correction to task brief:** the FDA NDA approval letter (dated March 2026) is addressed to GSK's Senior Director of Global Regulatory Affairs, and the approved label's adverse-event-reporting and manufacturing lines both list GlaxoSmithKline, not Intercept Pharmaceuticals/Alfasigma; linerixibat (GSK2330672) was originally a GSK-discovered asset and appears to remain GSK's NDA at approval, though Intercept/Alfasigma has been publicly associated with earlier-phase development of ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors in cholestatic pruritus more broadly
pivotal_trial: GLISTEN (Trial 212620, NCT04950127, N=238) — a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 24-week trial of linerixibat 40 mg twice daily vs. placebo in adults with PBC-associated pruritus; companion Phase 2b dose-finding trial GLIMMER (Trial 201000) supported dose selection and safety
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial (GLISTEN/Trial 212620); companion five-arm, adaptive, phase 2b dose-finding trial (GLIMMER/Trial 201000) whose interim-data-informed dose adaptations were, per FDA's review, "not accounted for in the statistical analysis" of that supportive study

pivotal_trial: Study B2305 (NCT00434148) — a single, randomized, double-blind, two-dose (600 mcg and 900 mcg subcutaneous, twice daily), non-comparative Phase 3 trial; this was a "one study application" (per FDA's own review keywords), with orphan-drug designation granted in 2009 given the rarity of Cushing's disease
design_text: randomized, double-blind, dose-comparison trial in which the two dose arms were each independently evaluated against a fixed responder threshold rather than compared to each other or to a placebo/control arm — matching the taxonomy's existing "Wald confidence interval decision rule for a single activity-threshold responder rate" entry, applied here in parallel to two independently randomized dose arms of the same drug within one trial rather than a single-arm design; a blinded dose-titration/response-adaptive element was embedded mid-trial — non-responding patients (by an interim mUFC criterion) were unblinded at Month 3 and dose-escalated, while responders remained blinded through Month 6

pivotal_trial: REPLACE, Study CL1-11-040, NCT00732615
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 24-week trial with a pre-randomization "optimization period" to bring all subjects to a common calcium/vitamin D baseline before treatment allocation, and an individually flexible, titratable active dose

sponsor: KAI Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Amgen Inc.
pivotal_trial: Study 20120229, NCT01785849; Study 20120230, NCT01788046 (both placebo-controlled); Study 20120360, NCT01896232 (active-controlled vs. cinacalcet)
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (Studies 229, 230); randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, dose-titration (Study 360, vs. cinacalcet)

pivotal_trial: ACTIVE (Study BA-058-05-003), NCT01343004, with supportive data from ACTIVExtend (Study BA-058-05-005), NCT01657162
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm (abaloparatide 80 μg / teriparatide 20 μg / placebo) with the active-comparator arm restricted to a safety endpoint, not used for efficacy comparison; open-label, blinded-to-prior-treatment extension study with all patients receiving alendronate (ACTIVExtend)

pivotal_trial: Study 52 (AEZS-130-052), open-label, randomized, single-dose, 2-way crossover diagnostic-accuracy trial vs. the insulin tolerance test (ITT); original Study 47 (AEZS-130-047) was the initial pivotal study submitted under an SPA and failed its pre-specified primary analysis, contributing to a Complete Response recommendation before Study 52 was conducted
design_text: Diagnostic-accuracy study (single-arm, within-patient paired comparison) (existing taxonomy term — 2-way crossover of macimorelin GHST vs. insulin tolerance test, same subjects receiving both); primary-analysis-framework change across submission cycles following a failed SPA-agreed endpoint (ROC/AUC threshold replaced by a percent-agreement/benchmark framework)

sponsor: Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical Inc. (co-developed with Kyowa Kirin)
pivotal_trial: Adults: Study UX023-CL303, NCT02526160 (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled); Pediatrics: Study UX023-CL201, NCT02163577 (randomized, open-label, dose-finding, ages 5-12, compared via propensity-score analysis to the external Study UX023-CL002 conventional-therapy cohort) and Study UX023-CL205, NCT02750618 (ages 1-4)
control: Placebo; Active; Dose comparison; External/historical; None
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (adult Study CL303); randomized non-comparative dose-regimen cohort design (existing taxonomy term — pediatric Study CL201, Q2W vs. Q4W dosing-interval randomization, no placebo/active-control arm); propensity-score-weighted external/historical comparator substituting for a concurrent control arm, using an active conventional-therapy cohort (Study CL002) rather than placebo (extension of existing taxonomy term, which is defined for a placebo comparator)

pivotal_trial: FRAME (Study 20070337, NCT01575834), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and ARCH (Study 20110142, NCT01631214), randomized, double-blind, active (alendronate)-controlled
design_text: two co-primary Phase 3 trials with different comparators run in parallel — FRAME (placebo-controlled, N=7,180, 12 months double-blind then all subjects switched to open-label denosumab) and ARCH (active alendronate-controlled, N=4,093, romosozumab-then-alendronate vs. alendronate-alone, event-driven follow-up to a target of 440 confirmed nonvertebral-fracture events); a cardiovascular safety signal appeared in ARCH (active-controlled) but not in FRAME (placebo-controlled), producing a **cross-trial safety-signal discordance by comparator type** that drove a Complete Response Letter — closest existing taxonomy concept is "Approval program with a substantial proportion of negative/failed pivotal trials" (Vortioxetine), but that describes efficacy-trial discordance rather than a safety signal appearing only against one comparator type; propose **"Post-hoc cross-trial safety-signal reconciliation following comparator-dependent discordance (CRL-triggering)"**

sponsor: Recordati Rare Diseases, Inc. (originally developed by Novartis as LCI699; licensed to Recordati)
pivotal_trial: Study C2301/CLCI699C2301 (LINC-3, NCT02180217), a randomized-withdrawal design — the sole trial submitted that included randomization; supportive single-arm studies C1201 and C2201 (LINC-1/LINC-2) and an unfinished, separately conducted placebo-controlled Study C2302/CLCI699C2302 (LINC-4, NCT02697734), submitted for safety only at the time of this NDA
design_text: a single randomized-withdrawal (RW) trial (LINC-3) as the only submitted study with randomization, comprising a 12-week dose-titration period, a 12-week single-arm (open-label) treatment period, and an 8-week randomized-withdrawal period (osilodrostat continuation vs. placebo substitution) — the FDA statistical reviewer explicitly flagged this design as "not designed to directly evaluate the treatment effect in comparison to placebo in treatment-naïve patients," since randomization occurred only among patients who had already responded to 24 weeks of open-label osilodrostat; this maps to the existing taxonomy term "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment design" (seen in Pegvaliase-pqpz/Palynziq), extending it to an endocrine/orphan-disease context with a companion separately-sponsored-at-the-time placebo-controlled confirmatory trial (LINC-4) submitted for safety only

pivotal_trial: REAL 1, NCT02229851
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with an added open-label, active-referenced arm (daily Norditropin) not powered or intended for a formal non-inferiority claim — 2:1 randomization between once-weekly somapacitan and daily placebo, plus a separate open-label daily-Norditropin reference arm; 34-week double-blind main period followed by a 52-week open-label extension

pivotal_trial: Study RM-493-012 (POMC/PCSK1 deficiency), NCT02896192, and Study RM-493-015 (LEPR deficiency), NCT03287960 — two identically designed single-arm, open-label, 1-year Phase 3 trials, each with an embedded 8-week double-blind, placebo-controlled withdrawal period
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Crossover; Randomized withdrawal; Single-arm
design_text: single-arm, open-label, 1-year trial design in an ultra-rare genetically-defined population (matches "Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population," Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, seen in Lomitapide/Mipomersen/Metreleptin/Evinacumab-dgnb), with an embedded fixed-sequence double-blind placebo-controlled withdrawal period (4 weeks continued drug, then 4 weeks placebo, in that fixed order for every subject, not randomized) serving as a within-subject control absent any parallel comparator arm — *("Fixed-sequence double-blind placebo re-challenge window embedded within an open-label single-arm trial, providing a within-subject control without randomized withdrawal")*, distinct from the taxonomy's existing "Randomized-withdrawal enrichment design" (Pegvaliase/PRISM-2), where continuation vs. withdrawal is itself randomized among responders

pivotal_trial: heiGHt Trial (Study CT-301), NCT02781727
design_text: randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled (daily Genotropin) non-inferiority trial with a pre-specified superiority test to follow if non-inferiority was met (matches "Non-inferiority-then-superiority hierarchy," Keyword_Taxonomy.md §1, seen in EMPA-REG/DECLARE-TIMI58); prepubertal treatment-naive children with GHD, 52-week treatment period

pivotal_trial: TN-10, NCT01030861 — a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted by the NIH-funded Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet Study Group (lead sponsor on ClinicalTrials.gov is NIDDK, not Provention Bio); PROTECT, NCT03875729, an ongoing Provention-sponsored trial, contributed only safety/bridging data (see below), not efficacy, to this approval
design_text: efficacy claim built entirely on a single externally-sponsored, investigator-initiated (NIH/TrialNet) trial that the BLA applicant did not design or run under its own IND oversight — *("BLA efficacy claim built on a single externally-sponsored/investigator-initiated trial not conducted under the applicant's own IND")* — FDA's statistical reviewer noted explicitly that "TN-10 was first brought to the FDA after study completion or near completion. Reviewer's knowledge on protocol changes are all based on the applicant's narrative"; randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single 14-day drug course, event-driven follow-up (median 50.6 months) in autoantibody-positive, dysglycemic (Stage 2) relatives of type 1 diabetes patients age ≥8

pivotal_trial: SKYLIGHT 1, NCT04003155, and SKYLIGHT 2, NCT04003142 — two identically designed Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials
design_text: two identically designed randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, each with a 12-week placebo-controlled period followed by a non-controlled active-treatment extension; two doses (30 mg, 45 mg) tested in parallel against placebo in both trials, though the sponsor ultimately sought approval only for the 45 mg dose

sponsor: Pfizer Inc. (in collaboration with OPKO Health, Inc., which co-developed somatrogon/MOD-4023)
pivotal_trial: Study CP-4-006 / C0311009 (NCT02968004), a Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active (Genotropin)-controlled, 52-week non-inferiority trial; supportive Phase 2 dose-finding study CP-4-004 and supportive Japanese Phase 3 trial CP-4-009 (published as a distinct dataset, no independently located NCT number)
design_text: single adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 randomized, open-label, active-controlled, parallel-group non-inferiority trial (CP-4-006) plus confirmatory evidence resting on strong mechanistic understanding of the GH/IGF-1 pathway, rather than a second independent pivotal trial — FDA explicitly invoked the precedent that "historically, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted a single adequate and well controlled trial for the approval of hGH products with native GH sequences for the pediatric GHD indication" because of the rarity of pediatric GHD (closest Keyword_Taxonomy.md term, "Small single-arm or small randomized trial in an ultra-rare disease population," describes an adjacent but distinct scenario — a single randomized non-inferiority trial substituting for two independent pivotal trials specifically on same-pharmacologic-class/mechanistic grounds is not currently catalogued); prior Complete Response Letter (January 21, 2021) for unresolved immunogenicity (anti-drug antibody, including neutralizing antibody) concerns plus quality deficiencies, resolved via a resubmission with additional long-term/immunogenicity data — not a new efficacy trial

sponsor: Ascendis Pharma Bone Diseases A/S (Ascendis Pharma)
pivotal_trial: PaTHway (Study TCP-304, NCT04701203), a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial with an open-label extension; supportive Phase 2 trial TCP-201
design_text: randomized (3:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial with a 26-week blinded treatment period followed by a 156-week open-label extension; randomization stratified by etiology of hypoparathyroidism (postsurgical vs. other) "as per FDA recommendation"; dose titrated (6-60 mcg/day, in 3 mcg increments no more than every 7 days) based on serum calcium, aiming for independence from conventional calcium/active-vitamin-D therapy; the trial permitted study-drug up-titration throughout the blinded period even though FDA had recommended a fixed-dose period specifically to assess persistence of effect — FDA accepted the deviation from its own recommendation because the responder definition already treated any late study-drug increase as a treatment failure (a documented instance of FDA accepting a sponsor's departure from an Agency design recommendation because a countervailing feature of the responder-endpoint definition addressed the Agency's underlying concern)

pivotal_trial: CAHtalyst Adult (Study NBI-74788-CAH3003, NCT04490915, N=182) and CAHtalyst Pediatric (Study CAH2006, NCT04806451, N=103) — both Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of crinecerfont (a corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 receptor antagonist) added to existing glucocorticoid therapy
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with an unblinded interim analysis using the "promising zone" adaptive sample-size re-estimation method (Mehta and Pocock, 2011), managed by an Independent Statistical Committee (ISC) and a Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) with access to the Adaptation Plan restricted to a firewalled subset of sponsor staff — closest existing taxonomy term is "Adaptive seamless enrollment with a conditional-power enrollment gate" (Harvoni/ION-1), but that entry describes a simple stop/continue enrollment gate rather than a promising-zone conditional-power-driven sample-size increase (Stage 1 sample fixed at ~76 subjects/46% of planned N, Stage 2 sample size increased up to 210 subjects depending on interim conditional power) — flagged **("Promising-zone adaptive sample-size re-estimation (Mehta-Pocock)")**; adjunctive add-on design (both arms continued background glucocorticoid therapy)

pivotal_trial: PATHFNDR-1 ("Trial 09" in the FDA review, NCT04837040, N=58) and PATHFNDR-2 ("Trial 08," NCT05192382, N=111) — two Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of paltusotine (an oral nonpeptide somatostatin receptor ligand), each in a distinct acromegaly population
design_text: two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials — PATHFNDR-2 (Trial 08) enrolled medically naive, previously-treated, and washout subgroups (24-week randomized-control phase) while PATHFNDR-1 (Trial 09) enrolled only subjects previously biochemically controlled on injectable somatostatin analogs, testing paltusotine as maintenance therapy after a washout (36-week randomized-control phase); both followed by an open-label extension; note both trials' ClinicalTrials.gov records show overall status "Terminated," but this reflects early administrative closure of the post-approval open-label-extension follow-up for business reasons in 2026, not a failure of the randomized-controlled primary-endpoint phase (which completed normally in 2023-2024 and is the basis for approval)

pivotal_trial: OASIS 1 (NCT05042362, N=396), OASIS 2 (NCT05099159, N=400), and OASIS 3 (NCT05030584, N=628) — three Phase 3, randomized, quadruple/double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of elinzanetant (a neurokinin-1,3 receptor antagonist); OASIS 1 and 2 were 26-week identically designed efficacy trials, OASIS 3 a 52-week supportive/safety trial with a single primary endpoint
design_text: two identically protocoled randomized, quadruple-blind (participant/care-provider/investigator/outcomes-assessor), placebo-controlled, parallel efficacy trials (OASIS 1, OASIS 2) plus a third supportive/longer-duration double-blind placebo-controlled trial (OASIS 3) without subgroup-analysis or key-secondary-endpoint testing, all stratified by region (US vs. rest of world)

sponsor: Ascendis Pharma Growth Disorders A/S (Ascendis Pharma Endocrinology, Inc., U.S. applicant)
pivotal_trial: ApproaCH (Trial ASND0036 in the FDA review; "Trial 1" in the label; NCT05598320, N=84) — a Phase 2b/3, multicenter, quadruple-masked, randomized (2:1), placebo-controlled, 52-week trial of once-weekly subcutaneous navepegritide in treatment-naive children with genetically confirmed achondroplasia, followed by a single-arm open-label extension
design_text: randomized (2:1), quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled parallel trial with a 52-week double-blind period followed by an OLE; accelerated approval on a surrogate growth endpoint in a pediatric rare-disease population

pivotal_trial: ROSELLA (Trial CORT125134-556, NCT05257408, N=381) — a Phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled, two-arm trial of relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel vs. nab-paclitaxel alone in platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer
design_text: randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, two-arm add-on trial (relacorilant + nab-paclitaxel vs. nab-paclitaxel alone), stratified by number of prior lines of therapy (1 vs. >1) and region (North America vs. Europe vs. Korea/Australia/Latin America); dual primary endpoints with a group-sequential alpha-recycling structure

pivotal_trial: VIEW 1 (Study VGFT-OD-0605, NCT00509795) and VIEW 2 (Study 311523, NCT00637377) — two identically designed, multicenter, double-masked, randomized, active (ranibizumab)-controlled non-inferiority trials
design_text: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled non-inferiority trial design, 1:1:1:1 randomization across four arms (2 mg every 4 weeks [2Q4], 0.5 mg every 4 weeks [0.5Q4], 2 mg every 8 weeks after 3 monthly loading doses [2Q8], and 0.5 mg ranibizumab every 4 weeks [RQ4]); two identically protocoled trials (VIEW 1, VIEW 2) run in parallel by the same sponsor, a design pattern close to but not identical to the taxonomy's "two identically protocoled randomized... trials" entry (EMPA-REG/DECLARE-TIMI58 pattern), reused here; Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) periodic safety review with an alpha-spending-style significance-level correction (0.1%) applied to preserve overall Type I error across repeated safety looks

sponsor: Merck & Co., Inc. (originally developed by Santen Pharmaceutical/Asahi Kasei Pharma)
pivotal_trial: Study 001 ("MK-2452-001," NCT01026831, preservative-free tafluprost vs. preservative-free timolol, 12 weeks) and Study 15-003 (preservative-containing tafluprost vs. preservative-containing timolol, 12 months, no NCT identified — appears to predate/fall outside mandatory ClinicalTrials.gov registration as a non-US-only-era trial); bridging Study 77550 (preservative-containing vs. preservative-free tafluprost, crossover, no NCT identified) established formulation equivalence; supportive Study 74458 (tafluprost vs. latanoprost, 24 months) failed to demonstrate non-inferiority and was not used as a basis for approval
design_family: Parallel-group RCT; Crossover; Single-arm; External/historical control
design_text: Non-inferiority analysis against a fixed historical/regulatory-agreed margin, applied here as randomized, double-masked, active(timolol)-controlled parallel-group trials (Studies 15-003, 001) rather than a historical-control single-arm design — reuse of the taxonomy's non-inferiority-margin concept in a conventional concurrently-randomized active-controlled setting; separate crossover bridging study (77550) used specifically to establish preservative-free/preservative-containing formulation equivalence (PK/exposure-equivalence-bridging-adjacent concept, though here on a PD/efficacy endpoint rather than PK exposure); one of three "pivotal" non-inferiority trials submitted (Study 74458, vs. latanoprost) failed its own pre-specified non-inferiority criterion and was reviewed for safety only, not efficacy

pivotal_trial: TG-MV-006 (MIVI-TRUST, NCT00781859) and TG-MV-007 (MIVI-TRUST, NCT00798317) — two identically designed, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked, 6-month Phase 3 trials
design_text: randomized, double-masked, placebo(vehicle-injection)-controlled, parallel-group; the two MIVI-TRUST trials were identical in design and conduct except treatment allocation ratio (2:1 in TG-MV-006, US-only; 3:1 in TG-MV-007, EU+US) — a vehicle (not sham) injection was used specifically to preserve masking

sponsor: Shire Development LLC (lifitegrast originated at SARcode Bioscience, acquired by Shire in 2013)
pivotal_trial: OPUS-2, NCT01743729, and OPUS-3, NCT02284516 (the two trials FDA ultimately relied on as the efficacy basis); OPUS-1, NCT01421498, was part of the original submission but is supportive rather than independently confirmatory (see Regulatory history below)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials with co-primary sign/symptom endpoints in the original submission (OPUS-1, OPUS-2), followed by a Complete Response Letter and a single confirmatory resubmission trial (OPUS-3) in which the "sign" endpoint was redefined as a safety variable at FDA's request

sponsor: Bausch & Lomb Incorporated (originally developed by Nicox S.A.; licensed to Bausch & Lomb)
pivotal_trial: APOLLO (Study 770), NCT01749904, and LUNAR (Study 769), NCT01749930
design_text: Randomized, double-masked, active-controlled (vs. timolol 0.5%), parallel-group, multi-timepoint co-primary non-inferiority design requiring the NI margin to hold at every one of 9 measurement timepoints plus a tighter margin at a majority of timepoints

pivotal_trial: ROCKET-1 (Study AR-13324-CS301), NCT02207491; ROCKET-2 (Study AR-13324-CS302), NCT02207621; ROCKET-4 (Study AR-13324-CS304), NCT02558374
design_text: Randomized, double-masked, active-controlled (vs. timolol 0.5% BID) non-inferiority trials, multi-timepoint co-primary non-inferiority design requiring the NI margin to hold at every one of 9 measurement timepoints plus a tighter margin at a majority of timepoints (shared with Vyzulta/latanoprostene bunod); post-hoc subgroup from a failed pivotal trial promoted to the pre-specified primary analysis population of subsequent same-program trials

pivotal_trial: two co-pivotal trials — REPARO (Study NGF0212, NCT01756456), a Phase 1/2 trial conducted at 32 sites across 6 EU countries, and Study NGF0214 (NCT02227147), a Phase 2 trial conducted at 11 US sites; no Phase 3 trial was conducted for this program
design_text: two co-pivotal, randomized, multicenter, double-masked, vehicle-controlled trials of low sample size (REPARO Phase 2 part N=156, 1:1:1 across two rhNGF concentrations and vehicle; NGF0214 N=48, 1:1 rhNGF 20 µg/mL vs. vehicle) — no Phase 3 trial was run for this orphan-designated program

pivotal_trial: HAWK (Study RTH258-C001, NCT02307682) and HARRIER (Study RTH258-C002, NCT02434328), both randomized, double-masked, active (aflibercept)-controlled, non-inferiority trials
design_text: two-year, multicenter, randomized, double-masked, active(aflibercept 2 mg)-controlled, non-inferiority trials — HAWK (3-arm, 1:1:1, brolucizumab 3 mg/6 mg/aflibercept, N=1,082 randomized) and HARRIER (2-arm, 1:1, brolucizumab 6 mg/aflibercept, N=743 randomized); both used a fixed default q12w dosing interval after loading doses, with protocol-defined disease-activity criteria triggering an individualized switch to q8w dosing — **"Response-adaptive fixed-interval dosing with criteria-triggered rescue-to-shorter-interval switching"** (distinct from a treat-and-extend design, since the default interval is fixed and only shortens on a defined trigger rather than continuously extending/contracting)

sponsor: D.O.R.C. (Dutch Ophthalmic Research Center) International b.v.
pivotal_trial: none — approved under 505(b)(2) based entirely on FDA's own review of published literature; the applicant "has not conducted or sponsored any clinical studies of this product"
design_text: a 505(b)(2) NDA for a surgical visualization dye with no sponsor-conducted or sponsor-sponsored clinical trial of any kind; FDA's Medical Officer instead performed a MEDLINE literature search (searches run in March 2015 and September 2019) identifying 18 independently conducted clinical studies (12 controlled) using Brilliant Blue G from varied manufacturers, and reviewed a representative sample study-by-study — this maps closely to the existing taxonomy term "Literature-based approval (no dedicated pivotal trial)" (seen in Landiolol), but differs in that the underlying studies here were heterogeneous non-RCT designs (systematic review/meta-analysis, electron-microscopy specimen studies, nonrandomized comparative case series, one randomized 2-arm trial) rather than a set of published RCTs, and no pooled/composite endpoint was constructed across them — propose as a refinement: **"FDA-conducted qualitative narrative literature synthesis across heterogeneous non-sponsor study designs, with no formal Biostatistics review performed"**

sponsor: Genentech, Inc. (a member of the Roche Group)
pivotal_trial: for nAMD, TENAYA (NCT03823287) and LUCERNE (NCT03823300); for DME, YOSEMITE (NCT03622580) and RHINE (NCT03622593) — four identically structured Phase 3, randomized, double-masked, active-comparator (aflibercept)-controlled, non-inferiority trials
design_text: randomized (1:1:1), double-masked, active-comparator-controlled non-inferiority design comparing faricimab administered on a protocol-defined personalized treatment interval (PTI, extendable up to every 16 weeks based on objective disease-activity criteria) against fixed every-8-week aflibercept, replicated across two identically designed trials per indication — *("Personalized/extendable treatment-interval non-inferiority design tested against a fixed-interval active comparator")*; ICH E9(R1) estimand framework with mixed composite/hypothetical intercurrent-event strategies (treatment-policy strategy for non-COVID-19 intercurrent events, hypothetical/censored strategy for COVID-19-related intercurrent events) — matches Keyword_Taxonomy.md §4 term seen in Icotrokinra/Lebrikizumab-lbkz

pivotal_trial: three Phase 3 trials submitted in support: Study 01171505 / AYAME (vs. latanoprost), NCT02981446; Study 011710IN / Spectrum 4 (vs. timolol), NCT03691662; Study 011709IN / Spectrum 3 (vs. timolol), NCT03691649
design_text: three randomized, double-masked, active-controlled non-inferiority trials of a first-in-class selective prostaglandin EP2-receptor agonist (mechanistically distinct from prostaglandin-analog IOP-lowering agents such as latanoprost) against two different active comparators (latanoprost in one trial, timolol in two trials); notably, **one of the three pivotal trials (011709IN/Spectrum 3) failed to meet its non-inferiority objective** against timolol, while the other two succeeded — approval rested on the totality of evidence across all three rather than on a uniformly positive program

sponsor: Bausch + Lomb Incorporated (licensed from Novaliq GmbH, which originated the molecule as NOV03/EyeSol technology)
pivotal_trial: GOBI (Study NVU-003, NCT04139798) and MOJAVE (Study BL-904, NCT04567329) — two identically designed Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-masked, saline-controlled trials
design_text: two identically protocoled randomized, double-masked, saline-controlled superiority trials (GOBI, MOJAVE), 1:1 randomization, stratified by clinical site and baseline dryness score (VAS <70 vs. ≥70); parallel-group; no interim analyses planned

pivotal_trial: SATURN-1 (Study TRS-009, NCT04475432, a Phase 2b/3 trial) and SATURN-2 (Study TRS-010, NCT04784091, a Phase 3 trial) — two near-identically designed multicenter, randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trials
design_text: two near-identically protocoled randomized (1:1), double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trials (SATURN-1 as Phase 2b/3, SATURN-2 as a confirmatory Phase 3), both with a staggered two-cohort enrollment structure (Cohort 1 exiting at Day 43, Cohort 2 continuing to a Day 57 follow-up visit added by a protocol amendment) — first-in-class trial design for Demodex blepharitis, a previously untreated indication with no approved active comparator, so vehicle-control was used rather than an active comparator

sponsor: Astellas Pharma Inc. (via its 2023 acquisition of IVERIC bio, Inc., the original applicant; IVERIC bio, Inc. is named as Applicant throughout the FDA Statistical Review)
pivotal_trial: GATHER1 (Study OPH2003, NCT02686658, Phase 2/3) and GATHER2 (Study ISEE2008, NCT04435366, Phase 3) — two multicenter, double-masked, randomized, sham-controlled trials of intravitreal Zimura (avacincaptad pegol, a complement C5 inhibitor)
design_text: two randomized, double-masked, sham-controlled trials; GATHER1 enrolled in two sequential parts with different randomization ratios and dose arms (Part 1: 1:1:1 to Zimura 1mg/2mg/sham; Part 2: 1:2:2 to Zimura 2mg+sham/Zimura 4mg/sham+sham, with "Part" carried as a covariate in the primary MMRM rather than the two parts being naively pooled) — a within-trial multi-part enrollment structure with differing per-part randomization ratios and dose arms, distinct from Keyword_Taxonomy.md's existing "Post-hoc recombination of differently-enrolled cohorts" (which describes a data-driven pooling decision made *after* an interim look) since here the two-part structure and its covariate-adjustment were prespecified from the outset; GATHER2 additionally re-randomized Month-12 Zimura 2mg responders 1:1 to monthly vs. every-other-month dosing for Months 13-23, a design element not relevant to the Month-12 primary endpoint; randomization in both trials stratified by baseline visual acuity (<50 vs. ≥50 letters), baseline GA size (<4 vs. ≥4 disc areas), and FAF pattern at the GA junctional zone (none/focal vs. banded/diffuse)

sponsor: Alcon Laboratories, Inc. (trials were run under original developer Aerie Pharmaceuticals, Inc., subsequently acquired by Alcon)
pivotal_trial: COMET-2 (Study AR-15512-CS301, NCT05285644, N=465) and COMET-3 (NCT05360966, N=467) — Phase 3, randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trials of acoltremon (a TRPM8 cold-thermoreceptor agonist) ophthalmic solution
design_text: randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group design, two replicate confirmatory Phase 3 trials, with a vehicle run-in/requalification period preceding randomization

pivotal_trial: CLARITY-1 (Study 22-150-0015, NCT05656027, N=469) and CLARITY-2 (NCT05728944, N=229) — Phase 3, multicenter, double-masked, randomized, active-controlled (brimonidine) trials; each trial randomized to three arms: LNZ100 (aceclidine hydrochloride 1.75%, the approved VIZZ formulation, monotherapy), LNZ101 (aceclidine hydrochloride 1.75% + brimonidine 0.08% fixed combination, a separate investigational product not approved under this NDA), and brimonidine alone (active control)
design_text: randomized, double-masked (quadruple-masked including outcomes assessor), active (brimonidine)-controlled, three-arm parallel design; two confirmatory Phase 3 trials (CLARITY-1, CLARITY-2)

pivotal_trial: THRIVE (Study VRDN-001-101, NCT05176639, N=113) in active thyroid eye disease and THRIVE-2 (Study VRDN-001-301, NCT06021054, N=188) in chronic thyroid eye disease — two Phase 3, randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled trials of veligrotug (a full-antagonist IGF-1 receptor antibody), both 2:1 randomized to veligrotug 10 mg/kg IV or placebo, every 3 weeks for 5 infusions
design_text: two randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled (2:1) trials distinguished by disease chronicity — THRIVE enrolled active TED (onset ≤15 months, clinical activity score ≥3), THRIVE-2 enrolled chronic TED (onset >15 months, any activity score 0-7, including a substantial low-activity subgroup); dose (10 mg/kg) and regimen (5 infusions every 3 weeks) were set via extensive Type B/Type C FDA meetings using Phase 1/2 dose-ranging data (3, 10, and 20 mg/kg) showing 10 mg/kg achieved near-maximal response

pivotal_trial: NORSE TWO (Study ONS-5010-002, NCT03834753, N=228) — a randomized, multicenter, masked, active (ranibizumab)-controlled trial that met its primary endpoint — plus NORSE EIGHT (Study ONS-5010-008, NCT06190093, N=400), a Special-Protocol-Assessment-agreed randomized, masked, active-controlled non-inferiority confirmatory trial that **did not** meet its pre-specified non-inferiority margin
design_text: two independently conducted randomized, masked, active (ranibizumab)-controlled trials of different designs — NORSE TWO a superiority-framed 1-year comparison (unequal dosing frequency: monthly bevacizumab-vikg vs. front-loaded-then-quarterly ranibizumab) and NORSE EIGHT an SPA-agreed non-inferiority trial (equal 3-dose, 8-week regimen in both arms) intended as the second adequate-and-well-controlled study/confirmatory evidence; NORSE EIGHT failed its pre-specified NI margin, yet its results are disclosed in the approved label and the product was ultimately approved on NORSE TWO plus additional mechanistic/natural-history evidence — extends "Approval program with a substantial proportion of negative/failed pivotal trials" (Vortioxetine) to a two-trial program where the SPA-agreed *confirmatory* trial itself failed and is nonetheless labeled — flagged **("SPA-agreed confirmatory non-inferiority trial that failed its margin, disclosed in the label, with approval ultimately resting on the other trial plus additional evidence")**

sponsor: Forest Research Institute, Inc. (NDA originally filed by Nycomed GmbH/Altana Pharma AG under IND 57,883; ownership transferred to Forest Research Institute, Inc. on December 4, 2009, before the resubmission that led to approval)
pivotal_trial: Study M2-124 ("AURA," NCT00297102) and Study M2-125 ("HERMES," NCT00297115) — two identically designed, 52-week, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in patients with severe-to-very-severe COPD, chronic bronchitis, and a history of exacerbations; supportive trials M2-111 and M2-112 (similar design but without a bronchitis/exacerbation-history entry requirement) and 24-week trials M2-127/M2-128 (add-on to salmeterol/tiotropium) were also reviewed
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm (M2-124/M2-125); co-primary endpoints tested in a fixed-sequence hierarchy; the enrollment criteria for M2-124/M2-125 (severe/very-severe COPD, chronic bronchitis, exacerbation history) were deliberately narrowed relative to two earlier same-program trials (M2-111/M2-112, all-comers with severe/very-severe COPD but no bronchitis/exacerbation-history requirement) based on a post-hoc subgroup finding from those earlier trials that patients with bronchitis/exacerbation history showed the largest exacerbation-rate benefit — a design pattern of "using a post-hoc subgroup finding from an earlier same-program trial pair to define the enrichment criteria of the next, differently-enrolled pivotal trial pair" not currently in the taxonomy

pivotal_trial: Study B2336 ("INVOLVE," NCT00567996), Study B2346 (NCT00624286), Study B2354 (NCT01072448), and Study B2355 (NCT01068600) — randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (B2336 also active-controlled with salmeterol), parallel-arm Phase 3 trials in COPD, conducted as part of a resubmission following a 2009 Complete Response Letter; dose-selection trials B2223 and B2357 (asthma) and B2356 (COPD) were conducted specifically to address the CRL's dosing deficiencies
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (add-on active-controlled with salmeterol in B2336), parallel-arm; original NDA (150/300 mcg once daily) received a Complete Response Letter on October 16, 2009 citing excess cardiovascular/cerebrovascular serious adverse events versus placebo/formoterol and possible asthma-related deaths versus salmeterol, plus inadequate dose/frequency justification; FDA's End-of-Review meeting explicitly directed the sponsor to re-characterize dose and dosing frequency first in asthma patients (considered more sensitive to LABA-related adverse effects) before further COPD development — a "regulator-mandated re-sequencing of dose-finding through a more adverse-effect-sensitive population before the intended target population, following a safety-driven Complete Response Letter" not currently in the taxonomy

pivotal_trial: Study KL4-IRDS-06 — a multinational (Europe and Latin America), multicenter (50 sites), randomized, masked, active-controlled (Exosurf and Survanta), prophylaxis superiority trial in premature neonates; no NCT identified (trial conducted circa 1998-2000, predating ClinicalTrials.gov); supportive Study KL4-IRDS-02 (non-inferiority vs. Curosurf) was rejected by FDA as a basis for efficacy and was reviewed for safety only
design_text: randomized, masked, active-controlled (three-arm: lucinactant/Surfaxin, colfosceril palmitate/Exosurf, beractant/Survanta), prophylaxis-of-RDS superiority trial with a "short-term" efficacy/safety phase (36 weeks post-conceptual age) and a "long-term" outcomes/safety phase (6 and 12 months corrected age); the approval itself is an unusual regulatory pattern — efficacy on the single pivotal trial (KL4-IRDS-06) was accepted as early as the original 2004-2006 review cycles, but approval was withheld for three further review cycles (2006-2012) entirely on Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) grounds (drug-substance impurities, release/stability specifications, and — the final outstanding issue — validation of the fetal-rabbit bioassay used to confirm biological activity of drug product lots), a "multi-cycle approval delay driven entirely by unresolved CMC/bioassay-validation deficiencies after efficacy was already accepted" pattern not currently in the taxonomy; FDA separately rejected the sponsor's proposed non-inferiority design for the supportive trial KL4-IRDS-02 (vs. Curosurf) as statistically unsupportable, citing insufficient historical data to estimate the active-comparator effect and inappropriate margin justification, and required it be treated as safety-only evidence

pivotal_trial: ATTAIN (Study M/34273/34, NCT01001494), ACCORD COPD I (Study LAS-MD-33, NCT00891462), and ACCORD COPD II (Study LAS-MD-38, NCT01045161) — randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials of aclidinium bromide 200 mcg and 400 mcg twice daily
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm (three trials: ATTAIN 24 weeks, ex-US; ACCORD COPD I and II 12 weeks each, North America); two Phase 2 crossover dose-ranging trials (M23, M29) conducted in Germany/Belgium preceded the Phase 3 program

pivotal_trial: Studies HZC112206 (NCT01053988) and HZC112207 (NCT01054885), two 24-week lung-function trials; Studies HZC102871 (NCT01009463) and HZC102970 (NCT01017952), two 12-month exacerbation-rate trials
design_text: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trials; prespecified factorial combination-product design in which the fixed-dose combination, each individual monotherapy component, and placebo were all randomized from trial inception, specifically to satisfy 21 CFR 300.50's requirement to demonstrate each component's contribution (**"Prespecified factorial combination-product design (combination + each monotherapy component + placebo randomized from inception, per 21 CFR 300.50)"**; seen in Studies 2206/2207 here and in the companion umeclidinium/vilanterol program below)

pivotal_trial: Study 113373 (NCT01313650, the pivotal-dose placebo-controlled trial at the approved 62.5/25 mcg dose); supportive Studies 113361 (NCT01313637), 113360 (NCT01316900), and 113374 (NCT01316913)
design_text: randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, 24-week trials; prespecified factorial combination-product design (combination + each monotherapy component + placebo randomized from inception, per 21 CFR 300.50; also seen in the Breo Ellipta program above) for Studies 361/373; active (tiotropium)-controlled factorial design for Studies 360/374; supportive incomplete-block randomized crossover exercise-endurance trials (Studies 417/NCT01328444 and 418/NCT01323660) with co-primary endpoints
